title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄉試錄序
聖天子嗣承大統紀元萬曆之年
浙江例當貢士巡按監察御
史蕭廩新承
任使實維監臨乃按依
令章申飭糾虔罔或不毖届期進
前御史劉堯卿所預徵校官
===
列之簾內而以大器與教授
萬濟川職考試教授伍希德
張澍顧登龍教諭張文獻黃
鏊秦延緒翟毓奇職同考試
又遴郡邑有司列之簾外而
以左布政使謝鵬舉右參政
蒙詔職提調按察使劉繼文
punctuated:
浙江鄉試錄序
聖天子嗣承大統、紀元萬曆之年，浙江例當貢士。巡按監察御史蕭廩新承任使，實維監臨。乃按依令章，申飭糾虔，罔或不毖。届期，進前御史劉堯卿所預徵校官，列之簾內，而以大器與教授萬濟川職考試，教授伍希德、張澍、顧登龍，教諭張文獻、黃鏊、秦延緒、翟毓奇職同考試；又遴郡邑有司，列之簾外，而以左布政使謝鵬舉、右參政蒙詔職提調，按察使劉繼文
translation_en:
Preface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

In the year when His Sacred Majesty the Son of Heaven succeeded to the Great Lineage and inaugurated the Wanli reign era (1573), Zhejiang was due by statute to present tribute scholars through the provincial examination. Regional Investigating Censor Xiao Lin 蕭廩, having newly received his commission, served as the Supervising Official. Accordingly, in compliance with the statutory regulations, he issued strict injunctions and enforced reverent discipline, leaving nothing unattended to with the utmost caution. When the appointed time arrived, he admitted the school officials who had been summoned in advance by the former Censor Liu Yaoqing 劉堯卿, placing them inside the curtain: he assigned me, [Yang] Daqi 大器, together with Prefectural Confucian School Instructor Wan Jichuan 萬濟川, to serve as Examiners; and Prefectural Confucian School Instructors Wu Xide 伍希德, Zhang Shu 張澍, and Gu Denglong 顧登龍, along with County Confucian School Instructors Zhang Wenxian 張文獻, Huang Ao 黃鏊, Qin Yanxu 秦延緒, and Zhai Yuqi 翟毓奇, to serve as Associate Examiners. He also selected prefectural and county civil officials and placed them outside the curtain, assigning Left Provincial Administration Commissioner Xie Pengju 謝鵬舉 and Right Administration Vice Commissioner Meng Zhao 蒙詔 to serve as Proctors, and Surveillance Commissioner Liu Jiwen 劉繼文…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
吾無懼已因屬大器書之簡
端以爲諸士厚望焉是役也
提督軍務右副都御史方弘
靜節鉞保釐士樂寧宇而先
任巡撫鄔璉絳騶未遠聲猷
尚存巡鹽御史馬應夢輶車
諏度士知嚮方而清軍御史
===
田樂
簡命方新風猷先達若工部員外
郎錢楷南京戶部主事劉伯
縉時維榷稅禮科都給事中
宗弘暹中書舍人沈文時維
將指則皆樂觀盛典者也其
襄理於外若右布政使江一
punctuated:
吾無懼已！」因屬大器書之簡端，以爲諸士厚望焉。

是役也，提督軍務、右副都御史方弘靜節鉞保釐，士樂寧宇；而先任巡撫鄔璉絳騶未遠，聲猷尚存。巡鹽御史馬應夢輶車諏度，士知嚮方；而清軍御史田樂簡命方新，風猷先達。若工部員外郎錢楷、南京戶部主事劉伯縉時維榷稅，禮科都給事中宗弘暹、中書舍人沈文時維將指，則皆樂觀盛典者也。其襄理於外，若右布政使江一
translation_en:
…‘I have nothing to fear!’” Consequently, he charged me, Daqi, to write this at the head of the register, as an earnest expectation for the scholars.

In this undertaking, Superintendent of Military Affairs and Vice Censor-in-Chief of the Right Fang Hongjing 方弘靜, bearing the insignia of command, has protected and governed the region, so that scholars rejoice in a peaceful realm; while the former Grand Coordinator Wu Lian 鄔璉, whose crimson-clad outriders have not long departed, still leaves behind his reputation and influence. Salt-Control Censor Ma Yingmeng 馬應夢, touring in his light carriage to make inquiries and assessments, has guided the scholars to know the proper direction; while Military-Inspection Censor Tian Yue 田樂, whose imperial commission is newly conferred, has already made his moral influence and plans known in advance. As for Vice Director in the Ministry of Works Qian Kai 錢楷 and Secretary in the Nanjing Ministry of Revenue Liu Bojin 劉伯縉, who were at this time overseeing commercial taxes, as well as Chief Supervising Secretary of the Office of Scrutiny for Rites Zong Hongxian 宗弘暹 and Drafter in the Central Drafting Office Shen Wen 沈文, who were at this time carrying out imperial missions—all of them delighted in witnessing this grand ceremony. Among those assisting with administration in the outer precincts were figures such as Right Administration Commissioner Jiang Yi…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
麟左參政史朝宜左參議劉
宗岱副使趙宋郭天祿華汝
礪劉翺僉事戴延容沈奎王
嘉言防範於外若署都指揮
僉事謝詔潘清張澡而右參
議徐雲程僉事徐廷裸署都
指揮僉事魏堯相則以入
===
===
賀行按察使勞堪則以遷秩行
皆嘗與聞盛典者也例得竝
書用告成事
直隸淮安府儒學敎授吳大
器謹序
punctuated:
麟，左參政史朝宜，左參議劉宗岱，副使趙宋、郭天祿、華汝礪、劉翺，僉事戴延容、沈奎、王嘉言；防範於外，若署都指揮僉事謝詔、潘清、張澡；而右參議徐雲程、僉事徐廷裸、署都指揮僉事魏堯相則以入賀行，按察使勞堪則以遷秩行，皆嘗與聞盛典者也。例得竝書，用告成事。

直隸淮安府儒學敎授吳大器謹序。
translation_en:
… [Jiang Yi]lin 江一麟, Left Administration Vice Commissioner Shi Chaoyi 史朝宜, Left Assistant Administration Commissioner Liu Zongdai 劉宗岱, Surveillance Vice Commissioners Zhao Song 趙宋, Guo Tianlu 郭天祿, Hua Ruli 華汝礪, and Liu Ao 劉翺, and Assistant Surveillance Commissioners Dai Yanrong 戴延容, Shen Kui 沈奎, and Wang Jiayan 王嘉言; those who maintained security on the outside, such as Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioners Xie Zhao 謝詔, Pan Qing 潘清, and Zhang Zao 張澡; while Right Assistant Administration Commissioner Xu Yuncheng 徐雲程, Assistant Surveillance Commissioner Xu Tingluo 徐廷裸 [?], and Acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Wei Yaoxiang 魏堯相, who departed to offer congratulations at court, and Surveillance Commissioner Lao Kan 勞堪, who departed upon promotion in rank—all of them had taken part in and been apprised of this grand ceremony. In accordance with precedent, their names may all be recorded together, so as to announce the completion of the undertaking.

Respectfully prefaced by Wu Daqi 吳大器, Instructor of the Confucian School of Huai'an Prefecture 淮安府 in the Metropolitan Area (Zhili 直隸).

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:

===

punctuated:

巡按浙江監察御史蕭廩〔可發，江西萬安縣人，乙丑進士。〕

浙江等處提刑按察司副使沈人种〔時雍，直隸嘉定縣人，己未進士。〕

translation_en:
Zhejiang Provincial Examination of the First Year of the Wanli Reign (1573)

Supervising Official (監臨官):
Xiao Lin 蕭廩, Investigating Censor and Regional Inspector of Zhejiang [courtesy name Kefa 可發, a native of Wan'an County, Jiangxi, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the yichou year (1565)].

Xie Pengju 謝鵬舉, Left Administration Commissioner of the Zhejiang Provincial Administration Commission [courtesy name Zhongnan 仲南, a native of Puqi County, Huguang, and a metropolitan graduate (jinshi) of the guichou year (1553)].

Wu Xide 伍希德, Instructor of the Confucian School of Qingzhou Prefecture, Shandong [courtesy name Rumao 汝懋, a native of Nanchang County, Jiangxi, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the yimao year (1555)].

Zhang Wenxian 張文獻, Instructor of the Confucian School of Wuhe County, Fengyang Prefecture, Zhili [courtesy name Yongzheng 用徵, a native of Ouning County, Fujian, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiyou year (1549)].
Huang Ao 黃鼇, Instructor of the Confucian School of Tong'an County, Quanzhou Prefecture, Fujian [courtesy name Yongli 用礪, a native of Panyu County, Guangdong, and a tribute scholar (gongshi) of the jiazi year (1564)].

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
林放問禮之本子曰大哉問
凡爲天下國家有九經曰脩身也尊賢也
親親也敬大臣也體羣臣也子庶民也
來百工也柔遠人也懷諸侯也脩身則
道立尊賢則不惑親親則諸父昆弟不
怨敬大臣則不眩體羣臣則士之報禮
重子庶民則百姓勸來百工則財用足
===
柔遠人則四方歸之懷諸侯則天下畏
之
智譬則巧也聖譬則力也
易
坤道其順乎承天而時行
初九利用爲大作元吉无咎
祐者助也
昔者聖人之作易也幽賛於神明而生蓍
參天兩地而倚數觀變於陰陽而立卦
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

林放問禮之本。子曰：「大哉問！」

凡爲天下國家有九經，曰：脩身也，尊賢也，親親也，敬大臣也，體羣臣也，子庶民也，來百工也，柔遠人也，懷諸侯也。脩身則道立，尊賢則不惑，親親則諸父昆弟不怨，敬大臣則不眩，體羣臣則士之報禮重，子庶民則百姓勸，來百工則財用足，柔遠人則四方歸之，懷諸侯則天下畏之。

智，譬則巧也；聖，譬則力也。

易

坤道其順乎，承天而時行。

初九，利用爲大作，元吉，无咎。

祐者，助也。

昔者聖人之作《易》也，幽賛於神明而生蓍，參天兩地而倚數，觀變於陰陽而立卦，
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

Lin Fang asked about the fundamental principle of ritual propriety. The Master said, "A great question indeed!"

In all governance of the world, the state, and the ruling family, there are nine standard rules: cultivating one's own person, honoring the worthy, cherishing one's relatives, respecting the great ministers, empathetically identifying with the whole body of officers, treating the common people as one's children, attracting the hundred artisans, showing tenderness to men from afar, and cherishing the feudal lords. By cultivating one's own person, the Way is established; by honoring the worthy, one is free from perplexity; by cherishing one's relatives, there is no resentment among one's uncles and brothers; by respecting the great ministers, one does not go astray in affairs; by empathetically identifying with the whole body of officers, gentlemen will repay courtesy heavily; by treating the common people as one's children, the hundred surnames are encouraged; by attracting the hundred artisans, wealth and resources are made sufficient; by showing tenderness to men from afar, people from all four quarters will turn in allegiance; by cherishing the feudal lords, the whole world will hold one in awe.

Wisdom may be compared to skill, and sageliness may be compared to strength.

Classic of Changes (Yi)

How compliant is the Way of Kun! It receives from Heaven and acts in accordance with the seasons.

Nine at the beginning: It is advantageous to undertake great works. Supreme good fortune, without blame.

"To bless" means "to assist."

In ancient times, when the sages made the Classic of Changes, they mysteriously assisted the spiritual and luminous forces and thus produced the yarrow stalks; they assigned three to Heaven and two to Earth and from these derived the numbers; they observed the changes in yin and yang and thus established the hexagrams; …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
發揮於剛柔而生爻和順於道德而理
於義窮理盡性以至於命
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝曰后克艱厥后
臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏德
若金用汝作礪
惟公德明光于上下勤施于四方
拜手稽首告嗣天子王矣用咸戒于王曰
王左右常伯常任準人綴衣虎賁
===
詩
不稼不穡胡取禾三百廛兮不狩不獵胡
瞻爾庭有縣貆兮
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于野魚潜在淵或在于
渚樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維蘀他山
之石可以爲錯鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天
魚在于渚或潜在淵樂彼之園爰有樹
檀其下維穀他山之石可以攻玉
受天之祜四方來賀於萬斯年不遐有佐
punctuated:
發揮於剛柔而生爻，和順於道德而理於義，窮理盡性以至於命。

書
文命敷于四海，祗承于帝。曰：「后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。」
若金，用汝作礪。
惟公德明光于上下，勤施于四方。
拜手稽首，告嗣天子王矣。用咸戒于王，曰：「王左右常伯、常任、準人、綴衣、虎賁。」

詩
不稼不穡，胡取禾三百廛兮？不狩不獵，胡瞻爾庭有縣貆兮？
鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于野。魚潜在淵，或在于渚。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維蘀。他山之石，可以爲錯。鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。魚在于渚，或潜在淵。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維穀。他山之石，可以攻玉。
受天之祜，四方來賀。於萬斯年，不遐有佐。
translation_en:
…brought forth movements in the firm and the yielding and thus generated the lines; harmonized with the Way and its Virtue and ordered them according to righteousness; and exhausted the principles of things and fulfilled nature in order to arrive at Destiny.”

Book of Documents (Shu):
1. “His civilizing influence and ordinances were spread throughout the four seas, and he reverently received from the Supreme Ancestor [Shun], saying: ‘If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of his sovereignty, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of his ministry, government will be well ordered, and the black-haired people will swiftly advance in virtue.’”
2. “Suppose me to be steel: I will use you as a whetstone.”
3. “It is the Duke’s virtue that shines brightly above and below, and is diligently extended to the four quarters.”
4. “Bowing their hands to their heads and their heads to the ground, they announced to the succeeding Son of Heaven that he was now King. Thereupon they all admonished the King, saying: ‘In attendance on the King at his left and right are the Regular Elders (changbo), the Regular Officeholders (changren), the Keepers of the Law (zhunren), the Wardrobers (zhuiyi), and the Tiger Warriors (huben).’”

Book of Odes (Shi):
1. “You do not sow and you do not reap—how do you take in grain from three hundred farmsteads? You do not hunt in winter and you do not chase—how do we see badgers hanging in your courtyard?”
2. “The crane cries in the九皋 (nine marshes), and its voice is heard in the wilds. The fish lies hidden in the deep, or rests by the islet. Pleasant is that garden, where there are sandalwood trees planted, and beneath them are fallen leaves. The stones of other hills may be used as grindstones. The crane cries in the nine marshes, and its voice is heard in heaven. The fish rests by the islet, or lies hidden in the deep. Pleasant is that garden, where there are sandalwood trees planted, and beneath them is the paper-mulberry. The stones of other hills may be used to polish jade.”
3. “He receives the blessing of Heaven, and the four quarters come to offer congratulations. For ten thousand years, will there not be helpers from afar?”

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
昊天有成命二后受之成王不敢康夙夜
基命宥密
春秋
秋七月〔隱公六年〕六月雨〔僖公三年〕
春王正月城楚丘〔僖公二年〕五月癸丑公
會晉侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衞子莒子
盟于踐土〔僖公二十有八年〕
鄭公孫舍之帥師侵宋公會晉侯宋公
衞侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛
===
伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭秋七月巳未同
盟于亳城北公至自伐鄭楚子鄭
伯伐宋公會晉侯宋公衞侯曹伯齊
世子光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔俱襄公十有一年〕
齊人歸讙及闡〔哀公八年〕
禮記
東方曰寄南方曰象西方曰狄鞮北方曰
譯
punctuated:
昊天有成命，二后受之；成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。

《春秋》
秋七月〔隱公六年〕；六月雨〔僖公三年〕。
春王正月，城楚丘〔僖公二年〕；五月癸丑，公會晉侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衞子、莒子盟于踐土〔僖公二十有八年〕。
鄭公孫舍之帥師侵宋。公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。秋七月巳未，同盟于亳城北。公至自伐鄭。楚子、鄭伯伐宋。公會晉侯、宋公、衞侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭，會于蕭魚〔俱襄公十有一年〕。
齊人歸讙及闡〔哀公八年〕。

《禮記》
東方曰寄，南方曰象，西方曰狄鞮，北方曰譯。
translation_en:
"Heaven Most High has its settled mandate, which the two sovereigns received. King Cheng did not dare to rest in ease; day and night he laid deep the foundations of the mandate in quietude and stillness."

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu):
"In autumn, in the seventh month" [sixth year of Duke Yin]; "In the sixth month, it rained" [third year of Duke Xi].
"In spring, in the King's first month, they walled Chuqiu" [second year of Duke Xi]; "In the fifth month, on the guichou day, the Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu" [twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi].
"Gongsun Shezhi of Zheng led a force and made an incursion into Song. The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu to attack Zheng. In autumn, in the seventh month, on the jiwei day, they made a joint covenant north of the capital of Bo. The Duke arrived from the campaign against Zheng. The Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng attacked Song. The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu to attack Zheng, and they met at Xiaoyu" [all in the eleventh year of Duke Xiang].
"The people of Qi restored Huan and Chan" [eighth year of Duke Ai].

Record of Rites (Liji):
"In the east they are called transmitters (ji), in the south they are called representers (xiang), in the west they are called Didi interpreters, and in the north they are called translators (yi)."

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
故聖人作則必以天地爲本以陰陽爲端
以四時爲柄以日星爲紀月以爲量鬼
神以爲徒五行以爲質禮義以爲器人
情以爲田四靈以爲畜
廉直勁正莊誠之音作而民肅敬寬裕肉
好順成和動之音作而民慈愛
福者備也
第貳塲
論
===
宗社生靈長乆之計
詔誥表〔內科一道〕
擬漢除肉刑詔〔文帝元年〕
擬唐以虞世南等兼弘文館學士誥〔武德九年〕
擬宋行崇天萬年曆羣臣賀表〔慶曆元年〕
判語〔五條〕
私役部民夫匠
邊境申索軍需
punctuated:
故聖人作則，必以天地爲本，以陰陽爲端，以四時爲柄，以日星爲紀，月以爲量，鬼神以爲徒，五行以爲質，禮義以爲器，人情以爲田，四靈以爲畜。
廉直、勁正、莊誠之音作，而民肅敬；寬裕、肉好、順成、和動之音作，而民慈愛。
福者，備也。

第貳塲
論
宗社生靈長乆之計。
詔、誥、表〔內科一道〕
擬漢除肉刑詔〔文帝元年〕。
擬唐以虞世南等兼弘文館學士誥〔武德九年〕。
擬宋行《崇天萬年曆》羣臣賀表〔慶曆元年〕。
判語〔五條〕
私役部民夫匠。
邊境申索軍需。
translation_en:
"Therefore, when the sage establishes rules, he must take heaven and earth as the foundation, yin and yang as the starting points, the four seasons as the handle, the sun and stars as the markers of order, the moon as the measure, ghosts and spirits as the attendants, the five phases as the substance, ritual and righteousness as the instruments, human feelings as the field to be cultivated, and the four numinous creatures as the domestic animals."

"When tones that are pure and direct, strong and upright, grave and sincere arise, the people become reverent and respectful; when tones that are broad and generous, full and melodious, harmonious and accomplished, gentle and moving arise, the people become kind and loving."

"Good fortune means completeness."

Second Session

Discourse:
"Plans for the enduring longevity of the ancestral altars and the living people."

Edict, Mandate, and Memorial (Candidates are examined on one of these):
Imitation of the Han Dynasty Edict Abolishing Corporal Punishment (1st year of Emperor Wen [179 BCE]).
Imitation of the Tang Dynasty Mandate Appointing Yu Shinan 虞世南 and Others to Serve Concurrently as Academician of the Institute for the Advancement of Literature (9th year of the Wude reign [626]).
Imitation of the Congratulatory Memorial from thesembled Officials on the Song Dynasty's Promulgation of the Chongtian Wannian Calendar (1st year of the Qingli reign [1041]).

Legal Judgments (Five items):
Illegally putting subjects, laborers, and artisans under one's jurisdiction to private labor service.
Requesting and demanding military supplies on the frontier.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
公事應行稽程
詐教誘人犯法
織造違禁段疋
第叄場
策五道
問聖帝明王稽古正學爲之臣者恒陳說
媺惡以明昭法戒若書益稷無逸諸篇
具可見已然亦唯其君之聖明然後嘉
納而體行之用臻盛治此論世者所以
===
不徒歎其臣而尤仰其君之哲焉惟我
皇上體聖神之資紹雍煕之統時御
經筵日親儒彦上嘉堯舜下陋唐宋稽古正
學亹亹然日就月將矣輔弼大臣啓沃
有見忠愛無窮乃令講官博采古今理
亂興衰得失凡百十七事繪圖系說草
疏而進之用佐
燕間之觀進之日
上爲起受褒答頃間
punctuated:
公事應行稽程。
詐教誘人犯法。
織造違禁段疋。

第叄場
策五道

問：聖帝明王，稽古正學，爲之臣者，恒陳說媺惡，以明昭法戒。若《書》〈益稷〉、〈無逸〉諸篇，具可見已。然亦唯其君之聖明，然後嘉納而體行之，用臻盛治。此論世者所以不徒歎其臣，而尤仰其君之哲焉。惟我皇上，體聖神之資，紹雍煕之統，時御經筵，日親儒彦，上嘉堯、舜，下陋唐、宋，稽古正學，亹亹然日就月將矣。輔弼大臣，啓沃有見，忠愛無窮，乃令講官博采古今理亂興衰得失，凡百十七事，繪圖系說，草疏而進之，用佐燕間之觀。進之日，上爲起受，褒答。頃間，
translation_en:
Delaying Official Business That Should Be Carried Out.
Deceitfully Instructing or Inducing Others to Violate the Law.
Weaving Prohibited Satin and Piece Goods.

Third Session
Five Policy Questions

Question: When sage emperors and enlightened kings examine antiquity to rectify their learning, those who serve as their ministers constantly set forth the good and the bad so as to clearly illustrate models to emulate and warnings to heed. This can all be seen in such chapters of the Book of Documents (Shu) as "Yi and Ji" (Yiji) and "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi). Yet it is only when the ruler himself is sage and enlightened that he approvingly accepts and personally practices them, thereby achieving flourishing governance. This is why those who discuss the ages do not merely admire the ministers, but especially look up to the wisdom of their rulers.

Now His Majesty the Emperor embodies a sage and divine nature and continues a lineage of harmonious peace. He regularly attends the Classics Colloquium (jingyan) and daily draws close to Confucian worthies; looking upward, he admires Yao and Shun, and looking downward, he disdains the Tang and Song. Examining antiquity to rectify his learning, he tirelessly advances day by day and month by month. The grand ministers who assist him, having insight in enlightening his mind and boundless loyalty and affection, thereupon ordered the Lecturers (jiangguan) to broadly gather instances of order and disorder, rise and decline, and success and failure from ancient and modern times—one hundred and seventeen items in all—to paint illustrations, attach explanations, draft a memorial, and present them to assist His Majesty's viewing during moments of leisure. On the day they were presented, the Emperor rose to receive them and replied with praise. Recently, …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
指顧清問德意益亹亹焉且
宣付史館以昭交脩之義視虞周君臣先後
眞同一軌也猗歟休哉今
宣付之書傳布中外人知莊誦其爲諸士之
所莊誦無疑也不知其善可爲法與惡
可爲戒者亦能悉指而言之歟其取數
命意與宏旨微文亦能詳舉而繹之歟
圖說所載治忽畢陳政體咸備矣不知
廣引博喻之中當以何者尤爲切近要
領之實歟觀省旣具法戒斯存輔養誠
篤矣不知日陳時觀之外尚有何道可
爲緝熙基命之助歟昔我
世皇因儒臣進講旣
註心箴四箴又
特著敬一箴以昭示心學萬世言心學者必歸
焉
皇上春秋日盛
問學日新行且統一聖眞光紹
punctuated: 指顧清問，德意益亹亹焉。且宣付史館，以昭交脩之義，視虞、周君臣，先後眞同一軌也。猗歟休哉！今宣付之書，傳布中外，人知莊誦，其爲諸士之所莊誦無疑也。不知其善可爲法與惡可爲戒者，亦能悉指而言之歟？其取數命意，與宏旨微文，亦能詳舉而繹之歟？圖說所載，治忽畢陳，政體咸備矣。不知廣引博喻之中，當以何者尤爲切近要領之實歟？觀省旣具，法戒斯存，輔養誠篤矣。不知日陳時觀之外，尚有何道可爲緝熙基命之助歟？昔我世皇因儒臣進講，旣註《心箴》、《四箴》，又特著《敬一箴》，以昭示心學，萬世言心學者必歸焉。皇上春秋日盛，問學日新，行且統一聖眞，光紹
translation_en: …pointing to the illustrations and asking clear questions, His virtuous intent all the more tireless. Moreover, He ordered it delivered to the Historiography Institute to manifest the principle of mutual cultivation between ruler and minister; compared to the rulers and ministers of Yu and Zhou, across the ages they truly follow the same track. How admirable and splendid! Now the book delivered to the Institute has been circulated throughout the court and the provinces, and everyone knows to recite it reverently; there is no doubt that you scholars have also reverently recited it. Yet I wonder: regarding the good deeds in it that can serve as models and the evil deeds that can serve as warnings, are you able to point them all out and speak of them? Regarding the rationale behind the number of items selected, as well as its grand purport and subtle wording, are you also able to enumerate them in detail and explicate them? What is recorded in the illustrations and explanations sets forth governance and negligence in their entirety, and encompasses the whole body of administration. Yet I wonder: amid its wide citations and broad metaphors, what should be taken as the most urgent, pertinent, and essential substance? With the materials for viewing and reflection now complete, models and warnings are thereby preserved, and the aid to imperial cultivation is truly earnest. Yet I wonder: beyond daily presentation and timely perusal, what further way is there to assist in luminous sagely learning and the establishment of the Heavenly Mandate? Formerly, because of the lectures presented by Confucian ministers, our Emperor Shizong not only annotated the Admonition on the Mind (Xinzhen) and the Four Admonitions (Sizhen), but also specially composed the Admonition on Reverent Unity (Jingyi zhen) to clearly reveal the learning of the mind, so that for ten thousand generations those who speak of the learning of the mind must turn to it as their standard. As His Majesty grows in years and vigor day by day, and His inquiry and learning are daily renewed, He is about to unify the true essence of the sages and gloriously continue…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
祖德爾草茅之臣亦有能仰窺而頌言之者歟
請詳著于篇執事者將聞于
上也
問隆古大臣明保弼亮功在國家載之訓
誥中聲施百代而未有以社稷臣名之
者乃古今人君亦未有於其臣而預以
社稷臣許之者蓋惟孟子列品人臣始
言之而漢武帝於汲長孺則特許之亦
何見歟竊嘗上下古今名臣有定太子
===
===
而建羽翼之策者有鋤外戚而成左袒
之謀者有功蓋天下而以其身係安危
三十年者有望達四夷而以其身係輕
重二十年者有決策親征一渡河而折
强虜者有正色立朝一設計而除大姦
者之數公者定變決疑委身殫赤視孟
子所稱若少過之即使長孺爲之無以
踰此而論者顧有許有不許亦何說歟
豈社稷之功別有所庄歟抑處艱大之
punctuated:
祖德，爾草茅之臣，亦有能仰窺而頌言之者歟？請詳著于篇，執事者將聞于上也。

問：隆古大臣，明保弼亮，功在國家，載之訓誥中，聲施百代，而未有以「社稷臣」名之者。乃古今人君，亦未有於其臣而預以「社稷臣」許之者。蓋惟孟子列品人臣始言之，而漢武帝於汲長孺則特許之，亦何見歟？竊嘗上下古今，名臣有定太子而建羽翼之策者；有鋤外戚而成左袒之謀者；有功蓋天下而以其身係安危三十年者；有望達四夷而以其身係輕重二十年者；有決策親征，一渡河而折强虜者；有正色立朝，一設計而除大姦者。之數公者，定變決疑，委身殫赤，視孟子所稱若少過之，即使長孺爲之，無以踰此。而論者顧有許有不許，亦何說歟？豈社稷之功別有所庄歟？抑處艱大之
translation_en:
… the virtue of His imperial ancestors. Among you, subjects from the humble countryside, is there anyone able to gaze up in contemplation and speak in praise of this? Please set it forth in detail in your essays, for the officials in charge will report it to the Emperor.

Question: In high antiquity, the great ministers were enlightened protectors and loyal assistants whose merits lay with the state; recorded in the Instructions and Announcements, their renown has extended across a hundred generations, yet none of them was ever designated a "minister of the altars of soil and grain" (sheji chen). Moreover, among rulers ancient and modern, none had ever commended one of his own ministers in advance as a "minister of the altars of soil and grain." Indeed, it was only when Mencius (Mengzi 孟子) ranked the grades of ministers that the term was first spoken of, and Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi 漢武帝) specially accorded this recognition to Ji Changru 汲長孺 [Ji An 汲黯]—what was the insight behind this? I have privately surveyed ancient and modern times: among famous ministers, there was one who secured the Heir Apparent by devising the plan of bringing in "wings" of support [Zhang Liang 張良]; there was one who rooted out the consort clan by carrying through the stratagem of "baring the left arm" [Zhou Bo 周勃]; there was one whose merit covered the realm and upon whose own person the security or peril of the empire depended for thirty years [Guo Ziyi 郭子儀]; there was one whose reputation reached the four barbarian quarters and upon whose own person the weight of the empire depended for twenty years [Pei Du 裴度]; there was one who resolved upon the policy of an imperial campaign in person and broke the strong northern enemy as soon as the Yellow River was crossed [Kou Zhun 寇準]; and there was one who stood at court with stern countenance and eliminated a great traitor by a single plan [Han Qi 韓琦]. These several worthies settled crises and resolved doubts, devoting their lives and exhausting their utmost loyalty; compared to what Mencius described, they seem slightly to surpass it, and even had Changru himself been in their place, he could not have gone beyond this. Yet commentators have approved of some and disapproved of others—what is the explanation for this? Could it be that merit toward the altars of soil and grain resides [reading 在 for 庄?] in something else? Or is it that when situated in times of great difficulty and…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
時當呼吸之會其靜定堅凝非若戇者
之賁育弗奪固亦有不可歟夫社稷之
臣朝廷不得則不尊海宇不得則不奠
後世所願見當時所願誦者也故樂與
諸士爲之評隲焉
問學者尚友千古而其取法恒先一鄉浙
固文獻奧區也往哲吾無論已試以耳
目所及言之有以道學名者文懿文成
其著也而詳繹其造果有大小歟有以
===
節義名者寧海餘姚其烈也而夷考其
遭果有難易歟勳業如青田如龍泉偉
矣翊運之功孰爲盛歟詞章如浦江如
義烏富矣華國之文孰爲醇歟甞就諸
賢論之道學氣節勳業文章鮮有能兼
之者而昔人謂王文成爲具有之然則
舉國故之典而躋之從祀之列如諸臣
所請信爲當可歟又甞就人情較之勳
業詞章固所共貴節義出於不偶之遭
punctuated:
時，當呼吸之會，其靜定堅凝，非若戇者之賁育弗奪，固亦有不可歟？夫社稷之臣，朝廷不得則不尊，海宇不得則不奠，後世所願見、當時所願誦者也，故樂與諸士爲之評隲焉。
問：學者尚友千古，而其取法恒先一鄉。浙固文獻奧區也，往哲吾無論已，試以耳目所及言之：有以道學名者，文懿、文成其著也，而詳繹其造，果有大小歟？有以節義名者，寧海、餘姚其烈也，而夷考其遭，果有難易歟？勳業如青田、如龍泉，偉矣，翊運之功孰爲盛歟？詞章如浦江、如義烏，富矣，華國之文孰爲醇歟？甞就諸賢論之，道學、氣節、勳業、文章，鮮有能兼之者，而昔人謂王文成爲具有之，然則舉國故之典而躋之從祀之列，如諸臣所請，信爲當可歟？又甞就人情較之，勳業、詞章固所共貴，節義出於不偶之遭，
translation_en:
… times and facing moments as critical as a single breath, is it indeed impossible unless one's calm resolve and firm constancy are like that of the blunt man [Ji An 汲黯], whose will even the brave warriors Meng Ben 孟賁 and Xia Yu 夏育 could not shake? Now, a minister of the altars of soil and grain (sheji zhi chen 社稷之臣) is one without whom the court cannot be revered and the realm cannot be stabilized—one whom later generations wish to see and contemporaries wish to praise. Therefore, I gladly evaluate and rank them together with you gentlemen.

Question: When scholars make friends with the ancients across a thousand ages, they always look first to their own native region for models. Zhejiang is indeed a rich heartland of literature and worthy traditions. Setting aside the sages of distant antiquity, let us speak of those within the reach of our own eyes and ears [i.e., of our dynasty]. There are those renowned for the Learning of the Way (Daoxue 道學), among whom Wenyi 文懿 [Zhang Mao 章懋] and Wencheng 文成 [Wang Shouren 王守仁] are the most prominent; yet if we carefully examine their attainments, is there truly a difference between great and small? There are those renowned for integrity and righteousness, among whom the men of Ninghai 寧海 [Fang Xiaoru 方孝孺] and Yuyao 餘姚 [Sun燧 or Xie Qian / Huang Zunsu—specifically Sun Sui 孫燧] are the most heroic; yet if we fairly investigate the circumstances they encountered, was one truly easier or more difficult than the other? Meritorious achievements like those of the men of Qingtian 青田 [Liu Ji 劉基] and Longquan 龍泉 [Zhang Yi 章溢] were magnificent indeed—whose contribution to assisting the dynastic destiny was greater? Literary writings like those of the men of Pujiang 浦江 [Song Lian 宋濂] and Yiwu 義烏 [Wang Wei 王禕] were abundant indeed—whose state-adorning prose was purer? If we discuss these worthies, few have been able to combine the Learning of the Way, moral integrity, meritorious achievement, and literary writing; yet people in the past said that Wang Wencheng 王文成 [Wang Shouren] possessed them all. That being so, to invoke the statutory rites of the dynasty and elevate him to the ranks of those enshrined as correlates in the Confucian Temple, as various officials have petitioned—is this truly appropriate and permissible? Moreover, if we compare them in light of ordinary human sentiment, meritorious achievements and literary writings are of course universally prized, while integrity and righteousness arise from extraordinary encounters…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
而道學則隱若無補之空言也乃文成
自言願盡捐三者而獨從事道學以毋
愧完人然則致力心性而遺棄事物如
昔人所疑得無近似歟諸生景行有年
其爲論必有定矣願極言之因以明已
志焉毋曰方人則不暇
問古今譚吏治者不越寬猛二端其說蓋
出於左氏左氏者記孔子之言也儒者
亟稱之爲不易之說而考之論語似又
===
不類豈亦各有攸當乎抑語之所謂寬
所謂不猛者其義微其用廣固已該括
而言之乎言之不類姑不論即以左語
論之夫謂一寬一猛則平中之治不有
出於寬猛之外者乎其謂寬猛之相濟
也則慢殘之弊不又有乘於寬猛之中
者乎安在其爲不易也古今吏治推高
漢人韓延壽守潁川專崇禮敎黃覇承
之以寬和而潁川治趙廣漢尹京兆專
punctuated:
而道學則隱若無補之空言也；乃文成自言，願盡捐三者而獨從事道學，以毋愧完人。然則致力心性而遺棄事物，如昔人所疑，得無近似歟？諸生景行有年，其爲論必有定矣，願極言之，因以明已志焉，毋曰「方人則不暇」。

問：古今譚吏治者，不越寬、猛二端。其說蓋出於《左氏》，《左氏》者，記孔子之言也。儒者亟稱之爲不易之說，而考之《論語》，似又不類，豈亦各有攸當乎？抑《語》之所謂「寬」、所謂「不猛」者，其義微、其用廣，固已該括而言之乎？言之不類姑不論，即以左語論之：夫謂一寬一猛，則平中之治，不有出於寬猛之外者乎？其謂寬猛之相濟也，則慢殘之弊，不又有乘於寬猛之中者乎？安在其爲不易也！古今吏治推高漢人：韓延壽守潁川，專崇禮敎，黃覇承之以寬和，而潁川治；趙廣漢尹京兆，專…
translation_en:
…while Learning of the Way (daoxue) seems obscure, like empty words of no practical benefit. Yet Wencheng [Wang Yangming 王陽明] himself stated that he wished to cast aside all three of those other pursuits and devote himself solely to the Learning of the Way, so as not to fall short of being a complete person. If so, does this not come close to what people in the past suspected—namely, devoting one's efforts to the mind and human nature while abandoning practical affairs? You students have admired virtuous conduct for years, and your views on this must be settled. I hope you will speak of it exhaustively, and thereby make clear your own aspirations; do not say, "As for comparing people, I have no leisure for that."

Question: Those who discuss administrative governance, past and present, do not go beyond the two extremes of leniency and severity. This theory comes from the Zuo Commentary (Zuoshi), where Zuo recorded the words of Confucius. Confucians frequently praise it as an immutable doctrine, yet when we examine it against the Analects (Lunyu), it seems dissimilar. Could it be that each is appropriate to its own context? Or is it that what the Analects calls "leniency" and "not being severe" has a subtle meaning and broad application that already encompasses the whole matter? Setting aside for the moment the dissimilarity between the statements, let us discuss it simply in terms of the words in the Zuo Commentary: When it speaks of alternating between leniency and severity, is there not a balanced and moderate governance that transcends leniency and severity altogether? And when it speaks of leniency and severity complementing each other, do not the abuses of negligence and cruelty also take advantage of the very practice of leniency and severity? Wherein, then, lies its immutability? In administrative governance past and present, the men of the Han dynasty are held in the highest esteem. When Han Yanshou 韓延壽 was Grand Administrator of Yingchuan, he exclusively venerated ritual and moral instruction; Huang Ba 黃霸 succeeded him with leniency and harmony, and Yingchuan was well governed. When Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 was Governor of the Capital Prefecture (Jingzhao), he exclusively…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
厲威嚴尹如霸承之以平易而京兆不
治是寬之後不必猛而猛之後亦有不
宜寬者則亦安在其爲相濟也今吏之
治不依於猛則漸靡而寬寬猛之義不
明而姑息操切之弊兩無當矣不知自
漢以還諸家之說果孰爲足發而足据
乎子諸生博達古今其必有見也試爲
主司言之
問東南之民舊稱柔脆素未習兵也曩自
===
倭夷爲患徵調紛紜困於罔效於是始
募民赴敵旋亦告捷而浙兵於是有名
乃今南北征備議徵募者遂皆曰非浙
兵不可豈浙民武勇四方果皆不及歟
抑頑民狃兵之利故樂於從而宿將狃
浙兵之利故又樂於用歟或謂募兵驕
縱難制終非邊境之福或謂民喜爲兵
盡去農業將爲浙中隱憂是皆可爲長
慮矣廼老於事者又謂浙旣多兵用之
punctuated:
厲威嚴，尹如霸承之以平易而京兆不治。是寬之後不必猛，而猛之後亦有不宜寬者，則亦安在其爲相濟也？今吏之治，不依於猛，則漸靡而寬；寬猛之義不明，而姑息、操切之弊兩無當矣。不知自漢以還，諸家之說，果孰爲足發而足据乎？子諸生博達古今，其必有見也，試爲主司言之。

問：東南之民，舊稱柔脆，素未習兵也。曩自倭夷爲患，徵調紛紜，困於罔效；於是始募民赴敵，旋亦告捷，而浙兵於是有名。乃今南北征備，議徵募者遂皆曰：「非浙兵不可。」豈浙民武勇，四方果皆不及歟？抑頑民狃兵之利，故樂於從；而宿將狃浙兵之利，故又樂於用歟？或謂募兵驕縱難制，終非邊境之福；或謂民喜爲兵，盡去農業，將爲浙中隱憂，是皆可爲長慮矣。廼老於事者又謂：浙旣多兵，用之
translation_en:
…solely exercised stern authority; when a governor like Ba [Huang Ba 黃霸] succeeded him with gentle simplicity, the Capital Prefecture (Jingzhao 京兆) was not brought to order. Thus, after leniency one need not employ severity, and after severity there are also cases where leniency is inappropriate—how then does this amount to their complementing one another? In present-day administration, when officials do not rely on severity, they gradually lapse into laxity and leniency; because the true meaning of leniency and severity is not understood, the twin abuses of indulgent laxity and harsh urgency both miss the mark. Looking from the Han dynasty onward, among the theories of the various thinkers, which indeed are sufficient to illuminate the issue and serve as a reliable basis? You students are broadly learned in ancient and modern affairs and must surely have insights on this; try to set them forth for the examiners.

Question: The people of the Southeast have long been described as gentle and fragile, and have never been accustomed to warfare. In the past, when the Japanese raiders (Woyi 倭夷) caused disaster, troop requisitions and transfers were manifold and confused, yet we were distressed by their lack of results. Thereupon we first began recruiting local commoners to go forth and engage the enemy; before long they reported victories, and the soldiers of Zhejiang thus gained renown. Now, in punitive expeditions and defense preparations in both the North and the South, those who deliberate on requisitioning and recruiting troops all say: "Nothing but Zhejiang soldiers will do." Is it really that the martial valor of the people of Zhejiang is unmatched by any of the other regions? Or is it that unruly commoners have grown accustomed to the profits of soldiering and thus gladly enlist, while veteran generals have grown accustomed to the advantage of Zhejiang troops and thus gladly employ them? Some say that recruited soldiers are arrogant, undisciplined, and hard to control, and in the end are no blessing to the frontiers; others say that because the common people delight in becoming soldiers and entirely abandon agriculture, this will become a hidden trouble within Zhejiang—all of these are matters warranting far-sighted concern. Yet those experienced in affairs further argue that since Zhejiang already has many soldiers, employing them…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可急四方之危不用將貽本土之患是
其爲說然歟否歟今日欲止募兵非南
北練兵不可也顧
廷議之責望甚殷而邊鎭之振飭未效豈亦
各有其說歟諸鎭之兵未練則募兵之
令未可已浙之事將安極歟今兵之入
薊者凡數千矣期以數年一罷其罷將
安歸而兵之入廣者亦毋慮數千廣土
且寧是兵亦將安厝也當事者甚慄焉
===
故以問之諸生諸生明於當世之務以
待用者不特廑於桑梓之慮抑亦憂先
天下之憂矣願悉言之毋隱
punctuated: 可急四方之危，不用將貽本土之患。是其爲說然歟？否歟？今日欲止募兵，非南北練兵不可也。顧廷議之責望甚殷，而邊鎭之振飭未效，豈亦各有其說歟？諸鎭之兵未練，則募兵之令未可已，浙之事將安極歟？今兵之入薊者凡數千矣，期以數年一罷，其罷將安歸？而兵之入廣者亦毋慮數千，廣土且寧，是兵亦將安厝也？當事者甚慄焉，故以問之諸生。諸生明於當世之務以待用者，不特廑於桑梓之慮，抑亦憂先天下之憂矣。願悉言之，毋隱。
translation_en: … can address the emergencies of all quarters, whereas not employing them will leave behind a menace to their native soil. Is this argument sound or not? Today, if we wish to stop recruiting soldiers, it is impossible unless both the North and the South train their own troops. Yet although court deliberations demand and expect this most earnestly, the revitalization and drilling in the frontier commands have not yet produced results—could it be that each side has its own explanation? If the troops of the various commands remain untrained, then the orders to recruit soldiers cannot cease; where, then, will the troubles of Zhejiang ever end? Now, the Zhejiang soldiers who have entered Jizhou number several thousand in all; they are scheduled to be discharged once every few years—when discharged, where will they return to? And the soldiers who have entered Guangdong and Guangxi likewise number roughly several thousand; now that the territories of Guangdong and Guangxi are becoming pacified, where will these soldiers be settled? Those in charge of affairs tremble greatly over this, and therefore we ask it of you students. You students who understand the affairs of the present age while awaiting employment are not only attentive to concerns for your native homeland, but also worry before the rest of the Empire worries. We wish you to speak of this in full, holding nothing back.
