title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
林放問禮之本子曰大哉問
莫睿
同考試官教諭張批得本則全體在中乃聖人
大之之意是作闡明精確宜錄之
同考試官教授伍批不尚辭華深切題意于其
可與言禮者
考試官教授萬批明妥
===
考試官教授吳批典實
時人問禮而識其大者聖人所以與之也夫有
本則有文禮之所以大也時人之問及此聖人
之與之也固宜且時至春秋爲禮者已不知有
其本矣時則有若林放者獨以之爲問焉蓋不
安於末流之趨而將以求夫作者之意有見於
靡文之失而思以探夫無體之真也是其爲問
與夫子之從先進有默契者故夫子與之曰習
俗易以移人忠信乃可學禮今之言禮者孰不
punctuated:
第壹場
四書

「林放問禮之本。子曰：『大哉問！』」

莫睿

同考試官教諭張批：得本則全體在中，乃聖人大之之意。是作闡明精確，宜錄之。
同考試官教授伍批：不尚辭華，深切題意，于其可與言禮者。
考試官教授萬批：明妥。
考試官教授吳批：典實。

時人問禮而識其大者，聖人所以與之也。夫有本則有文，禮之所以大也。時人之問及此，聖人之與之也固宜。且時至春秋，爲禮者已不知有其本矣。時則有若林放者，獨以之爲問焉。蓋不安於末流之趨，而將以求夫作者之意；有見於靡文之失，而思以探夫無體之真也。是其爲問，與夫子之從先進有默契者，故夫子與之曰：習俗易以移人，忠信乃可學禮。今之言禮者，孰不
translation_en:
First Session
Four Books

"Lin Fang asked about the fundamental root of ritual. The Master said, 'A great question indeed!'" [Analects 3.4]

Mo Rui 莫睿

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor Zhang 張: Once one grasps the root, the entire substance is contained within it; this is the meaning of the Sage's praising it as great. This essay elucidates the point with precision and accuracy; it ought to be selected for recording.
Comment by Associate Examiner Professor Wu 伍: It does not prize华麗 flowery verbiage, yet deeply and incisively grasps the meaning of the theme—here [reading 于 as 予/於?] is one with whom one can speak of ritual.
Comment by Examiner Professor Wan 萬: Clear and sound.
Comment by Examiner Professor Wu 吳: Classical and substantial.

When a man of the age asked about ritual and recognized what was great in it, that was why the Sage commended him. Now, where there is the root, there is the cultural pattern; this is why ritual is great. When a man of the age extended his inquiry to this, it was certainly fitting that the Sage commended him.

Moreover, by the time of the Spring and Autumn period, those who practiced ritual already no longer knew that it had a root. At that time there was someone like Lin Fang, who alone made this his question. This was because he was not content with the tendencies of a decadent age, and sought to recover the intent of the ancient creators of ritual; he perceived the failings of extravagant artifice, and wished to probe the genuine reality of ritual that has no fixed physical form. Thus his question was in tacit accord with the Master's own preference for following the men of former times [in ritual and music, Analects 11.1].

Therefore the Master commended him, saying: Customary habits easily sway men, yet only with loyalty and good faith can one learn ritual. Among those today who speak of ritual, who does not…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
貴文也而放也獨有尚質之思焉實意未漓則
儀章具備是問之雖止於本也而凡禮之品式
百爲者皆將於此乎出矣今之爲禮者孰不逐
末也而放也乃有崇本之論焉本真既得則物
采具存是問之雖未及其全也而凡禮之經緯
萬端者皆將於此乎具矣斂之無文而自有以
基天下之至文採之無體而實可以該天下之
全體不亦大哉其問乎吁是可以見夫子維世
之意不得已之心矣夫有本有文者禮之全亦
===
禮之大也大林放之問者若曰世之忘本甚矣
苟有本焉即無文亦不失其爲大也故曰寧儉
寧戚禮豈止於儉戚哉他日又曰文質彬彬然
後君子是則夫子議道之意
凡爲天下國家有九經曰脩身也尊賢也
親親也敬大臣也體羣臣也子庶民也
來百工也柔遠人也懷諸侯也脩身則
道立尊賢則不惑親親則諸父昆弟不
怨敬大臣則不眩體羣臣則士之報禮
punctuated:
貴文也，而放也獨有尚質之思焉。實意未漓，則儀章具備；是問之雖止於本也，而凡禮之品式百爲者，皆將於此乎出矣。今之爲禮者，孰不逐末也，而放也乃有崇本之論焉。本真既得，則物采具存；是問之雖未及其全也，而凡禮之經緯萬端者，皆將於此乎具矣。斂之無文，而自有以基天下之至文；採之無體，而實可以該天下之全體。不亦大哉，其問乎！吁！是可以見夫子維世之意、不得已之心矣。夫有本有文者，禮之全，亦禮之大也。大林放之問者，若曰：世之忘本甚矣！苟有本焉，即無文亦不失其爲大也。故曰「寧儉」、「寧戚」。禮豈止於儉、戚哉？他日又曰：「文質彬彬，然後君子。」是則夫子議道之意。
「凡爲天下國家有九經，曰：脩身也，尊賢也，親親也，敬大臣也，體羣臣也，子庶民也，來百工也，柔遠人也，懷諸侯也。脩身則道立，尊賢則不惑，親親則諸父昆弟不怨，敬大臣則不眩，體羣臣則士之報禮…
translation_en:
…prize outward refinement? Yet Lin Fang alone harbors the thought of esteeming unadorned substance. When genuine intent has not yet grown thin, ceremonial forms and insignia are fully provided for; thus, although his question stops at the root, all the hundred enactments and graded rules of ritual will emerge from this. Among those who practice ritual today, who does not chase after the branches? Yet Lin Fang comes forth with a discussion that exalts the root. Once fundamental authenticity is grasped, material ornaments and colors are all preserved; thus, although his question does not yet reach the entirety of ritual, all the myriad threads and warp and woof of ritual will be complete herein. Gathered in, it is without ornament, yet of itself it serves to lay the foundation for the utmost refinement in the world; sought out, it is without fixed form, yet in reality it can encompass the complete body of ritual in the world. How great indeed is his question!

Ah! From this one can see the Master's intent to uphold the age and his heart that had no other choice. Now, having both root and refinement is the completeness of ritual, and also the greatness of ritual. In praising Lin Fang's question as great, it was as if to say: The world's forgetting of the root has gone to extremes! If only the root is present, even without outward refinement it does not lose its greatness. Therefore he said, "It is better to be frugal," and "It is better to be sorrowful." Yet how could ritual merely stop at frugality and sorrow? On another day he also said, "When substance and refinement are in due proportion, only then is one a gentleman." This, then, is the Master's meaning in deliberating upon the Way.

"In all governance of the empire, the state, and the family, there are nine standard rules: namely, cultivating the person, honoring the worthy, cherishing relatives, respecting the great ministers, identifying with the whole body of officers, treating the common people as one's children, encouraging the hundred artisans to come, showing tenderness to men from afar, andcherishing the feudal lords. If one cultivates the person, the Way is established; if one honors the worthy, one is free from doubt; if one cherishes relatives, uncles and brothers bear no resentment; if one respects the great ministers, one is not confused in affairs; if one identifies with the whole body of officers, the gentlemen will repay courtesy…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
重子庶民則百姓勸來百工則財用足
柔遠人則四方歸之懷諸侯則天下畏
之
張潘
同考試官教諭黃批此題難於隱括是作比對
嚴整點綴融切可式之文也宜錄之
同考試官教授顧批體裁雅飭意義渾融是得
長題之法者
考試官教授萬批融會題義文亦瑩然
===
考試官教授吳批整潔
中庸第言爲治之常道而因以著其效焉夫九
經爲治之常道也舉而行之其效有不類應者
哉夫子以此告魯君也謂夫明於三近以脩身
者固知所以治天下國家矣然道豈一端而已
乎其爲正大而不偏常乆而不易者蓋有九焉
九者維何身者天下國家之本脩身要矣欲以
脩身而人之有賢不可以不尊也欲以仁身而
家之有親不可以不親也以經朝廷而大臣吾
punctuated:
重，子庶民則百姓勸，來百工則財用足，柔遠人則四方歸之，懷諸侯則天下畏之。
張潘。
同考試官教諭黃批：此題難於隱括，是作比對嚴整，點綴融切，可式之文也。宜錄之。
同考試官教授顧批：體裁雅飭，意義渾融，是得長題之法者。
考試官教授萬批：融會題義，文亦瑩然。
考試官教授吳批：整潔。
《中庸》第言爲治之常道，而因以著其效焉。夫九經，爲治之常道也，舉而行之，其效有不類應者哉？夫子以此告魯君也，謂夫明於三近以脩身者，固知所以治天下國家矣；然道豈一端而已乎？其爲正大而不偏、常乆而不易者，蓋有九焉。九者維何？身者，天下國家之本，脩身要矣。欲以脩身，而人之有賢，不可以不尊也；欲以仁身，而家之有親，不可以不親也。以經朝廷，而大臣吾…
translation_en:
… heavy; by treating the common people as one's children, the hundred surnames are encouraged; by attracting the hundred artisans, wealth and resources are made sufficient; by showing tenderness to men from afar, the four quarters submit to him; by cherishing the feudal lords, all under Heaven hold him in awe."

Zhang Pan.

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Huang: This topic is difficult to summarize comprehensively. This composition has strictly ordered parallelisms and harmoniously fitting embellishments; it is an essay worthy of serving as a model. It ought to be recorded for publication.

Comment by Associate Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Gu: The form is elegant and disciplined, and the meaning is seamlessly integrated; this is one who has grasped the method for handling a long topic.

Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Wan: It thoroughly synthesizes the meaning of the topic, and the writing is also lustrous.

Comment by Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Wu: Neat and clean.

The Doctrine of the Mean (Zhongyong) enumerates in order the constant principles for governing, and thereby sets forth their effects. Now, the Nine Standard Rules are the constant principles for governing; if one takes them up and puts them into practice, how could their effects fail to respond in kind? The Master spoke of this to the ruler of Lu, saying that one who understands the three things near to the Way in order to cultivate his person surely knows wherewith to govern the empire, the state, and the family. Yet how could the Way consist of merely a single aspect? Those principles that are upright, great, and unbiased, constant, enduring, and unchanging, are indeed nine in number. What are the nine? The person is the root of the empire, the state, and the family, so cultivating the person is essential. If one wishes to cultivate one's person, then where there are worthy men among others, one cannot fail to honor them; if one wishes to make one's person benevolent, then where there are kinsmen in one's family, one cannot fail to show affection to them. To regulate the royal court, as for the great ministers, we…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
其敬之羣臣吾其體之焉以經邦國而庶民吾
其子之百工吾其來之焉以經天下而遠人吾
其柔之諸侯吾其懷之焉此皆文武之所已行
者信能行之而其效豈無可見乎彼身具脩齊
治平之道身脩則道立矣賢者尊之則道益以
明而不惑焉親者親之則仁益以洽而不怨焉
由是而觀政於朝則大臣敬之而有以資其斷
羣臣體之而有以資其忠也由是而觀治於國
則庶民子之而有以得其心百工來之而有以
===
得其財也由是而觀化於天下則遠人柔之而
有以致其歸諸侯懷之而有以致其畏也此皆
文武之所已試者誠欲致之而其事豈無可舉
乎雖然九經以爲天下國家固矣而究其本尤
約于一心蓋能純其心則推之九經皆實政也
苟心有不純則雖脩之身者且爲虛文而況其
施之家國天下者乎故曰有關雎麟趾之意而
後可以行周官之法度
智譬則巧也聖譬則力也
punctuated:
其敬之，羣臣吾其體之焉；以經邦國，而庶民吾其子之，百工吾其來之焉；以經天下，而遠人吾其柔之，諸侯吾其懷之焉。此皆文、武之所已行者，信能行之，而其效豈無可見乎？彼身具脩、齊、治、平之道，身脩則道立矣；賢者尊之，則道益以明而不惑焉；親者親之，則仁益以洽而不怨焉。由是而觀政於朝，則大臣敬之而有以資其斷，羣臣體之而有以資其忠也；由是而觀治於國，則庶民子之而有以得其心，百工來之而有以得其財也；由是而觀化於天下，則遠人柔之而有以致其歸，諸侯懷之而有以致其畏也。此皆文、武之所已試者，誠欲致之，而其事豈無可舉乎？雖然，九經以爲天下國家固矣，而究其本，尤約于一心。蓋能純其心，則推之九經皆實政也；苟心有不純，則雖脩之身者且爲虛文，而況其施之家、國、天下者乎？故曰：「有《關雎》、《麟趾》之意，而後可以行《周官》之法度。」
智，譬則巧也；聖，譬則力也。
translation_en:
… must respect them, and the body of minor officials, we must treat them with empathetic consideration; to regulate the state, the common people, we must treat them as our children, and the artisans of all trades, we must attract them; to regulate the world, the people from afar, we must treat them gently, and the feudal lords, we must cherish them. These are all things that Kings Wen and Wu already practiced; if one can truly practice them, how could their efficacy fail to be seen?

Now, the ruler's own person embodies the way of self-cultivation, ordering the family, governing the state, and bringing peace to the world; when the person is cultivated, the Way is established. When the worthy are honored, the Way becomes ever clearer and one is free from perplexity; when relatives are treated with affection, benevolence becomes ever more harmonious and there is no resentment. Looking from this at governance in the court: when the great ministers are respected, one may draw upon their decisiveness in judgment, and when the body of minor officials are treated with empathetic consideration, one may draw upon their loyalty. Looking from this at administration in the state: when the common people are treated as one's children, one wins their hearts, and when the artisans of all trades are attracted, one secures a sufficiency of goods. Looking from this at moral transformation throughout the world: when people from afar are treated gently, one brings about their allegiance, and when the feudal lords are cherished, one inspires their reverent awe. These are all things that Kings Wen and Wu already tested; if one truly wishes to bring them about, how could there be no concrete measures to undertake?

Even so, that the Nine Standard Rules serve to govern the world, the state, and the family is certain, yet if we trace them to their root, they are even more succinctly converged in the single mind. For if one can keep one's mind pure, then when extended to the Nine Standard Rules, all of them become substantive governance; if the mind is not pure, then even what is applied to cultivating one's own person will be mere empty formality, how much more so what is extended to the family, the state, and the world! Therefore it is said: "Only when one has the spirit of the 'Guanju' and 'Linzhi' odes can one implement the institutional measures of the Offices of Zhou (Zhouguan)."

Wisdom may be compared to skill; sageliness may be compared to strength.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
沈堯中
同考試官教諭翟批聖智巧力比擬獨難是作
辭不繁而義明晰中鵠之文也可以錄矣
同考試官教授張批以巧力發智聖辭約而精
意婉而盡
考試官教授萬批明潔
考試官教授吳批莊雅
大賢擬智聖於射者之事見其所由全也夫智
聖合一而德斯全矣其與射之巧力又何以異
===
哉此孟子推尊孔子之言也蓋曰大哉孔子之
爲聖乎故以樂言之始條理者固爲智之事矣
是智也譬之於射則又巧之謂焉蓋巧以神用
所以運其力於必中者也孔子之心神明所會
凡其爲清爲任爲和之理莫不兼照於始而昭
然有眞知焉是即射者之得心應手而躍然有
定見也精其道於中正不偏與精其藝於正鵠
不失其爲明諸心則一而已智非巧而何哉終
條理者固爲聖之事矣是聖也譬之於射則又
punctuated:
沈堯中
同考試官教諭翟批：聖智巧力，比擬獨難。是作辭不繁而義明晰，中鵠之文也，可以錄矣。
同考試官教授張批：以巧力發智聖，辭約而精，意婉而盡。
考試官教授萬批：明潔。
考試官教授吳批：莊雅。
大賢擬智聖於射者之事，見其所由全也。夫智聖合一，而德斯全矣。其與射之巧力，又何以異哉？此孟子推尊孔子之言也。蓋曰：大哉，孔子之爲聖乎！故以樂言之，始條理者，固爲智之事矣。是智也，譬之於射，則又巧之謂焉。蓋巧以神用，所以運其力於必中者也。孔子之心，神明所會，凡其爲清、爲任、爲和之理，莫不兼照於始，而昭然有眞知焉。是即射者之得心應手，而躍然有定見也。精其道於中正不偏，與精其藝於正鵠不失，其爲明諸心則一而已。智非巧而何哉？終條理者，固爲聖之事矣。是聖也，譬之於射，則又
translation_en:
Shen Yaozhong 沈堯中
Comment by Associate Examiner County Director of Studies Zhai 翟: The analogy between sageliness and wisdom on the one hand, and skill and strength on the other, is uniquely difficult to expound. In this composition, the words are not prolix and the meaning is clear and distinct; it is an essay that hits the bull's-eye and is worthy of being recorded for publication.
Comment by Associate Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Zhang 張: Using skill and strength to elucidate wisdom and sageliness, the wording is concise yet precise, and the thought is subtle yet exhaustive.
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Wan 萬: Clear and lucid.
Comment by Examiner Prefectural Director of Studies Wu 吳: Dignified and elegant.

The great worthy compares wisdom and sageliness to the business of the archer, thereby revealing how they attain completeness. Now, when wisdom and sageliness are united as one, virtue is thus complete. How does this differ from the skill and strength of archery? These are the words with which Mencius extolled Confucius. It is as if he said: How great is Confucius as a sage! Therefore, speaking of it in terms of music, beginning the orderly progression is indeed the work of wisdom. This wisdom, if compared to archery, is what is called skill. For skill functions through the spirit; it is that by which one directs one's strength to hit the mark without fail. In the mind of Confucius, where spiritual clarity converged, all the principles of being pure, of taking office, and of being harmonious were simultaneously illuminated from the very beginning, so that he luminously possessed true knowledge. This is just like the archer whose hand responds to his mind and who vividly possesses a settled vision. Perfecting one's Way in central correctness without bias, and perfecting one's art in not missing the target's center—as a matter of clear understanding within the mind, they are one and the same. What is wisdom if not skill? Completing the orderly progression is indeed the work of sageliness. This sageliness, if compared to archery, is what is…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
力之謂焉蓋力以形用所以將其巧於必至者
也孔子之身神化所備凡其爲清爲任爲和之
道莫不深造於終而渾然有成德焉是卽射者
之挽强引滿而毅然有定力也行之而必造其
極與射之而必及夫遠其爲體諸身則一而已
聖非力而何哉巧力兼資斯爲善射而巧則所
以用其力者智聖兼備斯爲全德而智則所以
成其聖者卽此觀之而孔子之異於三子可見
矣大抵聖人無知而無不知無不知者實有其
===
見也而其無知者不自有其見也若三子則各
有其見矣其爲清任和豈非至德然局於見而
不能相通則亦終歸於一偏之行而已故曰進
學則在致知
易
初九利用爲大作元吉无咎
錢應樂
同考試官教諭張 批 發揮大作元吉處深得人
臣報君之心且筆力清勁無一蔓語宜錄以式
punctuated:
力之謂焉。蓋力以形用，所以將其巧於必至者也。孔子之身，神化所備，凡其爲清、爲任、爲和之道，莫不深造於終，而渾然有成德焉；是卽射者之挽强引滿，而毅然有定力也。行之而必造其極，與射之而必及夫遠，其爲體諸身則一而已，聖非力而何哉？巧力兼資，斯爲善射，而巧則所以用其力者；智聖兼備，斯爲全德，而智則所以成其聖者。卽此觀之，而孔子之異於三子可見矣。大抵聖人無知而無不知，無不知者，實有其見也；而其無知者，不自有其見也。若三子則各有其見矣。其爲清、任、和，豈非至德？然局於見而不能相通，則亦終歸於一偏之行而已。故曰：進學則在致知。

易
「初九，利用爲大作，元吉，无咎。」
錢應樂
同考試官教諭張批：發揮「大作」、「元吉」處，深得人臣報君之心。且筆力清勁，無一蔓語，宜錄以式。
translation_en:
…is what is meant by strength. For strength operates through physical form, and is that by which one conveys one's skill to its certain destination. In the person of Confucius, spiritual transformation was complete; all the ways of being pure, responsible, and harmonious were deeply attained to the very end, resulting in a seamlessly perfected virtue. This is just like an archer drawing a strong bow to the full, possessing resolute and unyielding strength. Practicing virtue so as to inevitably reach its ultimate perfection, and shooting an arrow so as to inevitably reach afar, are one and the same in being embodied in the person. What is sageliness if not strength? Only when skill and strength are both relied upon does one become a good archer, yet skill is that by which one directs one's strength; only when wisdom and sageliness are both complete does one possess complete virtue, yet wisdom is that by which one brings one's sageliness to completion. Viewed from this perspective, how Confucius differed from the three worthies can be seen. Broadly speaking, the sage has no preconceptions and yet there is nothing he does not know. That there is nothing he does not know is because he truly possesses insight; and that he has no preconceptions is because he does not cling to his own views. As for the three worthies, each had his own fixed view. In their purity, responsibility, and harmony, how could these not be supreme virtues? Yet because they were confined to their own views and could not interpenetrate, in the end they merely ended up in one-sided conduct. Therefore it is said: advancing in learning lies in extending knowledge.

Book of Changes (Yi)
"Nine in the first place: It is beneficial to use this for great undertakings. Supreme good fortune, no blame."
By Qian Yingle 錢應樂.
Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Zhang 張 comments: His elaboration on "great undertakings" and "supreme good fortune" deeply captures the heart of a minister repaying his sovereign. Moreover, the force of his brush is clear and vigorous, without a single superfluous word. It should be recorded as a model.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官敎授伍批意旣親切詞復典雅是始
進而懷圖報之志者錄之
考試官敎授萬批典雅
考試官敎授吳批明健
聖人繫益初爻而勉人臣之報君者至矣蓋臣
之報君不易也必大作而又元吉斯其至矣乎
且益之初九居卦之下是爲始進之士而受益
於上則寵遇爲特隆矣是豈可以無報乎必也
奮許國之忠而大有爲於天下竭致身之義而
===
懋樹立於當時計安社稷者毅然圖之無少遜
避也澤被生民者慨然任之不少因循也蓋必
如是而後可以報明主答殊恩也是乃所謂利
矣然居下而任上之事則衆望攸歸始進而圖
非常之功則羣疑畢集若之何而可免於咎也
必其學術純正矣而謀之孔臧心事光明矣而
行之盡善爲社稷而周萬世之慮真無毫髮之
可議也夫然後我任之人信之而庶可有辭於
天下也已爲生民而垂永賴之烈真無纖悉之
punctuated:
同考試官敎授伍批：意旣親切，詞復典雅，是始進而懷圖報之志者，錄之。
考試官敎授萬批：典雅。
考試官敎授吳批：明健。
聖人繫《益》初爻，而勉人臣之報君者至矣。蓋臣之報君不易也，必「大作」而又「元吉」，斯其至矣乎！且《益》之初九居卦之下，是爲始進之士，而受益於上，則寵遇爲特隆矣。是豈可以無報乎？必也奮許國之忠，而大有爲於天下；竭致身之義，而懋樹立於當時。計安社稷者，毅然圖之，無少遜避也；澤被生民者，慨然任之，不少因循也。蓋必如是，而後可以報明主、答殊恩也，是乃所謂「利」矣。然居下而任上之事，則衆望攸歸；始進而圖非常之功，則羣疑畢集，若之何而可免於「咎」也？必其學術純正矣，而謀之孔臧；心事光明矣，而行之盡善。爲社稷而周萬世之慮，真無毫髮之可議也，夫然後我任之，人信之，而庶可有辭於天下也已；爲生民而垂永賴之烈，真無纖悉之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Wu, comments: The ideas are relevant and earnest, and the phrasing is furthermore refined and elegant. This is someone just entering service who harbors the ambition to repay his sovereign; record it.
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Wan, comments: Refined and elegant.
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Wu, comments: Lucid and vigorous.

When the sage appended the line statement to the first line of the hexagram Increase (Yi), his exhortation for a minister to repay his sovereign was utmost indeed. For a minister to repay his sovereign is no easy matter; only when he engages in "great undertakings" and moreover achieves "supreme auspiciousness" has he reached the utmost! Moreover, the nine at the beginning of Increase occupies the bottom of the hexagram. This represents a scholar just entering official service; yet because he receives benefit from above, the favor and reception he enjoys are especially generous. How could this go without repayment? He must rouse the loyalty of dedicating himself to the state and accomplish great deeds in the world; he must exhaust the righteousness of devoting his life and strive for distinguished achievements in his own time. In plans to secure the altars of state, he resolutely pursues them without the slightest shrinking or evasion; in measures that shower blessings upon the common people, he wholeheartedly takes responsibility for them without the least procrastination or conformity to routine. Only when he acts like this can he repay an enlightened ruler and answer extraordinary grace; this is what is meant by "advantageous." Yet when one occupies a lower position and takes on the affairs of superiors, the expectations of the multitude converge upon him; when one has just entered service and plans extraordinary achievements, all manner of doubts gather around him. How then can he avoid "blame"? Only when his learning is pure and upright will his counsels be thoroughly good; only when his intentions are open and bright will his actions be wholly perfected. Working for the altars of state, he forms comprehensive plans for ten thousand generations until there is truly not a hair's breadth to be criticized; only then, when I take responsibility for it, will others trust in it, and one may perhaps be able to justify oneself before the world. Working for the common people, he hands down glorious achievements on which they may perpetually rely until there is truly not the slightest detail that is…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不備也夫然後我爲之人安之而實爲有利於
吾君也已不然跡疑而議起得无咎乎吁周公
之所以勉報君者至矣夫報君固不易也而報
君之事皆生於心心純矣又何事不可爲也是
故公遜碩膚赤舃几几之心其諸萬世臣道之
極與
昔者聖人之作易也幽贊於神明而生蓍
參天兩地而倚數觀變於陰陽而立卦
發揮於剛柔而生爻和順於道德而理
===
於義窮理盡性以至於命
莫睿
同考試官教諭張批作者多在揲蓍上說殊非
聖人作易事此作精透得旨是深於易者
同考試官教授伍批體裁整潔詞意簡明深得
潔淨精微之旨錄之
考試官教授萬批詞約而意盡
考試官教授吳批精確
大傳旣原易之所由因著易之所具甚矣易之
punctuated:
不備也。夫然後我爲之，人安之，而實爲有利於吾君也已。不然，跡疑而議起，得无咎乎？吁！周公之所以勉報君者至矣。夫報君固不易也，而報君之事皆生於心。心純矣，又何事不可爲也？是故「公遜碩膚，赤舃几几」之心，其諸萬世臣道之極與！

昔者聖人之作易也，幽贊於神明而生蓍，參天兩地而倚數，觀變於陰陽而立卦，發揮於剛柔而生爻，和順於道德而理於義，窮理盡性以至於命。

莫睿

同考試官教諭張批：作者多在揲蓍上說，殊非聖人作《易》事。此作精透得旨，是深於《易》者。
同考試官教授伍批：體裁整潔，詞意簡明，深得潔淨精微之旨，錄之。
考試官教授萬批：詞約而意盡。
考試官教授吳批：精確。

大傳旣原《易》之所由，因著《易》之所具，甚矣《易》之
translation_en:
… left unprovided for. Only then, when I act upon it, will others rest content with it, and it will truly be advantageous to my ruler. Otherwise, if one's actions arouse suspicion and criticisms arise, how could one be free from blame? Ah! That whereby the Duke of Zhou exhorted ministers to repay their ruler reached the utmost. Indeed, repaying one's ruler is certainly not easy, yet all matters of repaying the ruler arise from the mind. Once the mind is pure, what matter cannot be undertaken? Therefore, the mind expressed in "The Duke humbly bore his great美 [grandeur], his red slippers calm and composed" is perhaps the ultimate standard of the way of the minister for ten thousand generations!

"In ancient times, when the sages made the Changes (Yi), they mysteriously assisted the spiritual and luminous and thus produced the milfoil stalks; they assigned three to Heaven and two to Earth and thus established the numbers; they observed the transformations in yin and yang and thus established the hexagrams; they brought forth the firm and the yielding and thus produced the lines; they harmonized with the Way and its virtue and ordered them according to righteousness; and they exhausted the principles of things and fulfilled their nature, so as to arrive at the decree of Heaven."

Mo Rui 莫睿

Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang comments: Most writers discuss this in terms of sorting the milfoil stalks, which is really not the business of how the sages made the Changes. This essay is subtle, penetrating, and grasps the main purport; the author is someone deeply versed in the Changes.
Associate Examiner, Professor Wu comments: The structure is neat and clean, the diction and meaning are concise and clear. It deeply grasps the purport of purity, stillness, subtlety, and refinement. Record it for publication.
Examiner, Professor Wan comments: The words are economical, yet the meaning is fully expressed.
Examiner, Professor Wu comments: Precise and accurate.

The Great Commentary, having traced from what the Changes originated, thereupon sets forth what the Changes possesses. Great indeed is the Changes in its…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
爲道大也觀其所由稽其所具易誠造化之書
也哉說卦以此盡易之蘊蓋曰易之爲易其用
則有蓍數其本則有卦爻蓍何自而生乎聖人
幽賛神明而神物生焉則蓍者固神明之所寓
也數何自而倚乎聖人參兩天地而易數起焉
則數者固天地之所爲也天地之間陰陽而已
聖人達觀其變而立之爲純襍之卦是至賾者
在於卦焉物性之常剛柔而已聖人發揮其用
而斷之爲動靜之爻是至動者在於爻焉蓍數
===
具而變動不拘則凡天下之道莫不流行於易
矣卦爻立而廣大悉備則凡天下之道莫不統
體於易矣是故言乎其道也德也易固和順之
而不違而其散殊之義則又析之至精而不紊
焉言乎其理也性也易固窮盡之而各得而其
從出之命則亦與之爲一而無間焉夫其始也
莫非求端於造化而其既也有以通極於造化
易非造化之書而何抑此心易也聖人心涵道
德性命之精是故天地爲紀神明爲徒陰陽爲
punctuated: 爲道大也！觀其所由，稽其所具，《易》誠造化之書也哉！《說卦》以此盡《易》之蘊，蓋曰：《易》之爲《易》，其用則有蓍、數，其本則有卦、爻。蓍何自而生乎？聖人幽賛神明，而神物生焉，則蓍者固神明之所寓也。數何自而倚乎？聖人參兩天地，而《易》數起焉，則數者固天地之所爲也。天地之間，陰陽而已，聖人達觀其變，而立之爲純襍之卦，是至賾者在於卦焉。物性之常，剛柔而已，聖人發揮其用，而斷之爲動靜之爻，是至動者在於爻焉。蓍、數具而變動不拘，則凡天下之道，莫不流行於《易》矣；卦、爻立而廣大悉備，則凡天下之道，莫不統體於《易》矣。是故言乎其道也、德也，《易》固和順之而不違，而其散殊之義，則又析之至精而不紊焉；言乎其理也、性也，《易》固窮盡之而各得，而其從出之命，則亦與之爲一而無間焉。夫其始也，莫非求端於造化；而其既也，有以通極於造化。《易》非造化之書而何？抑此心《易》也，聖人心涵道德性命之精，是故天地爲紀，神明爲徒，陰陽爲…
translation_en: …Way is! Observing where it originates and examining what it comprises, the Changes (Yi) is truly the book of the creative transformation of nature! The "Discussion of the Trigrams" (Shuogua) uses this to exhaust the profound essence of the Changes, saying in effect: For the Changes to be the Changes, in its application there are milfoil stalks and numbers, and in its foundation there are hexagrams and lines. From where do the milfoil stalks arise? The sages mysteriously assisted the spiritual and luminous, and thus the divine things were born; therefore, the milfoil stalks are indeed where the spiritual and luminous reside. Upon what are the numbers established? The sages assigned three to Heaven and two to Earth, and thus the numbers of the Changes arose; therefore, the numbers are indeed what Heaven and Earth produce. Between Heaven and Earth there are only yin and yang; the sages comprehensively observed their transformations and established them as pure and mixed hexagrams—thus what is most intricate lies within the hexagrams. In the constant nature of things there are only the firm and the yielding; the sages brought forth their functions and determined them as moving and quiescent lines—thus what is most active lies within the lines. When milfoil stalks and numbers are present and their transformations and movements are unconstrained, then among all the Ways under heaven, there is none that does not flow through the Changes. When hexagrams and lines are established and in their breadth and greatness everything is complete, then among all the Ways under heaven, there is none that is not comprehensively embodied in the Changes. Therefore, speaking of the Way and of virtue, the Changes indeed harmonizes with and conforms to them without violation, while as for their diverse and particular meanings, it analyzes them with the utmost precision without confusion. Speaking of principle and of nature, the Changes indeed exhausts them so that each attains its proper place, while as for the destiny from which they issue, it also merges with it as one without any gap. In the beginning, nothing was not sought as an inception from creative transformation; and in the end, it was able to penetrate to the ultimate of creative transformation. What else is the Changes if not the book of creative transformation? Yet this is the Changes of the mind. The mind of the sages encompasses the essence of the Way, virtue, nature, and destiny; therefore, taking Heaven and Earth as its standard, the spiritual and luminous as its companions, yin and yang as its…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
柄剛柔為用其蓍數則此心之參伍也其卦爻
則此心之法象也故能先天開人而成天下之
務學易者苟不求諸心以窮性命之理而徒曰
用易用易是卜筮之易也易主卜筮而易其衰
矣
書
文命敷于四海祗承于帝曰后克艱厥后
臣克艱厥臣政乃乂黎民敏德
沈堯中
===
同考試官教諭翟批說出舜禹保治之心宛見
虞廷氣象可錄
同考試官教授張批發明克艱意殆盡是深於
書者
考試官教授萬批疏暢
考試官教授吳批明切
聖臣當治世而深有望於君臣之保治焉蓋保
治者聖人之心也文命四敷而猶持之以克艱
焉則治其永保之矣此大禹祗承之意也稽古
punctuated:
柄，剛柔為用；其蓍數則此心之參伍也，其卦爻則此心之法象也。故能先天開人，而成天下之務。學《易》者苟不求諸心以窮性命之理，而徒曰「用《易》、用《易》」，是卜筮之《易》也。《易》主卜筮，而《易》其衰矣。

《書》

「文命敷于四海，祗承于帝。曰：『后克艱厥后，臣克艱厥臣，政乃乂，黎民敏德。』」
沈堯中
同考試官教諭翟批：說出舜、禹保治之心，宛見虞廷氣象，可錄。
同考試官教授張批：發明「克艱」意殆盡，是深於《書》者。
考試官教授萬批：疏暢。
考試官教授吳批：明切。

聖臣當治世，而深有望於君臣之保治焉。蓋保治者，聖人之心也。文命四敷，而猶持之以克艱焉，則治其永保之矣。此大禹祗承之意也。稽古
translation_en:
… handle, and firmness and softness serve as the function; its milfoil numbers are the permutations and combinations of this mind, and its hexagrams and lines are the models and images of this mind. Therefore, it was able to precede Heaven in opening the way for humankind and to accomplish the affairs of the world. If those who study the Book of Changes (Yi) do not seek it within their own minds in order to exhaust the principles of human nature and destiny, and merely say, "Use the Changes, use the Changes," then this is merely the Changes of divination. When the Changes is devoted solely to divination, the Changes is in decline!

Book of Documents (Shu)

"Hiswen-jiao [civilizing teachings and ordinances] were spread throughout the four seas, and he reverently responded to the Sovereign, saying: 'If the sovereign can appreciate the difficulty of being a sovereign, and the minister can appreciate the difficulty of being a minister, government will be well-ordered, and the black-haired people will be quick to pursue virtue.'"

Shen Yaozhong 沈堯中

Comment by Associate Examiner Instructor (jiaoyu) Zhai: He articulates the minds of Shun and Yu in preserving good governance, vividly revealing the atmosphere of the虞 (Yu) court. Worthy of selection.
Comment by Associate Examiner Professor (jiaoshou) Zhang: He elucidates the meaning of "appreciating the difficulty" almost exhaustively; this is someone deeply versed in the Book of Documents.
Comment by Examiner Professor Wan: Fluent and unhindered.
Comment by Examiner Professor Wu: Clear and to the point.

In an age of good order, the sage minister held deep hopes that ruler and minister would preserve that good governance. Indeed, preserving good governance is the mind of the sages. When civilizing ordinances had been spread throughout the four quarters and yet were still maintained through an appreciation of the difficulties involved, good order could be preserved forever. This was the meaning of the Great Yu's reverent response. Examining antiquity, …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
有虞之世以舜爲君而以禹爲之臣明良合而
德先之化四達于濬導之餘上下交而聲敎之
隆四訖于疆理之後斯時也政巳治矣民巳化
矣君臣若可無虞矣然以四海之心爲心而思
以保之者帝也以帝之心爲心而思以共保之
者禹也於是陳謨而祗承于帝曰主治在后后
毋以文命巳敷而易心生也必思君道惟艱所
以出政臨民者益兢業以圖之于上焉佐治在
臣臣毋以文命旣敷而易心生也必思臣道惟
===
艱所以輔政化民者益祗懼以承之于下焉君
臣一心則可以經政而政乃允釐盡善盡美秩
然于四海之中矣不然而奚其乂哉上下一德
則可以化民而民日遷善會極歸極雍然于四
海之内矣不然而奚其敏德哉是可見安不忘
危者聖帝無巳之心也而忠不忘誨者聖臣無
窮之念也禹陳之帝卽俞之玆有虞之治所以
永保無虞歟雖然責難在臣而致其責難在君
使君非帝舜將小康以自足而豐亨豫大之說
punctuated: 有虞之世，以舜爲君，而以禹爲之臣。明良合而德先之化，四達于濬導之餘；上下交而聲敎之隆，四訖于疆理之後。斯時也，政巳治矣，民巳化矣，君臣若可無虞矣。然以四海之心爲心，而思以保之者，帝也；以帝之心爲心，而思以共保之者，禹也。於是陳謨而祗承于帝曰：主治在后，后毋以文命巳敷而易心生也。必思君道惟艱，所以出政臨民者，益兢業以圖之于上焉。佐治在臣，臣毋以文命旣敷而易心生也。必思臣道惟艱，所以輔政化民者，益祗懼以承之于下焉。君臣一心，則可以經政，而政乃允釐，盡善盡美，秩然于四海之中矣；不然，而奚其乂哉？上下一德，則可以化民，而民日遷善，會極歸極，雍然于四海之内矣；不然，而奚其敏德哉？是可見安不忘危者，聖帝無巳之心也；而忠不忘誨者，聖臣無窮之念也。禹陳之，帝卽俞之，玆有虞之治所以永保無虞歟！雖然，責難在臣，而致其責難在君。使君非帝舜，將小康以自足，而豐亨豫大之說
translation_en: … in the age of Youyu (Shun), with Shun as sovereign and Yu as his minister: the enlightened ruler and worthy minister were united, and the transformation of putting virtue first reached in all four directions following the dredging and channeling of the waters; superior and inferior were in harmony, and the flourishing of prestigious teachings extended to the four quarters after the demarcation and ordering of the land. At this time, governance was already well-ordered, the people were already transformed, and sovereign and minister might seem to have had nothing further to worry about. Yet he who took the mind of the Four Seas as his own mind and sought to preserve this order was the Emperor; and he who took the Emperor's mind as his own mind and sought to jointly preserve it with him was Yu. Thereupon Yu set forth his counsels and reverently responded to the Emperor, saying: "The mastery of governance lies with the sovereign; let not the sovereign allow a heedless mind to arise because his civilizing mandate has already been spread abroad. He must reflect on the difficulty of the way of the sovereign, and in issuing policies and overseeing the people, be ever more cautious and diligent in planning for it from above. Assisting in governance lies with the minister; let not the minister allow a heedless mind to arise because the civilizing mandate has already been spread abroad. He must reflect on the difficulty of the way of the minister, and in assisting governance and transforming the people, be ever more reverent and fearful in upholding it from below." When sovereign and minister are of one mind, governance can be regulated, and administration will be truly ordered—perfectly good and perfectly noble, well-regulated throughout the Four Seas; if not, how could there be such order? When superior and inferior are of one virtue, the people can be transformed, and the people will daily move toward goodness—converging upon and returning to the standard of perfection, harmonious within the Four Seas; if not, how could they be so earnest in virtue? From this it can be seen that not forgetting danger in times of security is the unceasing mind of the sage Emperor, and not forgetting to admonish out of loyalty is the boundless concern of the sage minister. Yu set it forth, and the Emperor immediately assented to it—is this not why the good governance of Youyu was preserved forever without cause for anxiety? Even so, urging difficult achievements lies with the minister, while inspiring him to urge difficult achievements lies with the sovereign. Had the sovereign not been Emperor Shun, he would have been self-satisfied with minor peace, and doctrines of abundance, prosperity, ease, and grandeur …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
進矣又安望其祗愼責難之若此哉故曰主聖
則臣直
拜手稽首告嗣天子王矣用咸戒于王曰
王左右常伯常任準人綴衣虎賁
公羽立德
同考試官敎諭翟批能發周公率屬進戒之意
是有懷致君者錄之
同考試官敎授張批周臣告君任人之意含蓄
婉順是作得之佳士也
===
考試官敎授萬批典雅
考試官敎授吳批簡古
大臣以盡忠率臣而羣臣因以任人望君焉甚
矣左右之臣任之不可不愼也大臣啓羣臣盡
忠而羣臣因以此進戒其諸協忠事君者哉昔
成王親政周公欲其知恤也故率羣臣而贊之
曰嗣王臨御之初正任賢圖治之際爾諸臣皆
有尊君之義則亦皆有忠君之心者也其尚拜
手以致敬稽首以成禮而告吾嗣天子王焉凡
punctuated:
進矣，又安望其祗愼責難之若此哉？故曰：「主聖則臣直。」

拜手稽首，告嗣天子王矣。用咸戒于王，曰：「王左右常伯、常任、準人、綴衣、虎賁。」

公羽立德。
同考試官敎諭翟批：能發周公率屬進戒之意，是有懷致君者，錄之。
同考試官敎授張批：周臣告君任人之意，含蓄婉順，是作得之。佳士也。
考試官敎授萬批：典雅。
考試官敎授吳批：簡古。

大臣以盡忠率臣，而羣臣因以任人望君焉。甚矣，左右之臣，任之不可不愼也！大臣啓羣臣盡忠，而羣臣因以此進戒，其諸協忠事君者哉？昔成王親政，周公欲其知恤也，故率羣臣而贊之曰：「嗣王臨御之初，正任賢圖治之際，爾諸臣皆有尊君之義，則亦皆有忠君之心者也。其尚拜手以致敬，稽首以成禮，而告吾嗣天子王焉。凡
translation_en:
…would have been presented; how then could one hope for such reverent caution and demanding of what is difficult as this? Therefore it is said: "When the ruler is sage, the ministers are forthright."

"[Do you] bow with hands together and bow your heads to the ground, and make announcement to the succeeding Son of Heaven, the King!" Thereupon they all admonished the King, saying: "Among the King's personal attendants are the regular senior advisors (changbo), the regular administrative commissioners (changren), the legal officers (zhunren), thekeepers of the robes (zhuiyi), and the tiger braves (huben)."

Gongyu Lide 公羽立德.
Associate Examiner Instructor Zhai 翟 comments: Able to bring out the meaning of the Duke of Zhou leading his subordinates to present admonitions; this is someone who cherishes the aspiration to bring his ruler to perfection. Record it.
Associate Examiner Professor Zhang 張 comments: The meaning of the Zhou ministers advising their ruler on employing men is implicit, gentle, and compliant, and this composition captures it. A fine scholar!
Examiner Professor Wan 萬 comments: Classically elegant.
Examiner Professor Wu 吳 comments: Concise and archaic in style.

The great minister leads the ministers in exhausting their loyalty, and the assembled ministers consequently look to the ruler to employ the right men. Extreme indeed is the need for caution in employing the ministers who attend the ruler closely! When the great minister inspires the assembled ministers to exhaust their loyalty, and the assembled ministers consequently present this admonition, are they not uniting in loyalty to serve their ruler? In antiquity, when King Cheng assumed personal rule, the Duke of Zhou wished him to know solicitous care, so he led the assembled ministers and assisted them, saying: "At the beginning of the succeeding King's personal reign, it is precisely the moment to employ the worthy and plan for good governance. All you ministers share the duty of honoring the ruler, and thus all possess hearts loyal to the ruler. May you bow your hands together to show reverence, bow your heads to the ground to complete the ritual, and make announcement to our succeeding Son of Heaven, the King. Whatever…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可以翊贊王猷而奉天之道者莫不備舉之可
也凡可以輔養君德而答民之望者莫不畢柬
之可也是周公方示之意而羣臣則實協其心
者用是咸進戒於王曰惟王所與圖茲治理者
寔惟左右之臣哉以三事之官言之有子民之
常伯焉有理事之常任焉有司法之準人焉職
雖不同要皆表正百僚以左右乎王政者也以
侍御之官言之有掌服器之綴衣焉有執射御
之虎賁焉任雖不一要皆統率僕從以左右乎
===
王躬者也於此而得其人則或爲之翊贊或爲
之輔養而所以奉天之道答民之望者咸舉之
矣王其慎任之哉吁是可以觀周臣協心之義
矣雖然左右之臣固所均重而近臣于王爲親
尤當慎其選者蓋親則易狎尊則易疎使不以
正人處之則浸漬眩惑君心日移而大臣日遠
矣此周公所爲深致意也歟
詩
受天之祜四方來賀於萬斯年不遐有佐
punctuated:
可以翊贊王猷而奉天之道者，莫不備舉之可也；凡可以輔養君德而答民之望者，莫不畢柬之可也。」是周公方示之意，而羣臣則實協其心者，用是咸進戒於王曰：「惟王所與圖茲治理者，寔惟左右之臣哉！以三事之官言之：有子民之常伯焉，有理事之常任焉，有司法之準人焉。職雖不同，要皆表正百僚以左右乎王政者也。以侍御之官言之：有掌服器之綴衣焉，有執射御之虎賁焉。任雖不一，要皆統率僕從以左右乎王躬者也。於此而得其人，則或爲之翊贊，或爲之輔養，而所以奉天之道、答民之望者咸舉之矣。王其慎任之哉！」吁，是可以觀周臣協心之義矣。雖然，左右之臣固所均重，而近臣于王爲親，尤當慎其選者。蓋親則易狎，尊則易疎；使不以正人處之，則浸漬眩惑，君心日移而大臣日遠矣。此周公所爲深致意也歟！
詩
「受天之祜，四方來賀。於萬斯年，不遐有佐。」
translation_en:
… can assist the royal plans and uphold the Way of Heaven should all be fully presented; whatever can nurture the sovereign’s virtue and answer the hopes of the people should all be exhaustively set forth [?]." Just as the Duke of Zhou indicated this intention, the assembled ministers truly shared his heart, and consequently they all advanced their admonition to the King, saying: "Those with whom Your Majesty plans this governance are indeed the ministers at your left and right! Speaking of the officials of the Three Affairs: there are the High Pastors (changbo) who care for the people as their children, the High Administrators (changren) who manage affairs, and the Men of Law (zhunren) who administer justice. Though their duties differ, in essence they all stand as models to rectify the hundred officials and thereby assist the royal government. Speaking of the officials in personal attendance: there are the Keepers of the Robes (zhuiyi) who are in charge of garments and implements, and the Tiger Braves (huben) who practice archery and charioteering. Though their responsibilities are not the same, in essence they all lead the attendants and retinue to wait upon the King's person. If the right men are obtained for these posts, then some will assist his plans and others will nurture his virtue, and the means to uphold the Way of Heaven and answer the hopes of the people will all be realized. May Your Majesty be cautious in appointing them!" Ah, from this one can observe the righteousness of the Zhou ministers in uniting their hearts! Even so, while the ministers at the left and right are certainly of equal importance, the close attendants are intimate with the King, and their selection must be made with special caution. For intimacy easily breeds familiarity, while exaltedness easily leads to estrangement; if upright men are not placed in these positions, then through gradual saturation and delusion, the ruler’s mind will shift day by day and the great ministers will become ever more distant. Is this not what the Duke of Zhou so deeply took to heart?

Book of Odes (Shi):
"He receives the blessings of Heaven, and from the four quarters they come to offer congratulations. For ten thousand years, will there not be helpers from afar?"

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
馮應鳳
同考試官教諭黃批天與則人歸自是一理子
獨能敷張而揚厲之可以爲人君法祖之勸矣
同考試官教授顧批不遐有佐卽萬年來賀之
人心此作發揮明盡宜錄以式
考試官教授萬批溫潤無瑕
考試官教授吳批精確
後王得天以得人而永賴其助焉蓋天之所與
人必歸之也而王室之佐不永有賴哉此美武
===
王而作也以爲大哉武王之孝得天得人之本
也能繩其祖武者何如哉蓋人心視天命以爲
從違而國運視人心以爲隆替夫旣受天之祜
矣由是仰一人之有慶合萬國而朝宗其雝雝
以有來者若與帝心之簡在而協應矣覩世德
之重光率四方而來賀其肅肅而至止者若與
天意之默佑而交孚矣夫然則王室所賴以爲
佐助者豈特今日爲然哉冠裳萃則屏翰有託
而百世懋贊襄之烈玉帛同則藩宣有寄而萬
punctuated:
馮應鳳
同考試官教諭黃批：「天與則人歸，自是一理。子獨能敷張而揚厲之，可以爲人君法祖之勸矣。」
同考試官教授顧批：「『不遐有佐』，卽『萬年來賀』之人心。此作發揮明盡，宜錄以式。」
考試官教授萬批：「溫潤無瑕。」
考試官教授吳批：「精確。」
後王得天以得人，而永賴其助焉。蓋天之所與，人必歸之也，而王室之佐，不永有賴哉？此美武王而作也。以爲大哉武王之孝，得天得人之本也，能繩其祖武者何如哉？蓋人心視天命以爲從違，而國運視人心以爲隆替。夫旣受天之祜矣，由是仰一人之有慶，合萬國而朝宗，其雝雝以有來者，若與帝心之簡在而協應矣；覩世德之重光，率四方而來賀，其肅肅而至止者，若與天意之默佑而交孚矣。夫然，則王室所賴以爲佐助者，豈特今日爲然哉？冠裳萃則屏翰有託，而百世懋贊襄之烈；玉帛同則藩宣有寄，而萬
translation_en:
Feng Yingfeng 馮應鳳
Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang 黃 comments: "When Heaven grants its favor, the people give their allegiance—this is naturally a single principle. You alone have been able to expand upon and exalt this theme; it can serve as an exhortation for a ruler to model himself on his ancestors."
Associate Examiner and Professor Gu 顧 comments: "'Is there not a distant helper?' refers precisely to the hearts of the people who come to offer congratulations for ten thousand years. This composition expounds the meaning clearly and thoroughly; it ought to be recorded as a model."
Examiner and Professor Wan 萬 comments: "Warm, lustrous, and flawless."
Examiner and Professor Wu 吳 comments: "Precise and accurate."

Later kings win the favor of Heaven and thereby win the allegiance of the people, forever relying upon their assistance. For where Heaven bestows its favor, the people will surely turn in allegiance; will the royal house not then forever have helpers upon whom to rely? This ode was composed in praise of King Wu 武王. It holds that great indeed was the filial piety of King Wu—the very foundation for winning both Heaven and the people! What happens when one is able to follow in the footsteps of one's ancestors? For the hearts of the people look to the Mandate of Heaven in deciding whether to follow or turn away, and the destiny of the state depends upon the hearts of the people for its rise or decline. Now, once one has received the blessing of Heaven, all thereupon look up to the felicity of the One Man, uniting the myriad states to pay court as rivers flow to the sea; those who come in harmonious concord seem to act in concerted response to the selection residing in the mind of the Supreme Lord. Beholding the renewed brilliance of hereditary virtue, they lead the four quarters to come and offer congratulations; those who arrive in reverent solemnity seem to be in mutual accord with the silent protection of Heaven's will. Since this is so, how could those upon whom the royal house relies for assistance be limited merely to the present day? Where caps and robes gather, the protective screens and bulwarks have those to whom they can be entrusted, and for a hundred generations they will diligently advance the merit of assisting in governance; where jades and silks assemble in uniformity, the frontier defenses and royal proclamations have those in whom they can be vested, and for ten thousand…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
年資匡弼之功國運無疆也則翼國之運者亦
無疆豐鎬之基相與培之而益固視諸四友之
臣所以賛文王之耿光者不其愈推而愈遠耶
王祚無窮也則輔王之祚者亦無窮郟鄏之鼎
相與保之而益重視諸十亂之臣所以相武王
之大烈者不其彌久而彌昌耶吁此固後王繩
武之效而實武王達孝之應也永言孝思其裕
後也爲何如哉抑武王之孝武王之敬爲之也
彼大統旣集天與人歸敬義執競之心何嘗一
===
日懈哉觀其貽厥孫謀以燕翼子雖繼世之後
猶且廑於念慮也噫使周之子孫能世守焉則
雖至今存可也惜乎以此爲訓猶有謂祖宗不
足法者
昊天有成命二后受之成王不敢康夙夜
基命宥密
張潘
同考試官敎諭黃批成王心不敢康惟知積德
基命此作根極心源蓋知祈天永命之要者
punctuated:
年資匡弼之功。國運無疆也，則翼國之運者亦無疆，豐鎬之基，相與培之而益固，視諸四友之臣所以賛文王之耿光者，不其愈推而愈遠耶？王祚無窮也，則輔王之祚者亦無窮，郟鄏之鼎，相與保之而益重，視諸十亂之臣所以相武王之大烈者，不其彌久而彌昌耶？吁！此固後王繩武之效，而實武王達孝之應也。「永言孝思」，其裕後也爲何如哉！抑武王之孝，武王之敬爲之也。彼大統旣集，天與人歸，敬義執競之心，何嘗一日懈哉？觀其「貽厥孫謀，以燕翼子」，雖繼世之後，猶且廑於念慮也。噫！使周之子孫能世守焉，則雖至今存可也。惜乎以此爲訓，猶有謂祖宗不足法者。

昊天有成命，二后受之。成王不敢康，夙夜基命宥密。
張潘
同考試官敎諭黃批：成王心不敢康，惟知積德基命。此作根極心源，蓋知祈天永命之要者。
translation_en:
… ten thousand years they will supply the merit of rectifying and assisting. When the destiny of the state is boundless, those who support the destiny of the state are likewise boundless; the foundations at Feng and Hao are jointly nurtured by them and made ever more secure. Compared with the way the four companion-ministers assisted the bright glory of King Wen, is this not extended ever further as it goes on? When the royal line is endless, those who aid the royal line are likewise endless; the tripods at Jiaru are jointly preserved by them and made ever weightier. Compared with the way the ten governing ministers aided the great achievements of King Wu, is this not ever more flourishing the longer it endures? Ah! This is indeed the effect of later kings following in the footsteps of their ancestors, yet in reality it is the response to King Wu's far-reaching filial piety. "Forever thinking filial thoughts"—how great was the abundance it bequeathed to posterity! Moreover, King Wu's filial piety was brought about by King Wu's reverence. Once the great succession had been gathered in, and Heaven had granted it and men had turned to him, when did his mind of reverence, righteousness, and unyielding vigor ever slacken for a single day? Seeing how he "bequeathed his plans to his grandsons, in order to give peace and support to his sons," even what would come after the succession of generations remained an object of his anxious concern. Alas! Had the descendants of Zhou been able to guard this from generation to generation, it might well have survived even down to the present day. How regrettable that even with such a precept as this, there were still those who said that the ancestors were not worth emulating!

"August Heaven has a determinate Mandate, which the two sovereigns received. King Cheng did not dare to rest in ease; morning and night he laid the foundation of the Mandate in deep and silent virtue."
Zhang Pan 張潘

Associate Examiner Instructor Huang 黃 comments: King Cheng in his heart did not dare to rest in ease, knowing only to accumulate virtue and lay the foundation of the Mandate. This essay traces things back to the very source of the mind; indeed, the author understands the essential point of praying to Heaven for an enduring Mandate.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
同考試官教授顧批文武以德受命成王以德
繼之子能悉其蘊矣錄之
考試官教授萬批莊重典雅
考試官教授吳批純粹
詩人頌賢王本其受命之自而及其凝命之德
焉蓋德者命之本也二后受之於前而成王凝
之於後其一德之相承者哉此祀成王之詩也
意謂一代王業固貴乎有以開其始猶貴乎有
以衍其傳善作而善承之吾玆有感於成王矣
===
何則天監有周簡在已非一日而二后明德昭
受又有其基維新之成命文王之敬止者受之
也臨汝之成命武王之敬勝者受之也使嗣其
統而不嗣其德不幾於墜厥命耶惟我成王上
焉思天命之靡常不敢以逸豫焉也自夙而夜
積德以爲迂續天休之本者愈久而愈純下焉
念先德之當紹不敢以康寧處也自夜而夙積
德以爲祈承帝眷之地者愈養而愈盛見其宥
焉而弘以深也爲溥博爲淵泉充極乎此心之
punctuated:
同考試官教授顧批：「文武以德受命，成王以德繼之，子能悉其蘊矣，錄之。」
考試官教授萬批：「莊重典雅。」
考試官教授吳批：「純粹。」

詩人頌賢王，本其受命之自，而及其凝命之德焉。蓋德者，命之本也。二后受之於前，而成王凝之於後，其一德之相承者哉！此祀成王之詩也，意謂一代王業，固貴乎有以開其始，猶貴乎有以衍其傳。善作而善承之，吾玆有感於成王矣。何則？天監有周，簡在已非一日，而二后明德，昭受又有其基。維新之成命，文王之敬止者受之也；臨汝之成命，武王之敬勝者受之也。使嗣其統而不嗣其德，不幾於墜厥命耶？惟我成王，上焉思天命之靡常，不敢以逸豫焉也，自夙而夜，積德以爲迂續天休之本者，愈久而愈純；下焉念先德之當紹，不敢以康寧處也，自夜而夙，積德以爲祈承帝眷之地者，愈養而愈盛。見其宥焉而弘以深也，爲溥博，爲淵泉，充極乎此心之
translation_en:
Associate Examiner Instructor Gu comments: "Kings Wen and Wu received the Mandate through virtue, and King Cheng succeeded to it through virtue. You have fully grasped its profound meaning; let it be recorded for publication."
Examiner Instructor Wan comments: "Dignified and classical."
Examiner Instructor Wu comments: "Pure and unadulterated."

When the poet praised the worthy king, he traced the origin of how the Mandate was received and extended to the virtue by which the Mandate was consolidated. For virtue is the foundation of the Mandate. The two sovereigns received it beforehand, and King Cheng consolidated it afterward—was this not the transmission of a single virtue? This is an ode for sacrificing to King Cheng. Its meaning is that while the royal enterprise of an era certainly values having that by which its beginning is opened, it even more values having that by which its transmission is extended. In skillfully initiating and skillfully continuing it, I am here deeply moved by King Cheng. Why is this? Heaven surveyed the House of Zhou; its selection had already been in mind for more than a single day, and through the illustrious virtue of the two sovereigns, its glorious reception also had its foundation. The determinate Mandate of renewal was received by King Wen's resting in reverence; the determinate Mandate of "God is with you" was received by King Wu's reverence prevailing. Had one succeeded to their lineage without succeeding to their virtue, would he not have come close to letting their Mandate fall? Only our King Cheng, looking above, pondered the inconstancy of Heaven's Mandate and dared not indulge in ease and pleasure; from morning to night, he accumulated virtue as the foundation for welcoming and continuing [reading 迓 for 迂] the blessings of Heaven, becoming ever more pure the longer it went on. Looking below, he remembered that the virtue of his predecessors ought to be continued and dared not dwell in tranquil repose; from night to morning, he accumulated virtue as the ground for praying for and receiving the favor of the Supreme Lord, becoming ever more flourishing the more it was nourished. One sees how magnanimous it was—broad and deep—being all-pervading and an abyssal spring, filling to the utmost the… of this mind…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
量廓乎萬善之不遺矣見其密焉而靜以密也
爲沉潛爲貞固全盡乎此心之體凝然萬幾之
不露矣至是則所存者無非二后之心所積者
無非二后之德成王所以祈天永命不有道哉
抑成王之成德未易言也甞觀無逸召誥諸篇
周召二公勉之以敬德者不一而足及觀訪落
敬之諸詩所以求益於其臣者又屢致意焉君
臣交勉上下相成成王所以能爲有周令主有
由然矣守成業者尚念茲哉
===
春秋
春王正月城楚丘〔僖公二年〕五月癸丑公
會晋侯齊侯宋公蔡侯鄭伯衞子莒子
盟於踐土〔僖公二十有八年〕
劉志在
同考試官教諭秦批春秋大義在尊王此作發
揮殆盡可以式矣
考試官教授萬批詞嚴義正
考試官教授吳批雅而健
punctuated:
量，廓乎萬善之不遺矣；見其密焉而靜以密也，爲沉潛，爲貞固，全盡乎此心之體，凝然萬幾之不露矣。至是，則所存者無非二后之心，所積者無非二后之德，成王所以祈天永命，不有道哉？抑成王之成德，未易言也。甞觀《無逸》、《召誥》諸篇，周、召二公勉之以敬德者，不一而足；及觀《訪落》、《敬之》諸詩，所以求益於其臣者，又屢致意焉。君臣交勉，上下相成，成王所以能爲有周令主，有由然矣。守成業者，尚念茲哉！

《春秋》
「春，王正月，城楚丘。」〔僖公二年〕「五月，癸丑，公會晋侯、齊侯、宋公、蔡侯、鄭伯、衞子、莒子，盟於踐土。」〔僖公二十有八年〕
劉志在
同考試官教諭秦批：春秋大義在尊王，此作發揮殆盡，可以式矣。
考試官教授萬批：詞嚴義正。
考試官教授吳批：雅而健。
translation_en:
…capacity of this mind, expansive so that not one of the myriad goods is left out; one sees it in its stillness, quiet and dense: it is submerged and deep, firm and steadfast, completely fulfilling the substance of this mind, concentrated so that not one of the myriad affairs is prematurely exposed. Having reached this point, what he preserved was nothing other than the minds of the two former kings, and what he accumulated was nothing other than the virtue of the two former kings. Did King Cheng not indeed have the Way by which to pray to Heaven for an enduring mandate?

Yet the completion of King Cheng's virtue is not easily spoken of. When we examine chapters such as "Against Luxurious Ease" (Wuyi) and the "Announcement of the Duke of Shao" (Shao gao), the ways in which the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao exhorted him to revere virtue were not limited to a single instance; and when we examine odes such as "Counsel at the Beginning of Rule" (Fangluo) and "Reverence" (Jingzhi), the ways in which he sought benefit from his ministers were likewise repeatedly expressed with earnest intent. Sovereign and ministers mutually exhorted one another, and superior and inferior brought one another to completion—there was truly a reason why King Cheng was able to become an admirable ruler of the Zhou! May those who guard an established patrimony ever bear this in mind!

Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu)

"In spring, in the King's first month, they walled Chuqiu." 〔Second year of Duke Xi〕 "In the fifth month, on the guichou day, the Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Marquis of Qi, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Cai, the Earl of Zheng, the Viscount of Wei, and the Viscount of Ju, and made a covenant at Jiantu." 〔Twenty-eighth year of Duke Xi〕

By Liu Zhizai 劉志在.

Associate Examiner, Instructor (jiaoyu) Qin comments: The great principle of the Spring and Autumn Annals lies in honoring the King; this composition has expounded it almost exhaustively and can serve as a model.
Examiner, Professor (jiaoshou) Wan comments: The diction is stern and the principle upright.
Examiner, Professor Wu comments: Refined and vigorous.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
春秋明王法故於擅封建者而均貶之焉此見
封國建侯天子之大權也桓文以諸侯擅之春
秋能無貶乎昔楚丘城而衛人忘亡與桓公者
曰庶幾繼絶之義矣而春秋畧諸侯以示貶者
何曰分土惟三惟天子得以行之非諸侯所可
干也衛人迫狄東徙渡河楚丘豈非當封者乎
使桓也請于王而封之則尊主恤鄰是爲義之
大者顧乃徼惠於康叔市恩於文公甲士乘馬
莫非自齊歸之則以諸侯而封諸侯矣衛雖無
===
國而有國齊則有王而無王其失不但攘善也
故春秋不書桓公而微其事若曰衛之國非桓
公可得而封也踐土會而叔武與盟與文公者
曰庶幾擇賢之義矣而春秋子衛武以示貶者
何曰列爵惟五惟天子得以行之非諸侯所可
亂也衛成失國南向卽楚叔武豈其當立者乎
使文也請于王而立之報怨行私已爲譎之大
者况乃奉以元晅列之載書土宇人民儼若由
晉授之則以諸侯而立諸侯矣武旣內無所承
punctuated: 《春秋》明王法，故於擅封建者而均貶之焉。此見封國建侯，天子之大權也，桓、文以諸侯擅之，《春秋》能無貶乎？昔楚丘城而衛人忘亡，與桓公者曰：「庶幾繼絶之義矣！」而《春秋》畧諸侯以示貶者，何？曰：「分土惟三」，惟天子得以行之，非諸侯所可干也。衛人迫狄，東徙渡河，楚丘豈非當封者乎？使桓也請于王而封之，則尊主恤鄰，是爲義之大者；顧乃徼惠於康叔，市恩於文公，甲士、乘馬，莫非自齊歸之，則以諸侯而封諸侯矣。衛雖無國而有國，齊則有王而無王，其失不但攘善也。故《春秋》不書桓公而微其事，若曰：衛之國，非桓公可得而封也。踐土會而叔武與盟，與文公者曰：「庶幾擇賢之義矣！」而《春秋》「子」衛武以示貶者，何？曰：「列爵惟五」，惟天子得以行之，非諸侯所可亂也。衛成失國，南向卽楚，叔武豈其當立者乎？使文也請于王而立之，報怨行私，已爲譎之大者；况乃奉以元晅，列之載書，土宇、人民，儼若由晉授之，則以諸侯而立諸侯矣。武旣內無所承，
translation_en:
The Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) clarifies the kingly law, and therefore equally censures those who usurp the power to enfeoff and establish rulers. This shows that enfeoffing states and establishing feudal lords is the great prerogative of the Son of Heaven; when Duke Huan of Qi and Duke Wen of Jin usurped it as feudal lords, how could the Spring and Autumn Annals refrain from censuring them?

In the past, when Chuqiu was walled, the people of Wei forgot the ruin of their state. Those who approved of Duke Huan said, "This comes close to the righteous principle of restoring extinguished states!" Why then did the Spring and Autumn Annals omit the feudal lords in order to show censure? It is because "apportioning lands into three grades" is something only the Son of Heaven may carry out, not something feudal lords may encroach upon. When the people of Wei were pressed by the Di tribes and migrated east across the Yellow River, was not Chuqiu indeed worthy of being enfeoffed? Had Huan petitioned the King to enfeoff them, then honoring the sovereign and showing compassion for a neighbor would have been the greatest of righteous acts. Instead, he sought to claim credit for bestowing favor upon Kangshu's line and peddled grace to Duke Wen of Wei; armored soldiers and teams of horses were all sent from Qi, which amounted to one feudal lord enfeoffing another feudal lord. Although Wei went from having no state to having a state, Qi acted as though there were no King even while a King existed; his fault was not merely appropriating credit for a good deed. Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals does not record Duke Huan and obscures the affair, as if to say: the state of Wei was not something Duke Huan was entitled to enfeoff.

When the assembly at Jiantu took place and Shuwu participated in the covenant, those who approved of Duke Wen of Jin said, "This comes close to the righteous principle of selecting the worthy!" Why then did the Spring and Autumn Annals refer to Shuwu of Wei as "Viscount" (zi) in order to show censure? It is because "arranging noble ranks into five orders" is something only the Son of Heaven may carry out, not something feudal lords may throw into disorder. When Duke Cheng of Wei lost his state and headed south to align with Chu, was Shuwu indeed the one who ought to have been established? Even had Wen petitioned the King to establish him, avenging a personal grievance and acting out of private interest would already have been the greatest of duplicitous acts. How much worse when he had him upheld by Yuan Xuan and listed in the covenant document, so that territory and populace appeared as though conferred by Jin—which amounted to one feudal lord establishing another feudal lord! Since Shuwu had no mandate of succession from within,…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
文則上無所稟其失不但脩怨也故春秋特稱
衛子而異其詞若曰衛之君非文公可得而立
也吁此義明而可以肅侯度正王法命討賞罰
出於一矣抑是役也其事之無王不必言而其
心則尤有可責者何也使桓能以伐山戎者伐
狄則衛不滅矣何事於城而斂盂不拒則衛無
恙也武可無立矣惟其養亂爲心鑿智不廣故
至此噫義士薄其德聖門羞其功有由然哉
鄭公孫舍之帥師侵宋公會晉侯宋公
===
衛侯曹伯齊世子光莒子邾子滕子薛
伯杞伯小邾子伐鄭秋七月己未同
盟于亳城北公至自伐鄭楚子鄭
伯伐宋公會晉侯宋公衛侯曹伯齊
世子光莒子邾子滕子薛伯杞伯小邾
子伐鄭會于蕭魚〔俱襄公十有一年〕
王士崧
同考試官敎諭秦批鄭人失信由不知義篇中
識得此意
punctuated:
文則上無所稟，其失不但脩怨也。故《春秋》特稱「衛子」而異其詞，若曰：衛之君，非文公可得而立也。吁！此義明，而可以肅侯度、正王法，命討賞罰出於一矣。抑是役也，其事之無王不必言，而其心則尤有可責者，何也？使桓能以伐山戎者伐狄，則衛不滅矣，何事於城？而斂盂不拒，則衛無恙也，武可無立矣。惟其養亂爲心，鑿智不廣，故至此。噫！義士薄其德，聖門羞其功，有由然哉！
鄭公孫舍之帥師侵宋。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。秋七月己未，同盟于亳城北。公至自伐鄭。楚子、鄭伯伐宋。公會晉侯、宋公、衛侯、曹伯、齊世子光、莒子、邾子、滕子、薛伯、杞伯、小邾子伐鄭。會于蕭魚。〔俱襄公十有一年〕
王士崧
同考試官敎諭秦批：鄭人失信，由不知義，篇中識得此意。
translation_en:
… while Duke Wen had received no mandate from above; his fault was not merely nursing a personal grievance. Therefore the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) pointedly refers to him as "the Viscount of Wei" (Wei zi), altering its wording as if to say: the ruler of Wei is not someone whom Duke Wen may take it upon himself to install. Ah! Once this principle is made clear, the standards for the feudal lords can be enforced, the King's law rectified, and commands, punitive expeditions, rewards, and punishments will all issue from a single source. Moreover, in these campaigns, that their actions disregarded the King goes without saying, yet their underlying motives are even more open to censure—why is this? Had Duke Huan used the strength with which he attacked the Mountain Rong to attack the Di tribes instead, Wei would not have been destroyed—what need would there have been to wall a new capital for it? And had Duke Wen not rebuffed Wei at the covenant of Lianyu, Wei would have remained unharmed, and Shuwu would never have needed to be installed. It was only because they harbored the nurturing of disorder in their hearts, and their contrived cleverness was narrow in scope, that things came to this pass. Alas! That righteous gentlemen slighted their virtue and the disciples of the Sage were ashamed to speak of their achievements was certainly not without reason!

"Gongsun Shezhi of Zheng led a force to make an incursion into Song. The Duke [of Lu] met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu to attack Zheng. In autumn, in the seventh month, on the day jiwei, they made a covenant together north of Bocheng. The Duke arrived back from the attack on Zheng. The Viscount of Chu and the Earl of Zheng attacked Song. The Duke met the Marquis of Jin, the Duke of Song, the Marquis of Wei, the Earl of Cao, Heir Apparent Guang of Qi, the Viscount of Ju, the Viscount of Zhu, the Viscount of Teng, the Earl of Xue, the Earl of Qi, and the Viscount of Little Zhu to attack Zheng. They met at Xiaoyu." [All from the eleventh year of Duke Xiang.]

Wang Shisong 王士崧

Comment by Associate Examiner and County Director of Studies Qin: The people of Zheng broke faith because they did not understand righteousness; this essay grasps this essential point.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
考試官敎授萬批〔說題意瑩徹〕
考試官敎授吳批〔渾融〕
春秋詳貳國用謀從伯之事所以著其失也夫
小所以事大信也鄭之於晉非信是杖而顧用
謀以致之其失也大矣此春秋詳紀兵信以罪
之也在昔鄭國困於晉楚之交而圖爲反覆之
策始命舍之以侵宋晉也北林致武則服而同
盟焉尋復從楚以伐宋晉也東門觀兵則又服
而請會焉君子曰鄭之不善爲謀也一至此哉
===
夫以蕞爾小國而介乎大國之間其所可杖者
信而已其所當從者義而已夫何輕兵召兵玩
邦交而曾不之忌也尋盟尋叛慢鬼神而曾不
之恤也徒曰與宋爲惡諸侯必至吾且與之盟
矣而要其與晉之時未忘從楚之念不然楚狄
國不可一日向者也何必待其屈而後絕之乎
徒曰晉能驟來楚將不能吾乃固與晉矣而要
其從楚之時亦未堅與晉之心不然晉伯主不
可一日背者也何必待其疾而後與之乎雖伯
punctuated:
考試官敎授萬批：〔說題意瑩徹。〕
考試官敎授吳批：〔渾融。〕
《春秋》詳貳國用謀從伯之事，所以著其失也。夫小所以事大，信也。鄭之於晉，非信是杖，而顧用謀以致之，其失也大矣。此《春秋》詳紀兵信以罪之也。在昔鄭國困於晉、楚之交，而圖爲反覆之策。始命舍之以侵宋，晉也北林致武，則服而同盟焉；尋復從楚以伐宋，晉也東門觀兵，則又服而請會焉。君子曰：鄭之不善爲謀也，一至此哉！夫以蕞爾小國，而介乎大國之間，其所可杖者，信而已；其所當從者，義而已。夫何輕兵召兵，玩邦交而曾不之忌也？尋盟尋叛，慢鬼神而曾不之恤也？徒曰：「與宋爲惡，諸侯必至，吾且與之盟矣。」而要其與晉之時，未忘從楚之念。不然，楚，狄國，不可一日向者也，何必待其屈而後絕之乎？徒曰：「晉能驟來，楚將不能，吾乃固與晉矣。」而要其從楚之時，亦未堅與晉之心。不然，晉，伯主，不可一日背者也，何必待其疾而後與之乎？雖伯
translation_en:
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Wan's comment: [Explicates the meaning of the theme with crystal clarity.]
Examiner and Prefectural Director of Studies Wu's comment: [Harmonious and well-integrated.]
When the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records in detail the events of a vacillating state using calculating schemes in following the hegemon, it is in order to make manifest its fault. Now, that by which a small state serves a great one is good faith. In Zheng's dealings with Jin, it did not rely on good faith, but instead used calculating schemes to bring it about; its fault was great indeed. This is why the Spring and Autumn Annals records in detail the military expeditions and covenants in order to condemn it. In the past, the state of Zheng was distressed by its position between Jin and Chu, and plotted a policy of repeated vacillation. At first, it ordered Shezhi to invade Song; when Jin displayed its military might at Beilin, Zheng submitted and joined in a covenant. Soon after, it again followed Chu to attack Song; when Jin made a show of force at the Eastern Gate (Dongmen), Zheng submitted once more and requested a meeting. The gentleman says: How could Zheng's poorness at making plans reach such an extreme as this! Now, as a tiny state wedged between great powers, that upon which it could rely was good faith alone; that which it ought to have followed was righteousness alone. Why, then, did it lightly launch troops and provoke military action, trifling with interstate relations without the slightest scruple? Why did it no sooner make a covenant than rebel against it, showing contempt for the spirits and gods without the slightest concern? It merely said: "If we commit hostilities against Song, the feudal lords will certainly arrive, and we shall then make a covenant with them." Yet in essence, even at the time it allied with Jin, it had not forgotten the thought of following Chu. Otherwise, since Chu was a barbarian state toward which one should not turn for even a single day, why must Zheng wait until Chu was exhausted before breaking with it? And it merely said: "If Jin can come repeatedly in haste, Chu will be unable to do so, and we shall then firmly ally with Jin." Yet in essence, at the time it followed Chu, it had likewise not firmed up its resolve to ally with Jin. Otherwise, since Jin was the hegemonic lord against whom one should not turn one's back for even a single day, why must Zheng wait until Jin pressed it hard before allying with it? Even though Bo…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
騑行成終致良霄之執悼公推誠永肩蕭魚之
好而使中國勞於三駕鄭人疲於五會繄誰為
之故春秋詳紀其兵信之迹若曰與人之不一
謀國之不臧鄭之為鄭有以哉雖然鄭固失矣
而晉之善則有不容泯者當鄭人反覆之時而
知武子方以要盟為非禮以脩德息師為可恃
視子展何如哉故其始也要之以五會而不信
及其成也延之以貳紀而不叛罃之謀也悼亦
善用謀者哉
===
禮記
故聖人作則必以天地為本以陰陽為端
以四時為柄以日星為紀月以為量鬼
神以為徒五行以為質禮義以為器人
情以為田四靈以為畜
葉遵
考試官敎授萬批是作發明聖人作則感通
之妙意融詞徹可錄
考試官敎授吳批冲和明雅
punctuated:
騑行成，終致良霄之執，悼公推誠，永肩蕭魚之好，而使中國勞於三駕，鄭人疲於五會，繄誰為之？故《春秋》詳紀其兵信之迹，若曰：與人之不一，謀國之不臧，鄭之為鄭，有以哉！雖然，鄭固失矣，而晉之善則有不容泯者。當鄭人反覆之時，而知武子方以要盟為非禮，以脩德息師為可恃，視子展何如哉！故其始也，要之以五會而不信；及其成也，延之以貳紀而不叛。罃之謀也，悼亦善用謀者哉！
《禮記》
「故聖人作則，必以天地為本，以陰陽為端，以四時為柄，以日星為紀，月以為量，鬼神以為徒，五行以為質，禮義以為器，人情以為田，四靈以為畜。」
葉遵
考試官敎授萬批：是作發明聖人作則感通之妙，意融詞徹，可錄。
考試官敎授吳批：冲和明雅。
translation_en:
… [Bo]fei (Zisi) sought peace, finally leading to the detention of Liang Xiao, and Duke Dao of Jin extended his sincerity, permanently sustaining the amity of the meeting at Xiaoyu; yet who was it that caused the Central States to toil through three expeditions and the people of Zheng to be exhausted by five assemblies? Therefore, the Spring and Autumn Annals (Chunqiu) records in detail the traces of their military actions and oaths of good faith, as if to say: "Inconstancy in allying with others and poor counsel in governing the state—that Zheng was such as it was had its reasons indeed!" Even so, Zheng was certainly at fault, yet the merits of Jin cannot be obscured. At the time when the people of Zheng were vacillating, Zhi Wuzi (Zhi Ying) regarded coerced covenants as contrary to ritual propriety, and held that cultivating virtue and resting the troops could be relied upon—how does he compare with Zizhan! Thus, in the beginning, even when bound by five assemblies, Zheng did not keep faith; but once peace was achieved, for twenty-four years it did not rebel. Such was the counsel of Ying (Zhi Ying), and Duke Dao was indeed one who knew how to make good use of counsel!

Record of Rites (Liji)
"Therefore, when the sage establishes rules, he must take Heaven and Earth as the foundation, yin and yang as the clue, the four seasons as the handle, the sun and stars as the regulator, the moon as the measure, ghosts and spirits as the attendants, the Five Phases as the substance, ritual propriety and righteousness as the instruments, human feelings as the field, and the fournuminous creatures as the domestic animals."
Ye Zun
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Wan comments: This essay elucidates the wondrous resonance of the sage establishing rules; its ideas are harmonious and its diction penetrating—worthy of selection.
Examiner and Confucian Instructor Wu comments: Balanced, harmonious, clear, and elegant.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
記者著聖人之立極盡其道而獲其應焉甚矣
感應之理至神也聖人盡作則之道則其應不
有必然者哉記禮運者意謂聖人以一身為民
物之主則必以一心盡法制之詳是故其作則
於天下非以私智為也必本之于天而法其易
知者以為軌物之自本之于地而法其簡能者
以為經世之原分而為陰陽運而為四時皆變
通于天地者也則以之為考情之端為立事之
柄焉日星之昭布月之分限皆推行于天地者
===
也則以之為占候之準為程功之量焉鬼神天
地之良能固依之為徒矣而五行之周流於其
間者以之為質幹也禮義天地之常道固用之
為成器矣而人情之付畀於其內者治之如田
疇也夫如是將見德盛而化自神感通而應自
妙四靈非可常有之物也至是若為聖人之所
畜焉休徵協應殆相忘于天之高地之下而莫
知其所以然矣聖人道化之感如是信乎志一
動氣其理不可誣也甞觀道隆虞世而鳳儀于
punctuated: 記者著聖人之立極，盡其道而獲其應焉。甚矣，感應之理至神也！聖人盡作則之道，則其應不有必然者哉？記《禮運》者意謂：聖人以一身為民物之主，則必以一心盡法制之詳。是故其作則於天下，非以私智為也，必本之于天，而法其易知者以為軌物之自；本之于地，而法其簡能者以為經世之原。分而為陰陽，運而為四時，皆變通于天地者也，則以之為考情之端、為立事之柄焉；日星之昭布，月之分限，皆推行于天地者也，則以之為占候之準、為程功之量焉。鬼神，天地之良能，固依之為徒矣，而五行之周流於其間者，以之為質幹也；禮義，天地之常道，固用之為成器矣，而人情之付畀於其內者，治之如田疇也。夫如是，將見德盛而化自神，感通而應自妙。四靈，非可常有之物也，至是若為聖人之所畜焉。休徵協應，殆相忘于天之高、地之下，而莫知其所以然矣。聖人道化之感如是，信乎志一動氣，其理不可誣也。甞觀道隆虞世而鳳儀于
translation_en: The author of the Record sets forth how the sage establishes the supreme standard, fulfills its Way to the utmost, and thereby obtains its response. Profound indeed is the supreme marvel of the principle of stimulus and response! When the sage fulfills to the utmost the Way of establishing rules, is not the response he elicits a matter of certainty? The author of the "Evolution of Rites" (Liyun) in the Record meant to say: Since the sage in his single person acts as the lord of the people and all things, he must with his single mind exhaustively attend to the details of laws and institutions. Therefore, when he establishes rules for the world, he does not do so through private cleverness. He must ground them in Heaven, modeling himself on what is easy to know in it as the source for regulating things; and he must ground them in Earth, modeling himself on what is simple to accomplish in it as the origin for ordering the world. Divided into yin and yang, and revolving as the four seasons—all these are transformations and continuities within Heaven and Earth; thus he takes them as the starting points for examining the nature of things and the handles for establishing affairs. The bright array of the sun and stars, and the measured limits of the moon—all these are propelled across Heaven and Earth; thus he takes them as the standard for observing astronomical signs and the measure for assessing work accomplished. Ghosts and spirits, being the innate efficacy of Heaven and Earth, are naturally relied upon as his followers, while the Five Phases circulating among them are taken as the substantive framework. Ritual and righteousness, being the constant Way of Heaven and Earth, are naturally employed as finished vessels, while the human feelings endowed within them are cultivated like fertile fields. When it is like this, one will see that as virtue flourishes, transformation becomes naturally miraculous, and as stimulus penetrates, the response becomes naturally wondrous. The Four Numinous Creatures are not beings that can be constantly possessed, yet at this point it is as though they are domesticated by the sage. Auspicious signs respond in harmony, until all is nearly forgotten between the heights of Heaven and the depths of Earth, without anyone knowing how it comes to be so. Such is the resonance of the sage's moral transformation—truly, when the will is unified it moves the vital energy (qi), and this principle cannot be denied! One may observe how, when the Way flourished in the age of Yu [Shun], the phoenixes came with stately bearing to…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
廷化極成周而鳥鳴于岡天地效靈聖人無心
也若夫不求其作則之善而區區惟珍異之求
至有以一卉一物之異紀年致賀者噫何益哉
廉直勁正莊誠之音作而民肅敬寛裕肉
好順成和動之音作而民慈愛
邵夢弼
考試官教授萬批發揮民心愛敬婉切有味
迥異諸作
考試官教授吳批詳整明健
===
卽樂音之肅雍而可以知民心矣蓋樂音與民
心相爲感也觀音有肅雍之異而民之敬愛不
可知乎樂記之意蓋謂大哉樂乎肇端于一心
而感通于庶民者也故審音而可以知民矣彼
樂之作也自其介然有辨曰廉確然不回曰直
且勁正而無淫邪莊誠而無躁妄焉音不同莫
非一敬之發越也於是因知民之肅敬焉蓋以
敬心感者其聲直以廉理則然也故一傾聽之
餘而凡民心之爲嚴恪爲祗慎者已昭然于聲
punctuated:
廷，化極成周而鳥鳴于岡。天地效靈，聖人無心也。若夫不求其作則之善，而區區惟珍異之求，至有以一卉一物之異，紀年致賀者，噫，何益哉！

廉直勁正莊誠之音作，而民肅敬；寛裕肉好順成和動之音作，而民慈愛。
邵夢弼
考試官教授萬批：發揮民心愛敬，婉切有味，迥異諸作。
考試官教授吳批：詳整明健。

卽樂音之肅雍，而可以知民心矣。蓋樂音與民心相爲感也。觀音有肅雍之異，而民之敬愛不可知乎？《樂記》之意，蓋謂大哉樂乎！肇端于一心，而感通于庶民者也，故審音而可以知民矣。彼樂之作也，自其介然有辨曰廉，確然不回曰直，且勁正而無淫邪，莊誠而無躁妄焉。音不同，莫非一敬之發越也，於是因知民之肅敬焉。蓋以敬心感者，其聲直以廉，理則然也。故一傾聽之餘，而凡民心之爲嚴恪、爲祗慎者，已昭然于聲
translation_en:
… court, and when transforming influence reached its height in the Accomplished Zhou, birds sang on the mountain ridges. Heaven and Earth manifested their spiritual efficacy, yet the sages had no deliberate intention in it. As for those who do not seek the goodness of serving as the standard, but pettily seek only rare and strange things—even to the point of changing the reign title and offering congratulations on account of the anomaly of a single plant or a single creature—alas, what benefit is there in that!

"When tones that are sharp-edged, upright, vigorous, correct, grave, and sincere arise, the people become reverent and respectful; when tones that are宽generous, mellow, harmonious, accomplished, gentle, and moving arise, the people become kind and loving."
Shao Mengbi 邵夢弼
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wan's comment: It elaborates on the love and reverence in the people's hearts in a nuanced, fitting, and flavorful way, standing far apart from the other compositions.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wu's comment: Detailed, well-ordered, clear, and vigorous.

From the solemnity and harmony of musical tones, one can know the hearts of the people. For musical tones and the hearts of the people mutually move and respond to one another. Observing that tones have the distinction of solemnity and harmony, can one not know the reverence and love of the people? The meaning of the Record of Music (Yueji) is that great indeed is music! It originates in the single mind and moves and communicates with the multitude of the people; therefore, by examining the tones one can know the people. When that music arises: from its being distinctly discriminating, it is called "sharp-edged" (lian); from its being firmly unyielding, it is called "upright" (zhi); moreover, it is vigorous and correct without licentiousness or perversity, grave and sincere without rashness or falsehood. Though the tones differ, none is not the outward expression of a single reverence; thereupon, from this one knows the reverence and respectfulness of the people. For when moved by a mind of reverence, the sound is upright and sharp-edged; such is the principle of things. Therefore, upon listening attentively once, whatever in the people's hearts is sternly respectful and reverently cautious is already clearly manifest beyond the sound…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
氣之表矣奚必觀之于民而後知其肅敬耶自
其優柔不迫曰寛裕圓融不滯曰肉好且順成
而無拂逆和動而無乖戾焉音不同莫非一和
之形見也于是因知民之慈愛焉蓋以愛心感
者其聲和以柔理則然也故一傾聽之餘而凡
民心之爲慈良爲仁愛者已藹然于節奏之間
矣奚必驗之于民而後知其慈愛耶夫即音可
以知民之肅敬則以敬感民之道不可已矣即
音可以知民之慈愛則以愛感民之道不可已
===
矣此先王之所以必慎其所感也歟大抵聲音
之道寔與政通古今論盛治者莫過唐虞其樂
不可尚已而康衢之謠擊壤之歌油然愛敬之
風則至今可想見也亦惟堯舜之德有以感之
耳否則鄭衞之音何有于愛敬而亦奚取於樂
哉
第貳塲
論
宗社生靈長久之計
punctuated:
氣之表矣，奚必觀之于民而後知其肅敬耶？自其優柔不迫曰寛裕，圓融不滯曰肉好，且順成而無拂逆，和動而無乖戾焉，音不同，莫非一和之形見也，于是因知民之慈愛焉。蓋以愛心感者，其聲和以柔，理則然也。故一傾聽之餘，而凡民心之爲慈良、爲仁愛者，已藹然于節奏之間矣，奚必驗之于民而後知其慈愛耶？夫即音可以知民之肅敬，則以敬感民之道不可已矣；即音可以知民之慈愛，則以愛感民之道不可已矣。此先王之所以必慎其所感也歟！大抵聲音之道，寔與政通。古今論盛治者，莫過唐虞，其樂不可尚已。而康衢之謠、擊壤之歌，油然愛敬之風，則至今可想見也，亦惟堯舜之德有以感之耳。否則鄭衞之音，何有于愛敬，而亦奚取於樂哉？

第貳塲
論
宗社生靈長久之計
translation_en:
…manifest beyond the tones and vital breath! Why must one observe the people directly before knowing that they are solemn and reverent? When the music is gentle and unhurried, it is called expansive and generous; when it is well-rounded and unobstructed, it is called full and mellow; and when it furthermore brings things to completion smoothly without defiance, and stirs harmoniously without perversity—though the tones differ, none is anything other than the outward manifestation of a single harmony, and from this one consequently knows that the people are kind and affectionate. For when they are moved by a mind of affection, the sounds are harmonious and gentle; such is the principle of things. Therefore, the moment one lends an ear, all the kindness, goodness, and benevolent affection in the minds of the people are already warmly apparent within the rhythm and cadence! Why must one verify it among the people directly before knowing that they are kind and affectionate? Now, if from the tones one can know the solemn reverence of the people, then the way of moving the people through reverence must not be ceased; if from the tones one can know the kind affection of the people, then the way of moving the people through affection must not be ceased. Is this not why the former kings were always cautious about that by which they moved the people? In general, the way of sounds and tones is truly connected with governance. Past and present, in discussing eras of flourishing rule, none surpasses Tang and Yu [the ages of Yao and Shun], and their music could not be excelled. Yet in the ballads of the highroads and the songs of striking the clods, the spontaneous风 (ethos) of affection and reverence can still be envisioned even to this day; this too was simply because the virtue of Yao and Shun had the wherewithal to move them. Otherwise, what do the tones of Zheng and Wei have to do with affection and reverence, and what would there be to value in music?

Second Session
Discourse
A Plan for the Long-Term Enduring Security of the Ancestral Altars and the Living People

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
莫睿
同考試官教諭張批此作引周公輔養成王為
證似抱忠悃者錄之
同考試官教授伍批本忠愛之忱攄貤切之論
且格高調古佳士也
考試官教授萬批淵邃
考試官教授吳批懇切
夫人君之身所繫豈不重哉善計天下者有見
其重則所以輔養其德者不可以不密其功何
===
則天下之事知者能謀之力者能任之然非有
關君身則亦無益於治安之計事關君身忠者
能持之直者能諫之然無益於輔養成德則雖
日以布德捄過而久安長治之計亦未必盡出
於此也善計天下者不規規於用人行政之間
而唯致力於輔養君德之事至其所為輔養則
又不取必於論說之末而唯致密於涵育薰陶
之方廣其助於前後左右疑丞弼直之人而謹
其微於朝夕燕閒出入起居之際比其久也眾
punctuated:
莫睿
同考試官教諭張批：「此作引周公輔養成王為證，似抱忠悃者，錄之。」
同考試官教授伍批：「本忠愛之忱，攄貤切之論，且格高調古，佳士也。」
考試官教授萬批：「淵邃。」
考試官教授吳批：「懇切。」
夫人君之身，所繫豈不重哉？善計天下者，有見其重，則所以輔養其德者，不可以不密其功。何則？天下之事，知者能謀之，力者能任之；然非有關君身，則亦無益於治安之計。事關君身，忠者能持之，直者能諫之；然無益於輔養成德，則雖日以布德捄過，而久安長治之計，亦未必盡出於此也。善計天下者，不規規於用人行政之間，而唯致力於輔養君德之事。至其所為輔養，則又不取必於論說之末，而唯致密於涵育薰陶之方：廣其助於前後左右、疑丞弼直之人，而謹其微於朝夕燕閒、出入起居之際。比其久也，眾
translation_en:
Mo Rui 莫睿
Associate Examiner and Instructor Zhang 張 commented: "This essay cites the Duke of Zhou's (Zhougong 周公) assisting and cultivating of King Cheng (Chengwang 成王) as evidence. He seems to be one who harbors sincere loyalty; select him for inclusion."
Associate Examiner and Confucian School Director Wu 伍 commented: "Rooted in sincere loyalty and affection, he sets forth an expansive and earnest [?] discourse. Moreover, its structure is lofty and its tone antique—a fine scholar!"
Examiner and Confucian School Director Wan 萬 commented: "Profound and abstruse."
Examiner and Confucian School Director Wu 吳 commented: "Earnest and incisive."
Now, is not that which depends upon the person of the ruler of the utmost weight? Those who plan well for the empire, perceiving this weight, cannot fail to be meticulous in their efforts to assist and cultivate his virtue. Why is this? As for the affairs of the empire, the wise can plan them and the capable can shoulder them; yet if they do not pertain to the person of the ruler, they are of no benefit to plans for peace and order. When matters do pertain to the person of the ruler, the loyal can uphold them and the forthright can remonstrate over them; yet if this is of no benefit to assisting and cultivating his accomplished virtue, then even if one daily proclaims benevolence and remedies faults, the plan for enduring peace and lasting order will not necessarily issue wholly from this. Those who plan well for the empire do not busily confine themselves to the details of employing men and administering government, but devote their strength solely to the task of assisting and cultivating the ruler's virtue. As for how they carry out this assistance and cultivation, they do not insist upon relying on the superficialities of mere argumentation, but instead apply meticulous care to the methods of nurturing and edifying: broadening the assistance he receives from the men ahead and behind, to the left and right—the Grand Mentor, Grand Assistant, Grand Preceptor, and Grand Protector (Yi, Cheng, Bi, Zhi 疑丞弼直)—and guarding the subtle beginnings during his morning and evening hours of leisure, his goings out and comings in, his active and restful moments.
