title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
明良之盛敷陳芹曝之忱也愚雖非其人竊嘗
有所感焉夫自古帝王願治者莫不欲稽
古正學而啓沃則在於臣自古人臣凡願
忠者莫不欲開陳媺惡而聽納則在於君
君能受言不能必臣之審於進言蓋進言
難也論一事闢一說夫孰非進然一指掌
之間而三千餘年之治忽燦然畢備炯然
足爲稽古正學之助焉則非有格心之忠
悃者不能也臣能進言不能必君之樂於
===
受言蓋受言難也巽語而說法語而從夫
孰非受然一指顧之間而百十餘事之得
失怡然神會毅然顯其稽古正學之思焉
則非有憲天之聰明者不能也此
帝鑑圖說愚姑未陳其說而竊以爲
皇上之取善輔臣之納忠皆爲古今希遘者焉
昔者讀商書伊尹之告其君曰與治同道
罔不興與亂同事罔不亡此千古人臣開
陳法戒之說也前乎此者爲益稷之謨其
punctuated: 明良之盛，敷陳芹曝之忱也。愚雖非其人，竊嘗有所感焉。夫自古帝王願治者，莫不欲稽古正學，而啓沃則在於臣；自古人臣凡願忠者，莫不欲開陳媺惡，而聽納則在於君。君能受言，不能必臣之審於進言，蓋進言難也。論一事、闢一說，夫孰非進？然一指掌之間，而三千餘年之治忽燦然畢備，炯然足爲稽古正學之助焉，則非有格心之忠悃者不能也。臣能進言，不能必君之樂於受言，蓋受言難也。巽語而說、法語而從，夫孰非受？然一指顧之間，而百十餘事之得失怡然神會，毅然顯其稽古正學之思焉，則非有憲天之聰明者不能也。此《帝鑑圖說》，愚姑未陳其說，而竊以爲皇上之取善、輔臣之納忠，皆爲古今希遘者焉。昔者讀《商書》，伊尹之告其君曰：「與治同道，罔不興；與亂同事，罔不亡。」此千古人臣開陳法戒之說也。前乎此者，爲《益稷》之謨，其
translation_en: … the flourishing of an enlightened ruler and worthy ministers, and to set forth our humble sincerity. Though I am not worthy to be that person, I have privately felt deeply moved by this. Since antiquity, among emperors and kings who desired good governance, there have been none who did not wish to examine the past and rectify their learning—yet enlightening and enriching the sovereign's mind rests with the ministers. Since antiquity, among ministers who wished to be loyal, there have been none who did not wish to set forth examples of good and evil—yet listening to and accepting their counsel rests with the ruler. A ruler may be able to accept advice, yet he cannot be certain that his ministers will be judicious in offering it, for offering advice is difficult. Discussing a single affair or refuting a single argument—which of these is not offering advice? Yet within the span of pointing at one's palm, to have the order and neglect of more than three thousand years brilliantly and completely arrayed, shining forth brightly enough to aid in examining the past and rectifying learning—none could do this without possessing the heartfelt loyalty required to rectify the sovereign's mind. A minister may be able to offer advice, yet he cannot be certain that his ruler will delight in accepting it, for accepting advice is difficult. Being pleased by gentle words of admonition or complying with words of strict rectitude—which of these is not accepting advice? Yet within the span of a single glance, to joyfully comprehend in spirit the successes and failures of more than a hundred affairs, and to resolutely manifest the aspiration to examine the past and rectify learning—none could do this without possessing heaven-emulating intelligence and sagacity. Regarding this Illustrated Mirror for Emperors (Dijian tushuo 帝鑑圖說), before I even set forth its teachings, I privately consider that His Majesty's adoption of what is good and the Grand Secretaries' offering of loyalty are both rare encounters in past and present alike. In the past, when reading the "Documents of Shang" (Shangshu 商書), Yi Yin 伊尹 admonished his ruler, saying: "He who follows the same Way as those who brought order will never fail to flourish; he who engages in the same affairs as those who brought disorder will never fail to perish." Throughout the ages, this has been the doctrine by which ministers set forth models to emulate and warnings to heed. Earlier than this were the counsels of "Yi and Ji" (Yi Ji 益稷); in their…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
告舜也以堯之廣運爲勸而卽以丹朱之
傲佚爲儆後乎此者爲周公之書其告成
王也以殷三宗之無逸爲勸卽以殷後王
之耽樂爲儆是自古賢臣其矢謨弼德先
後率由一道然關龍逢非不告夏王也而
夏之爲夏何如也王子比干亦未嘗不告
殷王也而殷之爲殷又何如也故論者不
以禹之陳善閉邪爲難而以虞舜之從諫
爲聖不以周公之昭德塞違爲大而以成
===
王之聽言爲賢何也臣之願忠者衆而君
之願治者實鮮遭也仰惟
皇上體聖神之資紹雍煕之統
卽位以來時御
經筵日新
聖學上嘉堯舜下陋唐宋稽古正學之功亹亹
然日有就月有將矣輔弼大臣啓沃有見
忠愛無窮乃屬講官博采古今理亂興衰
得失之跡取唐人以古爲鑑之意名之曰
punctuated: 告舜也，以堯之廣運爲勸，而卽以丹朱之傲佚爲儆；後乎此者爲周公之書，其告成王也，以殷三宗之無逸爲勸，卽以殷後王之耽樂爲儆。是自古賢臣，其矢謨弼德，先後率由一道。然關龍逢非不告夏王也，而夏之爲夏何如也？王子比干亦未嘗不告殷王也，而殷之爲殷又何如也？故論者不以禹之陳善閉邪爲難，而以虞舜之從諫爲聖；不以周公之昭德塞違爲大，而以成王之聽言爲賢。何也？臣之願忠者衆，而君之願治者實鮮遭也。仰惟皇上體聖神之資，紹雍煕之統。卽位以來，時御經筵，日新聖學，上嘉堯、舜，下陋唐、宋，稽古正學之功，亹亹然日有就、月有將矣。輔弼大臣啓沃有見，忠愛無窮，乃屬講官博采古今理亂、興衰、得失之跡，取唐人以古爲鑑之意，名之曰
translation_en:
… admonition to Shun, encouraged him with Yao's vast and dynamic virtue while immediately warning him with Danzhu's arrogance and idleness. After this came the writings of the Duke of Zhou, which, in admonishing King Cheng, encouraged him with the freedom from idleness of the three worthy ancestors of Yin, while immediately warning him with the indulgence in pleasure of the later kings of Yin. Thus, worthy ministers since antiquity, in presenting counsels and assisting virtue, earlier and later have all followed the same path. Yet it is not that Guan Longfeng failed to admonish the king of Xia, and yet what became of Xia? Nor did Prince Bigan ever fail to admonish the king of Yin, and yet what became of Yin? Therefore, commentators do not regard Yu's setting forth of the good and shutting out of the perverse as what was difficult, but consider Yu Shun's following of remonstrance to be sage; they do not regard the Duke of Zhou's illuminating of virtue and blocking of transgressions as what was great, but consider King Cheng's heeding of words to be worthy. Why is this? Because ministers who wish to be loyal are many, whereas rulers who wish for good governance are truly rarely encountered.

Looking up in reverence, His Majesty embodies sage and spirit-like endowments and succeeds to a lineage of harmonious peace. Since ascending the throne, he has regularly attended the Classics Mat, daily renewing his sage learning. Above, he admires Yao and Shun; below, he disdains Tang and Song. In the work of examining antiquity and rectifying learning, he has tirelessly made daily achievements and monthly progress. The grand ministers of assistance and support, possessing insight in their enlightening counsels and boundless loyalty and affection, thereupon instructed the Lecturers to extensively gather historical traces of order and disorder, rise and fall, and success and failure from antiquity to the present. Adopting the Tang-dynasty idea of taking antiquity as a mirror, they named it the…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
帝鑑圖分之則爲聖哲芳規狂愚覆轍之目散
之則爲八十有一三十有六之條一條之
首各冠以圖一事之終各系以說繪繕既
畢開陳大旨草疏而進之
皇上御座爲起優旨褒答頃之披圖按說
指顧清問莫不竟其底裏辯其得失而定其
法戒之程且
宣付史館用昭君臣交脩之義大哉
聖心樂於受言周成之賢豈足方駕即虞帝之
===
===
聖固已齊軌矣猗歟休哉今
宣布之書殆徧海宇人知莊誦而經幄之臣
闡明眾義用資啓沃有不俟於應物箴規
皇上兼綜條貫悉見躬行有不待於隨時諫止
繇是道也行將登之三咸之五矣乃執事
復欲諸生悉數以終其物詳繹以明其意
舉要以提其綱獻忠以盡其蘊草茅之人
何足以及此然日者
宣布所及莊誦無已亦嘗管窺萬一竊惟自
punctuated: 《帝鑑圖》。分之則爲「聖哲芳規」、「狂愚覆轍」之目；散之則爲八十有一、三十有六之條。一條之首，各冠以圖；一事之終，各系以說。繪繕既畢，開陳大旨，草疏而進之。皇上御座爲起，優旨褒答。頃之，披圖按說，指顧清問，莫不竟其底裏，辯其得失，而定其法戒之程。且宣付史館，用昭君臣交脩之義。大哉！聖心樂於受言，周成之賢豈足方駕？即虞帝之聖，固已齊軌矣。猗歟休哉！今宣布之書，殆徧海宇，人知莊誦。而經幄之臣，闡明眾義，用資啓沃，有不俟於應物箴規；皇上兼綜條貫，悉見躬行，有不待於隨時諫止。繇是道也，行將登之三、咸之五矣。乃執事復欲諸生悉數以終其物，詳繹以明其意，舉要以提其綱，獻忠以盡其蘊。草茅之人，何足以及此？然日者宣布所及，莊誦無已，亦嘗管窺萬一。竊惟自
translation_en: … Illustrated Mirror for the Emperor (Dijian tu). Divided into main categories, they form the headings of "Fragrant Models of Sages and Worthies" and "Overturned Carts of the Reckless and Foolish"; broken down into individual entries, they comprise eighty-one and thirty-six items respectively. At the head of each entry, it is crowned with an illustration; at the end of each episode, it is appended with an explanation. Once the painting and transcription were completed, they set forth the grand purport, drafted a memorial, and presented it. His Majesty rose from the Imperial Throne for them and replied with a gracious decree of praise. Shortly thereafter, He opened the illustrations and examined the explanations, pointing, looking, and making clear inquiries, never failing to probe to the very bottom of each matter, distinguish its successes and failures, and establish the standard for what to emulate and what to guard against. Moreover, He ordered it delivered to the Historiography Institute to manifest the principle of ruler and ministers cultivating virtue together. Great indeed is the Sacred Mind in its delight at receiving counsel! How could the worthiness of King Cheng of Zhou suffice to ride abreast of Him? Even with the sageliness of Emperor Shun of Yu, He has surely already matched tracks. Oh, how magnificent! Now the promulgated book has reached almost everywhere within thefour seas, and people know to recite it with reverence. Meanwhile, the ministers of the Classics Mat expound its manifold meanings to aid in enlightening and enriching the imperial mind, without having to wait for specific occasions to offer admonitions; and His Majesty comprehensively synthesizes its threads and principles, manifesting them all in His personal conduct, without having to wait for timely remonstrances to deter Him. Following this path, we shall soon ascend to the level of the Three August Ones and reach harmony with the Five Emperors! Yet Your Excellency still wishes us students to enumerate the items in full to exhaust their substance, unpack them in detail to clarify their meaning, raise the essentials to grasp their overarching framework, and offer our loyalty to draw out their deepest implications. How could a rustic person from the thatched huts be equal to this? Nevertheless, in recent days, as the promulgated work has reached us, I have recited it endlessly with reverence and have also caught a humble glimpse of one ten-thousandth of it. I venture to reflect that since…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
古帝王得失興衰殊趣異狀總之不出治
亂兩塗其治也未有不以敬天法祖聽言
納諫節用愛人親賢臣遠小人憂勤惕厲
而治若圖中所載由堯帝之任賢圖治至
哲宗之燭送詞臣是已今按其圖攷其事
因以孰復其說蓋二帝如天之莫可形容
三代如地之靡不持載漢高以下如星辰
之各有光輝雖大小不同其所繇以適治
實同一軌也休哉治乎韋布對之且勃勃
===
然願見其盛矧
聖明紹虞夏商周之統將集漢唐宋英君誼辟
之大成者也有不超然而上嘉下樂者乎
其亂也未有不以不畏天地不法祖宗拒
諫遂非侈用虐民親小人遠賢臣盤樂怠
敖而亂若圖中所載由太康之遊畋失位
至宋徽之任用六賊是已今按其圖攷其
事因以孰復其說其以剛暴失國者直若
褻火以自焚其以昏庸失國者直若狎水
punctuated: 古帝王得失興衰，殊趣異狀，總之不出治亂兩塗。其治也，未有不以敬天法祖、聽言納諫、節用愛人、親賢臣、遠小人、憂勤惕厲而治。若圖中所載，由堯帝之「任賢圖治」至哲宗之「燭送詞臣」是已。今按其圖，攷其事，因以孰復其說。蓋二帝如天之莫可形容，三代如地之靡不持載，漢高以下如星辰之各有光輝。雖大小不同，其所繇以適治，實同一軌也。休哉治乎！韋布對之，且勃勃然願見其盛；矧聖明紹虞、夏、商、周之統，將集漢、唐、宋英君誼辟之大成者也，有不超然而上嘉下樂者乎？其亂也，未有不以不畏天地、不法祖宗、拒諫遂非、侈用虐民、親小人、遠賢臣、盤樂怠敖而亂。若圖中所載，由太康之「遊畋失位」至宋徽之「任用六賊」是已。今按其圖，攷其事，因以孰復其說。其以剛暴失國者，直若褻火以自焚；其以昏庸失國者，直若狎水
translation_en: … ancient emperors and kings, in their successes and failures, their rise and decline, varied in their inclinations and circumstances, yet in sum they never departed from the two paths of order and disorder. As for their achieving order, there was never a case where they did not achieve it through revering Heaven and modeling themselves on their ancestors, heeding counsel and accepting remonstrance, economizing on expenditures and cherishing the people, drawing close to worthy ministers and keeping petty men at a distance, and being anxious, diligent, vigilant, and strict. Such are the cases recorded in the illustrations, from Emperor Yao's "Employing the Worthy to Plan for Governance" down to Zhezong's "Escorting the Literary Official with Candles." Now, if we examine their illustrations, investigate their deeds, and thereby thoroughly ponder the explanations of them: the Two Emperors were like Heaven, beyond all description; the Three Dynasties were like Earth, sustaining and bearing all things; and from Han Gaozu onward, rulers were like the stars and constellations, each possessing its own radiance. Although they differed in magnitude, the path by which they attained good governance in fact followed the very same track. How splendid is such order! When a commoner in coarse cloth faces it, even he is stirred with an ardent desire to witness its flourishing; how much more so for His Sacred Majesty, who inherits the succession of Yu, Xia, Shang, and Zhou, and is about to synthesize the great achievements of the heroic and righteous sovereigns of Han, Tang, and Song—could he fail to rise above all and bring about a state where the sovereign is lauded above and the people rejoice below? As for their falling into disorder, there was never a case where they did not fall into it through failing to stand in awe of Heaven and Earth, failing to model themselves on their ancestors, rejecting remonstrance and persisting in wrong, spending extravagantly and tyrannizing the people, drawing close to petty men and keeping worthy ministers at a distance, and indulging in pleasure and indolent arrogance. Such are the cases recorded in the illustrations, from Tai Kang's "Losing the Throne Through Hunting Excursions" down to Song Huizong's "Employing the Six Traitors." Now, if we examine their illustrations, investigate their deeds, and thereby thoroughly ponder the explanations of them: those who lost their states through ruthless violence were simply like those who trifle with fire only to burn themselves; those who lost their states through benighted mediocrity were simply like those who dally with water …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以自溺其以小慧私智失國者又直若舞
劒以自戕爲事不同而其所繇以致亂若
同一轍也痛哉亂乎韋布對之且憬憬然
追悼其失矧
聖明心堯舜禹湯文武之心將深慨夫桀紂桓
靈煬徽之愚也有不毅然而深惡痛戒者
乎然上下古今其善可爲法者多矣乃儉
之于八十有一何也蓋曰九陽數也人君
之道要在當陽故用九九陽當發見汲汲
===
乎欲以亟法之也惡可爲戒者尤多矣乃
靳之于三十有六何也若曰六陰數也人
君之道要在銷陰故從六六陰當伏藏汲
汲乎欲以亟戒之也是其取數命意卽已
寓夫勸沮之誠而宏旨微文孰不由於忠
悃之發哉乃執事復欲廣引博喻之中求
切近要領之實愚謂凡爲陽爲吉德者孰
非可法也凡爲陰爲凶德者孰非可戒也
其切近要領則輔臣之疏固已具之亦何
punctuated: 以自溺，其以小慧私智失國者，又直若舞劒以自戕。爲事不同，而其所繇以致亂，若同一轍也。痛哉亂乎！韋布對之，且憬憬然追悼其失；矧聖明心堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之心，將深慨夫桀、紂、桓、靈、煬、徽之愚也，有不毅然而深惡痛戒者乎？然上下古今，其善可爲法者多矣，乃儉之于八十有一，何也？蓋曰：九，陽數也；人君之道，要在當陽，故用九九。陽當發見，汲汲乎欲以亟法之也。惡可爲戒者尤多矣，乃靳之于三十有六，何也？若曰：六，陰數也；人君之道，要在銷陰，故從六六。陰當伏藏，汲汲乎欲以亟戒之也。是其取數命意，卽已寓夫勸沮之誠，而宏旨微文，孰不由於忠悃之發哉！乃執事復欲廣引博喻之中，求切近要領之實。愚謂凡爲陽、爲吉德者，孰非可法也？凡爲陰、爲凶德者，孰非可戒也？其切近要領，則輔臣之疏固已具之，亦何
translation_en: … to drown themselves; and those who lost their states through petty cleverness and private cunning were just like those who brandish swords to slay themselves. Their deeds differed, yet the ways by which they brought about disorder followed the very same track. How painful is disorder! When even a commoner in coarse cloth confronts these examples, he awakens with a start and laments their failures; how much more so when His Sacred Enlightened Majesty, taking as his own the minds of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, King Wen, and King Wu, will deeply sigh over the folly of Jie, Zhou, Emperors Huan and Ling of Han, Emperor Yang of Sui, and Emperor Huizong of Song—could He fail to resolutely abhor them deeply and take painful warning from them? Yet looking up and down from antiquity to the present, the good deeds that can serve as models are many indeed; why then restrict them to eighty-one? It is as if to say: nine is the number of yang; the Way of the ruler lies essentially in occupying the yang position, and thus nine times nine is used. Since yang ought to be made manifest, one is urgently eager to emulate them at once. The evil deeds that can serve as warnings are even more numerous; why then limit them to thirty-six? It is as if to say: six is the number of yin; the Way of the ruler lies essentially in dispelling yin, and thus six times six is followed. Since yin ought to be hidden away, one is urgently eager to take warning from them at once. Thus, the very choice of numbers and conception of meaning already embody the sincerity of encouragement and deterrence; and as for the grand purport and subtle wording, which of them does not spring from an outpouring of loyal devotion? Now Your Excellency further wishes, amidst these broad citations and wide-ranging illustrations, to seek the substance of what is most immediate and essential. In my humble view, among all things that pertain to yang and to auspicious virtue, which is not worthy of emulation? Among all things that pertain to yin and to baleful vice, which is not worthy of serving as a warning? As for what is immediate and essential, the memorial of the Grand Secretaries has certainly already set it forth in full; how could one …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
能外此而他求乎必欲數其事求其人乎
竊謂堯舜之任賢圖治此其大矣而漢文
帝之止輦受言則近事之可法者也蓋人
君樂受直言則天下之善畢至凡仁孝恭
儉之德自將由眾善以弼成之矣桀紂之
酒色暴虐嘻其甚矣而宋徽宗之任用六
賊則近事之可戒者也蓋人君親信匪人
則天下之不善畢至而凡淫酗奢暴之事
自將由眾不善以釀成之矣是曰陳時觀
===
之内即已具夫緝熙基命之功而神會心
得之餘寧不可為宥密光明之助乎乃執
事復責之有言愚何言哉嘗觀我
世皇之初年也因儒臣進講四箴既
俯為之註矣又以視聽言動之用莫非由心
主之則為范浚心箴之註又以浚之為箴
言心之重而未及夫心之學也則
特著敬一箴以發明心學之要其曰
匪敬弗聚匪一弗純是致力於内者深矣又
punctuated: 能外此而他求乎？必欲數其事、求其人乎？竊謂堯、舜之任賢圖治，此其大矣；而漢文帝之止輦受言，則近事之可法者也。蓋人君樂受直言，則天下之善畢至，凡仁孝恭儉之德，自將由眾善以弼成之矣。桀、紂之酒色暴虐，嘻，其甚矣！而宋徽宗之任用六賊，則近事之可戒者也。蓋人君親信匪人，則天下之不善畢至，而凡淫酗奢暴之事，自將由眾不善以釀成之矣。是曰陳時觀之内，即已具夫緝熙基命之功，而神會心得之餘，寧不可為宥密光明之助乎？乃執事復責之有言，愚何言哉？嘗觀我世皇之初年也，因儒臣進講《四箴》，既俯為之註矣；又以視聽言動之用，莫非由心主之，則為范浚《心箴》之註；又以浚之為箴，言心之重而未及夫心之學也，則特著《敬一箴》以發明心學之要。其曰：「匪敬弗聚，匪一弗純。」是致力於内者深矣。又
translation_en:
… could one look outside of this and seek elsewhere? If one must enumerate specific events and seek out specific individuals, I would venture to say that Yao and Shun employing the worthy to plan for good governance is the grandest example; yet Emperor Wen of Han (Han Wendi) halting his imperial carriage to accept remonstrance is a more recent precedent worthy of emulation. For when a ruler delights in receiving frank speech, all the good in the world will gather before him, and all the virtues of benevolence, filial piety, reverence, and frugality will naturally be assisted to completion through these many goods. The indulgence in wine, women, and tyranny of Jie and Zhou—alas, that was extreme indeed! Yet Emperor Huizong of Song (Song Huizong) employing the Six Traitors (Liu zei) is a more recent precedent worthy of serving as a warning. For when a ruler is intimate with and trusts unworthy men, all the evil in the world will gather before him, and all manner of licentiousness, drunkenness, extravagance, and cruelty will naturally be fermented into being through these many evils. Thus, within the daily display and periodic contemplation of this mirror, the merit of continuing luminous virtue and establishing the Mandate is already present; and beyond spiritual comprehension and mental realization, how could it not serve as an aid to profound, tranquil, and radiant virtue?

Yet Your Excellency further demands that I offer words of my own—what can a foolish student like me say? I have observed that in the early years of our August Emperor Shizong, when Confucian courtiers presented lectures on the Four Admonitions (Si zhen), he condescended to write a commentary on them. Furthermore, considering that the functions of seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting are all governed by the mind, he wrote a commentary on Fan Jun's (范浚) Admonition on the Mind (Xin zhen). And considering further that while Jun's admonition spoke of the importance of the mind, it did not yet reach the learning of the mind, he specially composed the Admonition on Reverence and Unity (Jingyi zhen) to elucidate the essentials of the learning of the mind. In it he says: "Without reverence there is no concentration; without unity there is no purity." Here his exertion of effort within was profound indeed. He also…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
曰
郊則恭誠廟嚴孝趨肅于明庭慎于閒居其
爲敬之功之密如此曰
弗參以三弗貳以二行顧其言終如其始其
爲一之功之密又如此雖
聖心之所造終之所成非凡愚所能窺測然頒
之一時一時之言心學者必歸焉即垂之
萬世萬世之言心學者必歸焉何也聖學
之大不外乎博約二端弗博則約者無以
===
致精弗約則博者無以致一
世皇之學博之於視聽言動之著而復約之以
一心之微斂之於敬一之純而又慎之於
郊廟明庭閒居言行始終之際是爲心學之
全也然則今日所以爲
神孫法者亦豈有外於此乎蓋嘗伏讀
圖說古今之治忽靡所不陳而方
今之政體亦靡所不具矣然圖爲一事事爲一
說正傅說人求多聞之事孔子博學於文
punctuated: 曰：「郊則恭誠，廟嚴孝趨，肅于明庭，慎于閒居。」其爲敬之功之密如此。曰：「弗參以三，弗貳以二，行顧其言，終如其始。」其爲一之功之密又如此。雖聖心之所造、終之所成，非凡愚所能窺測，然頒之一時，一時之言心學者必歸焉；即垂之萬世，萬世之言心學者必歸焉。何也？聖學之大，不外乎博、約二端。弗博則約者無以致精，弗約則博者無以致一。世皇之學，博之於視聽言動之著，而復約之以一心之微；斂之於敬一之純，而又慎之於郊廟、明庭、閒居、言行、始終之際，是爲心學之全也。然則今日所以爲神孫法者，亦豈有外於此乎？蓋嘗伏讀《圖說》，古今之治忽靡所不陳，而方今之政體亦靡所不具矣。然圖爲一事，事爲一說，正傅說「人求多聞」之事，孔子「博學於文」
translation_en: … says: "At the suburban sacrifices, be reverent and sincere; in the ancestral temple, be solemn and hasten with filial piety; be grave in the bright court; be cautious when dwelling in leisure." Such was the meticulousness of His effort at reverence. And it says: "Do not complicate it with a third, nor divide it into two; let actions correspond to words, and the end be like the beginning." Such, again, was the meticulousness of His effort at oneness. Although what the sagely mind attained and what it ultimately accomplished are beyond what an ordinary, foolish person can fathom, yet when promulgated to that one era, those of that era who spoke of the learning of the mind-and-heart necessarily turned to it; and even when handed down for ten thousand generations, those of ten thousand generations who speak of the learning of the mind-and-heart must necessarily turn to it. Why is this? The greatness of sagely learning lies in nothing other than the two aspects of breadth and restraint. Without breadth, restraint has no means to reach precision; without restraint, breadth has no means to reach oneness. The learning of the August Emperor Shizong broadened itself in the manifest aspects of seeing, hearing, speaking, and acting, and then restrained itself through the subtlety of the one mind; it gathered itself into the purity of reverence and oneness, and furthermore exercised caution across the occasions of the suburban sacrifices and ancestral temple, the bright court, dwelling in leisure, words and actions, and beginning and end—this is the entirety of the learning of the mind-and-heart. If this is so, then how could that which serves today as a model for His divine grandson lie outside of this? Indeed, I have humbly read the Illustrated Explanations (Tushuo), in which nothing of the order and neglect of antiquity and the present is left unstated, and nothing of the governmental system of the present day is left unprovided. Yet each illustration represents a single matter, and each matter has a single explanation—this is precisely the business of "a man seeking to hear much" spoken of by Fu Yue, and the effort of "broadly learning in culture" spoken of by Confucius …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之功也意者尚有主敬之方俾意念有所
斂束主一之學俾心原有所持循矣乎盖
光明之用不徒常發於外而宥密之體必
使常保於中然後以之觀書則開卷而有
益以之考事則隨事而致精正言之所發
揮者常與心原流通而邪說之欲簧鼓者
將不能乘間而竊發矣
皇上光紹
祖德統一聖眞端其在此執事特舉
===
世皇諸箴爲問意者其出此乎然
敬一之功圖說固已具之而疏中所謂憂勤惕
厲卽敬之說常持之以憂勤惕厲而
明庭以之
閒居以之始焉以之終焉以之卽一之謂也
亦豈必外此而他求乎唯在正學之臣講
筵之中一發明之耳愚生狂斐不知所裁
唯執事者進而教之幸甚
第二問
punctuated:
之功也。意者尚有主敬之方，俾意念有所斂束；主一之學，俾心原有所持循矣乎？盖光明之用，不徒常發於外；而宥密之體，必使常保於中。然後以之觀書，則開卷而有益；以之考事，則隨事而致精。正言之所發揮者，常與心原流通；而邪說之欲簧鼓者，將不能乘間而竊發矣。皇上光紹祖德，統一聖眞，端其在此。執事特舉世皇諸箴爲問，意者其出此乎？然敬一之功，《圖說》固已具之。而疏中所謂「憂勤惕厲」，卽「敬」之說；常持之以憂勤惕厲，而明庭以之，閒居以之，始焉以之，終焉以之，卽「一」之謂也。亦豈必外此而他求乎？唯在正學之臣，講筵之中，一發明之耳。愚生狂斐，不知所裁，唯執事者進而教之，幸甚。

第二問
translation_en:
… [Confucius's] effort [of broadly studying texts]. Might it not be that there is still the method of abiding in reverence (zhujing), which causes one's thoughts and intentions to be restrained and gathered, and the learning of focusing on oneness (zhuyi), which gives the source of the mind something to hold fast to and follow? For the brilliant function should not merely be constantly manifested on the outside, while the deep and tranquil substance must be constantly preserved within. Only then, when one uses it to read books, opening a scroll will bring benefit; when one uses it to examine affairs, one will attain precision in every matter. What is expounded by orthodox words will constantly flow in harmony with the source of the mind, and heterodox doctrines that seek to beguile like reed-organs and drums will be unable to seize a gap and covertly break out. For His Majesty to gloriously continue the ancestral virtue and unify the sagely truth surely lies right here. When Your Excellency specifically cited the various admonitions of the August Emperor Shizong in your question, did your intention not stem from this? Yet the effort of Reverence and Oneness (Jingyi) is indeed already fully contained in the Illustrated Explanations (Tushuo). Moreover, what the memorial calls "anxious diligence and vigilant trepidation" is precisely the explanation of "Reverence"; to constantly uphold it with anxious diligence and vigilant trepidation—applying it in the bright court, applying it in leisure and seclusion, applying it at the beginning, and applying it to the end—is precisely what is meant by "Oneness." Why must one seek anything else outside of this? It depends solely on ministers of orthodox learning elucidating it once during the Classics Colloquium (jiangyan). I, an ignorant student, am rash and unrefined, and do not know how to judge; I only hope that Your Excellency will bring me forward and instruct me, which would be most fortunate.

Second Question

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
莫睿
同考試官敎諭張批品隲漢唐宋人物侃侃不
作詭隨語異日正色立朝之士也可慶
同考試官敎授伍批有斷制有抑揚非胸中銖
兩素定者不能也一結又有獨詣之見
考試官敎授萬批博洽之學奇崛之調
考試官敎授吳批蒼古
天下有任事之臣而不尚其事者爲難有
立功之臣而不有其功者爲大明足以察
===
===
難料之機辯足以決難剖之惑强足以勝
艱難之任權足以定倉卒之變皆所謂任
事者也然事之來則必有所由致國鼎旣
沸我底奠之强寇方張我式遏之儲貳將
危而復安人心幾搖而旋定皆所謂立功
者也然功之成亦必有所由起惟古之君
子出而以身任天下之重者常於無事之
時忠言至計求所以銷患於無形不幸而
有事則死生以之惟知有正而不知有身
punctuated:
莫睿
同考試官敎諭張批：品隲漢、唐、宋人物，侃侃不作詭隨語，異日正色立朝之士也。可慶！
同考試官敎授伍批：有斷制，有抑揚，非胸中銖兩素定者不能也。一結又有獨詣之見。
考試官敎授萬批：博洽之學，奇崛之調。
考試官敎授吳批：蒼古。

天下有任事之臣，而不尚其事者爲難；有立功之臣，而不有其功者爲大。明足以察難料之機，辯足以決難剖之惑，强足以勝艱難之任，權足以定倉卒之變，皆所謂任事者也。然事之來，則必有所由致。國鼎旣沸，我底奠之；强寇方張，我式遏之；儲貳將危而復安，人心幾搖而旋定，皆所謂立功者也。然功之成，亦必有所由起。惟古之君子，出而以身任天下之重者，常於無事之時，忠言至計，求所以銷患於無形；不幸而有事，則死生以之，惟知有正而不知有身
translation_en:
Mo Rui 莫睿
Associate Examiner, Instructor Zhang 張, comments: In evaluating figures of the Han, Tang, and Song, he speaks forthrightly without making deceitfully conformist remarks. In the future he will be a gentleman who stands at court with an upright countenance. Worthy of celebration!
Associate Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Wu 伍, comments: There is decisive judgment and balanced praise and censure; none could do this whose sense of weight and measure was not already firmly settled in his breast. The conclusion, moreover, displays uniquely penetrating insight.
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Wan 萬, comments: Broad and thorough learning; a strikingly rugged style.
Examiner, Prefectural Director of Studies Wu 吳, comments: Vigorous and antique in style.

In the world there are ministers who shoulder responsibilities, yet those who do not exalt their own handling of affairs are rare; there are ministers who establish merit, yet those who do not claim their merit as their own are great. Having perspicacity sufficient to discern unforeseeable turns of events, eloquence sufficient to resolve doubts hard to untangle, strength sufficient to bear arduous charges, and adaptability sufficient to settle sudden upheavals—all these describe those who shoulder responsibilities. Yet when crises arise, there is always something that brought them about. When the dynastic tripods are already boiling in turmoil and one brings them to settled stability; when powerful bandits are just spreading rampant and one checks them; when the heir apparent is on the verge of peril and is restored to safety; when the people's hearts are nearly shaken and are promptly steadied—all these describe those who establish merit. Yet when merit is achieved, there is likewise always something from which it originated. Only the noble men of antiquity who came forth to take the heavy burden of the empire upon themselves in person always offered loyal words and supreme counsels in times of peace, seeking the means to dissolve calamities before they took form; and if, unfortunately, crises did occur, they staked their life and death upon them, knowing only what was upright and not knowing that their own persons…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之可愛惟知有義而不知有名之可慕招
之不來麾之不去此其志要有大過人者
非徒乘時隨世而苟焉以就功名者比也
知此則社稷之臣可得而論矣執事謂奠
朝廷奠海宇處艱大之時當呼吸之會而
屬之戇者之臣有味乎其言之也愚想夫
唐虞之時吁咈陳謨都俞矢告君臣明保
弼亮無非折姦宄綏蠻夷之道不動聲色
而誅窮奇滅饕餮格有苗以及宗膾胥敖
===
之黨天下晏然不知誰之爲功吾所知者
曰九德咸事曰成允成功而已逮及商周
初造太甲不惠三叔流言邦之安危若蹈
虎尾伊尹周公以忠誠之德徐而正之行
天下所未有之事而天下不以爲疑及事
定復故而功泯於無迹此不惟事功非所
言而社稷之臣亦不足以名之眞孟子所
列大人之品而豈但天民之流亞也自是
而後不惟大人不可易見而社稷臣亦未
punctuated: 之可愛，惟知有義而不知有名之可慕，招之不來，麾之不去。此其志要有大過人者，非徒乘時隨世而苟焉以就功名者比也。知此，則社稷之臣可得而論矣。執事謂奠朝廷、奠海宇，處艱大之時，當呼吸之會，而屬之戇者之臣，有味乎其言之也！愚想夫唐虞之時，吁咈陳謨，都俞矢告，君臣明保弼亮，無非折姦宄、綏蠻夷之道。不動聲色，而誅窮奇、滅饕餮、格有苗，以及宗、膾、胥、敖之黨，天下晏然，不知誰之爲功。吾所知者，曰「九德咸事」，曰「成允成功」而已。逮及商周初造，太甲不惠，三叔流言，邦之安危若蹈虎尾。伊尹、周公以忠誠之德徐而正之，行天下所未有之事，而天下不以爲疑。及事定復故，而功泯於無迹。此不惟事功非所言，而社稷之臣亦不足以名之，眞孟子所列大人之品，而豈但天民之流亞也！自是而後，不惟大人不可易見，而社稷臣亦未
translation_en: … is worth cherishing, and knowing only righteousness without knowing that fame is worth coveting—when beckoned they do not come, and when waved away they do not leave. In this, their resolve surely far surpasses that of ordinary men; they cannot be compared to those who merely ride the times and follow the age, casually achieving merit and fame. Once one understands this, then ministers of state (sheji zhi chen) can be discussed. When Your Excellency speaks of stabilizing the court and stabilizing the realm, of coping with times of great difficulty and facing moments of life-and-death urgency, and attributes this to blunt and outspoken ministers, how deeply meaningful are those words! I reflect upon the era of Tang Yao and Yu Shun, when counsels were presented with sighs of dissent and declarations were made with cries of approval, and ruler and minister enlightened, protected, and assisted one another—none of this was anything other than the way to break wicked traitors and pacify the Man and Yi barbarians. Without changing countenance or raising their voices, they executed Qiongqi, destroyed Taotie, brought the ruler of Miao to submission, along with the factions of Zong, Kuai, Xu, and Ao; the realm was at peace, and no one knew whose merit it was. All that we know of it is what was called "those of the nine virtues all serving in office" and "achieving sincerity and achieving success," nothing more. Coming down to the early founding of the Shang and Zhou dynasties, when Tai Jia was disobedient and the Three Royal Uncles spread rumors, the safety and peril of the state was like treading on a tiger's tail. Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou, through their loyal and sincere virtue, calmly rectified the situation, carrying out deeds unprecedented in the world without the world doubting them. When affairs were settled and restored to normal, their achievements vanished without a trace. Of such men, not only are mere practical achievements unworthy of mention, even the title "minister of state" is insufficient to name them; they truly belonged to the rank of the "great man" (daren) set forth by Mencius—how could they be merely the equals of the "people of Heaven" (tianmin)! From that time onward, not only could great men no longer be easily seen, even ministers of state could not…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
可輕擬惟漢武帝始以汲黯爲近之而君
子亦有取焉豈亦謂其意在於格君心明
國是而不急於事功故耶蓋嘗由汲黯而
上下古今竊欲有所評隲焉請因明問而
陳之漢高帝旣定天下不能割戚姬之愛
而欲立趙王國本搖矣四皓一招而惠帝
之位定則子房之謀也呂后首背高帝之
約欲盡王諸呂漢統殆矣左袒一呼而炎
祚之業安則周勃之爲也此非有功於漢
===
者乎安史倡亂播蕩四海郭子儀起朔方
提孤軍再造王室功蓋天下以一身係安
危者三十年何其盛歟唐綱不振淮西拒
命裴度奮不顧身討吳元濟削平諸鎮名
聞四夷以一身係輕重者亦二十餘年何
其偉歟此非有功於唐者乎契丹舉國入
寇羣臣震慄國之安危在此時也寇準決
親征之策一渡河而虜首褫魄卒定南北
之盟丁謂諂事奄寺植黨驕橫大臣不得
punctuated: 可輕擬。惟漢武帝始以汲黯爲近之，而君子亦有取焉，豈亦謂其意在於格君心、明國是，而不急於事功故耶？蓋嘗由汲黯而上下古今，竊欲有所評隲焉。請因明問而陳之。漢高帝旣定天下，不能割戚姬之愛，而欲立趙王，國本搖矣；四皓一招而惠帝之位定，則子房之謀也。呂后首背高帝之約，欲盡王諸呂，漢統殆矣；左袒一呼而炎祚之業安，則周勃之爲也。此非有功於漢者乎？安、史倡亂，播蕩四海，郭子儀起朔方，提孤軍，再造王室，功蓋天下，以一身係安危者三十年，何其盛歟！唐綱不振，淮西拒命，裴度奮不顧身，討吳元濟，削平諸鎮，名聞四夷，以一身係輕重者亦二十餘年，何其偉歟！此非有功於唐者乎？契丹舉國入寇，羣臣震慄，國之安危在此時也；寇準決親征之策，一渡河而虜首褫魄，卒定南北之盟。丁謂諂事奄寺，植黨驕橫，大臣不得
translation_en:
… easily be compared to one. It was only Emperor Wu of Han (Han Wudi 漢武帝) who first considered Ji An 汲黯 to be close to such a minister, and gentlemen of virtue have also approved of this judgment. Was it not because his intention lay in rectifying the sovereign's mind and clarifying the principles of state policy, rather than rushing after mere practical achievements? Taking Ji An as a starting point to survey antiquity and the present, I have privately wished to offer an appraisal. Allow me to set it forth in response to Your insightful question.

After Emperor Gao of Han (Han Gaodi 漢高帝) had pacified the realm, he could not sever his affection for Consort Qi (Qi Ji 戚姬) and wished to establish the Prince of Zhao (Zhao Wang 趙王) as heir, thereby shaking the very foundation of the state. Yet with a single summons of the Four Graybeards (Sihao 四皓), the position of Emperor Hui (Huidi 惠帝) was secured—this was the stratagem of Zifang 子房 [Zhang Liang 張良]. Empress Lü (Lü Hou 呂后) was the first to violate Emperor Gao's covenant, wishing to enfeoff all the members of the Lü clan as kings, placing the Han succession in grave peril. Yet with a single call to bare the left shoulder, the enterprise of the Fiery Mandate [Han] was made secure—this was the deed of Zhou Bo 周勃. Were these men not meritorious toward the Han?

When An Lushan 安祿山 and Shi Siming 史思明 instigated rebellion and threw the Four Seas into turmoil, Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 rose up from Shuofang 朔方, leading a lone army to rebuild the royal house. His achievements overshadowed the realm, and upon his person alone hung the safety and peril of the empire for thirty years—how flourishing indeed! When the imperial authority of the Tang faltered and Huaixi 淮西 defied commands, Pei Du 裴度 roused himself without regard for his own safety to punish Wu Yuanji 吳元濟 and pacify the regional military commands. His renown was heard among the four surrounding tribes, and upon his person alone hung the weight of the empire for more than twenty years as well—how magnificent indeed! Were these men not meritorious toward the Tang?

When the Khitan (Qidan 契丹) mobilized their entire state to invade, the assembled ministers trembled in fear, and the survival or ruin of the state hung upon that moment. Kou Zhun 寇準 resolved upon the policy of an imperial campaign in person; no sooner had the Emperor crossed the Yellow River than the enemy chieftain lost heart, ultimately establishing the covenant between North and South. When Ding Wei 丁謂 flatteringly served the eunuchs, forming factions in arrogant tyranny so that the great ministers could not …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
與聞機政宋之理亂未可知也王曾進山
陵之議一設計而姦邪屏逐卒成奠安之
勢此非有功於宋者乎之數臣者或以一
言解危疑之變或以一身任天下之重或
定傾於旣著或遏亂於方萌三代而下不
多數也即以社稷臣許之未為不可而君
子顧不盡以與之乃以與長孺之戇者何
哉吾觀長孺立朝大節矯乎卓矣觀其發
倉賑河南之饑有出疆安社稷之義廷諍
===
折公孫弘之詐有不與佞臣同朝之節峻
刑罰則諫神寶馬則諫誅羣臣則諫敝中
國以事夷狄則諫至於內多慾外施仁義
之諫尤切中武帝之病而其抗丞相蚡揖
大將軍青寢淮南王安之謀所以肅清朝
廷皆非秦漢而下事君者所能幾及乃淮
陽之命不顧禁闥之請而故欲出之武帝
豈真不知黯者其意盖將堅其操挫其銳
而以異時社稷之重倚用之使黯尚存則
punctuated: 與聞機政，宋之理亂未可知也。王曾進山陵之議，一設計而姦邪屏逐，卒成奠安之勢。此非有功於宋者乎？之數臣者，或以一言解危疑之變，或以一身任天下之重，或定傾於旣著，或遏亂於方萌，三代而下不多數也。即以社稷臣許之，未為不可，而君子顧不盡以與之，乃以與長孺之戇者，何哉？吾觀長孺立朝大節，矯乎卓矣！觀其發倉賑河南之饑，有出疆安社稷之義；廷諍折公孫弘之詐，有不與佞臣同朝之節；峻刑罰則諫，神寶馬則諫，誅羣臣則諫，敝中國以事夷狄則諫，至於「內多慾外施仁義」之諫，尤切中武帝之病。而其抗丞相蚡，揖大將軍青，寢淮南王安之謀，所以肅清朝廷，皆非秦、漢而下事君者所能幾及。乃淮陽之命，不顧禁闥之請而故欲出之，武帝豈真不知黯者？其意盖將堅其操、挫其銳，而以異時社稷之重倚用之。使黯尚存，則
translation_en:
… participate in confidential state affairs; whether the Song dynasty would see order or disorder could not yet be known. Wang Zeng 王曾 put forward his deliberation regarding the imperial mausoleum; with a single stratagem, the treacherous and wicked were expelled, ultimately establishing a state of secure stability. Were these men not meritorious to the Song? Among these several ministers, some resolved crises of peril and doubt with a single word, some bore the weight of the empire in their own person, some stabilized what was tottering once it had already become manifest, and some suppressed disorder just as it was budding. Since the Three Dynasties, such men have not been numerous. Even if one were to grant them the title of "Ministers of the Altars of Soil and Grain" (sheji chen 社稷臣), it would not be inappropriate. Yet why do superior men not fully grant this title to all of them, and instead bestow it upon the blunt Ji An 汲黯 (style name Changru 長孺)?

When I observe Changru's great integrity in standing at court, how stalwart and preeminent it was! Look at his opening the granaries to relieve the famine in Henan 河南—it embodied the righteous principle of acting on one's own authority beyond the borders to bring peace to the Altars of Soil and Grain. His disputing at court to expose the deceit of Gongsun Hong 公孫弘 showed the integrity of refusing to share a court with a sycophantic minister. When punishments were made severe, he remonstrated; when the heavenly precious horses were revered as divine, he remonstrated; when officials were executed, he remonstrated; when the Central Plains were exhausted in order to campaign against the four barbarian tribes, he remonstrated. As for his remonstrance that the emperor "harbored many desires within while outwardly displaying benevolence and righteousness," it struck especially close to Emperor Wu's 武帝 (r. 141–87 BCE) failing. Moreover, his standing as an equal against Counselor-in-Chief Tian Fen 田蚡, his merely bowing to General-in-Chief Wei Qing 衛青, and his causing Liu An 劉安, the Prince of Huainan 淮南王, to abandon his treasonous plots—all by which he purified and brought awe to the imperial court—were things that those serving their rulers from the Qin and Han dynasties onward could scarcely approach.

As for the appointment to Huaiyang 淮陽, when Emperor Wu disregarded Ji An's plea to remain within the palace precincts and deliberately sent him out to the provinces, how could Emperor Wu truly have failed to understand Ji An? His intention was probably to temper his resolve and blunt his sharp edge, so as to rely on and employ him for the weighty affairs of the Altars of Soil and Grain at a future time. Had Ji An still been alive, then…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
周公襁褓之圖當首是賜而守成深堅賁
育不奪之節如嚴助所論雖霍子孟不能
過之矣此豈任事邀功之臣可與幾耶此
所以獨擅乎社稷之許也嗟乎人臣事君
能爲其所得爲而不能必其所難必當持
重以應國家之事而不可輕試以徼倖成
之功故履霜堅氷憂於陰之始生羸豕蹢
躅戒於姤之方壯何則防潰於蟻穴而止
燎於星星此深謀遠見之所圖也吾嘗反
===
===
覆考之高帝明達之君也親見扶蘇胡亥
之事而欲易太子豈其心得已哉彼其揣
摩天下之故審矣良雖假四皓以羽翼之
而未有爲漢家社稷長計者卽使惠帝可
立亦當明以大義而屬大臣輔導以沮睥
睨者之心今不出此而乃以子脅父謀臣
策士者爲之耳良蓋未聞君子之大道也
漢柄倒持周勃不能蚤正於王呂之初及
勢成禍迫倉卒交驩非有長策可以制諸
punctuated:
周公襁褓之圖，當首是賜；而守成深堅，賁、育不奪之節，如嚴助所論，雖霍子孟不能過之矣。此豈任事邀功之臣可與幾耶？此所以獨擅乎社稷之許也。

嗟乎！人臣事君，能爲其所得爲，而不能必其所難必；當持重以應國家之事，而不可輕試以徼倖成之功。故「履霜堅氷」，憂於陰之始生；「羸豕蹢躅」，戒於姤之方壯。何則？防潰於蟻穴，而止燎於星星，此深謀遠見之所圖也。吾嘗反覆考之：高帝，明達之君也，親見扶蘇、胡亥之事，而欲易太子，豈其心得已哉？彼其揣摩天下之故審矣。良雖假四皓以羽翼之，而未有爲漢家社稷長計者。卽使惠帝可立，亦當明以大義，而屬大臣輔導，以沮睥睨者之心。今不出此，而乃以子脅父，謀臣策士者爲之耳，良蓋未聞君子之大道也。漢柄倒持，周勃不能蚤正於王呂之初；及勢成禍迫，倉卒交驩，非有長策可以制諸
translation_en:
… the painting of the Duke of Zhou holding the infant king in swaddling clothes would surely have been bestowed upon him first; and in his deep firmness in preserving the accomplished order, with an integrity that not even Meng Ben 孟賁 or Xia Yu 夏育 could夺 (shake), just as Yan Zhu 嚴助 discussed, even Huo Zimeng 霍子孟 (Huo Guang 霍光) could not have surpassed him. How could ministers who merely take on tasks to seek personal credit ever hope to approach this? This is why he alone commanded the praise of being a minister of the altars of soil and grain.

Alas! When a minister serves his ruler, he can do what is within his power to do, but cannot guarantee what is difficult to make certain; he must maintain prudence and gravity in responding to affairs of state, and must not lightly experiment in hopes of chancing upon a lucky success. Therefore, "treading on frost, solid ice will come" expresses anxiety at the very first nascence of yin; "a lean pig pacing restlessly" warns when the Gou 姤 hexagram is just growing strong. Why is this? Because a dike collapses from an ant-hole, and a prairie fire starts from a tiny spark; this is what deep counsel and far-sighted vision seek to guard against. I have repeatedly examined this: Emperor Gao 高帝 was a discerning and perceptive ruler. Having personally witnessed the affair of Fusu 扶蘇 and Huhai 胡亥, when he wished to replace the Heir Apparent, how could his heart have done so lightly or willingly? He had weighed the circumstances of the empire most thoroughly. Although Zhang Liang 張良 borrowed the Four Graybeards (Sihao 四皓) to serve as wings to support him, he had no long-term plan for the altars of the House of Han. Even supposing Emperor Hui 惠帝 were fit to be established, he ought to have made the great principle of righteousness clear and entrusted the great ministers with his guidance and tutoring, so as to deter the ambitions of those who cast covetous eyes upon the throne. Instead of taking this course, he used the son to coerce the father—which is merely the work of scheming ministers and tacticians; Zhang Liang had evidently never heard the Great Way of the gentleman. When the handle of Han authority was held upside down, Zhou Bo 周勃 was unable to rectify matters early on when the Lü 呂 clan were first made kings; and when their power was consolidated and disaster pressed close, he hurriedly cultivated friendship [with Chen Ping 陳平], without possessing any long-range strategy capable of controlling the various…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
呂也使朱虛不先入酈寄不可紿勃蓋机
上肉耳既入北軍乃以左袒覘人心之向
背而已從之豈大臣舉動乎唐之中葉安
史跋扈藩鎮陸梁事孔棘矣始郭終裴皆
能以其身爲國家平大難成大功然一則
屢起屢削幾陷於朝恩之手而不免以奢
侈自汙論者每致疑焉一則朋黨作禍幾
中於异鑄之口而僅以浮沉自免何其始
奮而終懦也澶淵之役契丹以屢勝之兵
===
大舉入寇而宋方以承平不知戰之卒應
之使撻覽不斃於流矢而虜縱其驍騎以
撓我師雖準之忠其必能使之隻輪不返
乎孤注之譏良有自也曾雖計去丁謂然
舒徐同朝久而不發幸有山陵一事託之
包藏禍心以去之而其事亦近於設諼謂
之見陷於邢中和天使之也是數君子者
其任天下之事如此其成天下之功如此
其與不尚其事不有其功者孰難而孰易
punctuated: 呂也。使朱虛不先入，酈寄不可紿，勃蓋机上肉耳。既入北軍，乃以左袒覘人心之向背而已從之，豈大臣舉動乎？唐之中葉，安、史跋扈，藩鎮陸梁，事孔棘矣。始郭終裴，皆能以其身爲國家平大難、成大功；然一則屢起屢削，幾陷於朝恩之手，而不免以奢侈自汙，論者每致疑焉；一則朋黨作禍，幾中於异、鑄之口，而僅以浮沉自免，何其始奮而終懦也！澶淵之役，契丹以屢勝之兵，大舉入寇，而宋方以承平不知戰之卒應之。使撻覽不斃於流矢，而虜縱其驍騎以撓我師，雖準之忠，其必能使之隻輪不返乎？「孤注」之譏，良有自也。曾雖計去丁謂，然舒徐同朝，久而不發，幸有山陵一事，託之包藏禍心以去之，而其事亦近於設諼；謂之見陷於邢中和，天使之也。是數君子者，其任天下之事如此，其成天下之功如此，其與不尚其事、不有其功者，孰難而孰易、…
translation_en:
… the Lü clan. Had the Marquis of Zhuxu (Liu Zhang 劉章) not entered the palace beforehand, and had Li Ji 酈寄 not been amenable to deceiving [Lü Lu 呂祿], Zhou Bo 周勃 would probably have been no more than meat on the chopping block. Even after entering the Northern Army, he used the baring of left shoulders to gauge the inclinations of men's hearts and merely followed them—was this the conduct of a great minister?

In the mid-Tang, An Lushan 安祿山 and Shi Siming 史思明 grew domineering and the defense commands ran rampant; affairs were in extreme peril. Beginning with Guo Ziyi 郭子儀 and ending with Pei Du 裴度, both were able to devote themselves to pacifying great crises and achieving great merit for the state. Yet the one was repeatedly raised up and repeatedly stripped of power, nearly falling into the hands of Yu Chao'en 魚朝恩, and could not avoid sullying himself with extravagance—commentators have often raised doubts about this. The other faced the disaster of factionalism, was nearly struck down by the slanders of Cheng Yi 程异 and Huangfu Bo 皇甫鎛 [transcribed 鑄], and barely escaped by drifting along with the times—how resolute at the start, yet how timid at the end!

In the campaign of Chanyuan, the Khitan launched a massive invasion with repeatedly victorious troops, while the Song responded with soldiers who had known only peace and were unfamiliar with war. Had Xiao Dalan 蕭撻覽 not been killed by a stray arrow, and had the enemy loosed their valiant cavalry to harass our forces, even with Kou Zhun's 寇準 loyalty, could he certainly have ensured that not a single wheel of theirs returned? The taunt of "wagering all on a single throw" truly had a basis.

Although Wang Zeng 王曾 schemed to remove Ding Wei 丁謂, he lingered alongside him at court for a long time without acting. Fortunately, there occurred the matter of the imperial mausoleum, which allowed him to accuse Ding of harboring treacherous intentions in order to remove him—yet this affair came close to setting a deceitful trap; that Ding Wei was ensnared through Xing Zhonghe 邢中和 was the doing of Heaven.

That these several gentlemen shouldered the affairs of the empire in such a manner, and accomplished the merits of the empire in such a manner—compared with those who do not exalt their own deeds and do not claim their own merits, which is harder and which is easier, …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
孰大而孰小耶大抵君子之任國家幸而
安常處順則雖無勇功無知名亦奚不可
其或時殊勢拂不得已起而整頓之伸縮
緩急當獨睹乎萬全之計敬圖國家之福
不以吾身居之此則任事而不尚其事立
功而不有其功心乎社稷者之爲也而漢
唐宋之六君子亦已庶幾乎此故以風節
而論則汲直爲高以功名而論則六君子
亦盛未可少也若夫依阿於始事而遘會
===
於偶成乃倖功徼事者之所欲匪惟古之
社稷臣者有所不爲卽六君子之見亦不
出此也抑愚因是而竊有論焉古稱神龍
以其無欲故人莫得而豢之所謂欲者豈
曰富貴有意於立名有心於避害皆是也
究而極之則心有所向念有所倚皆是也
有欲則不神矣惟古之至人萬物一體而
泊然無一物之干其心周於天下而實則
視天下於不與事之未形去健羨絀聰明
punctuated: 孰大而孰小耶？大抵君子之任國家，幸而安常處順，則雖無勇功，無知名，亦奚不可？其或時殊勢拂，不得已起而整頓之，伸縮緩急，當獨睹乎萬全之計，敬圖國家之福，不以吾身居之。此則任事而不尚其事，立功而不有其功，心乎社稷者之爲也，而漢、唐、宋之六君子，亦已庶幾乎此。故以風節而論，則汲直爲高；以功名而論，則六君子亦盛，未可少也。若夫依阿於始事，而遘會於偶成，乃倖功徼事者之所欲，匪惟古之社稷臣者有所不爲，卽六君子之見，亦不出此也。抑愚因是而竊有論焉。古稱神龍，以其無欲，故人莫得而豢之。所謂欲者，豈曰富貴？有意於立名，有心於避害，皆是也；究而極之，則心有所向，念有所倚，皆是也。有欲則不神矣。惟古之至人，萬物一體，而泊然無一物之干其心。周於天下，而實則視天下於不與。事之未形，去健羨，絀聰明，
translation_en:
…and which is greater and which is smaller? On the whole, when a gentleman shoulders responsibility for the state, if by good fortune times are peaceful and circumstances favorable, then even if he achieves no feats of valor and wins no renown, what harm is there in that? Yet if the times change and circumstances turn adverse, so that he has no choice but to rise up and set things in order, in knowing when to advance or retreat and when to act with urgency or deliberation, he should perceive with singular foresight a plan of complete safety, reverently seeking the welfare of the state without claiming the credit for himself. This is to shoulder affairs without exalting one's own deeds, and to establish merit without possessing that merit—the conduct of one whose heart is devoted to the altars of soil and grain. And the six gentlemen of the Han, Tang, and Song already came quite close to this. Therefore, if we speak in terms of moral integrity, then Ji An [Ji Zhi 汲直] stands highest; if we speak in terms of meritorious achievement, then the six gentlemen were also illustrious and must not be disparaged. As for being compliant and equivocal when initiating an affair, and then happening upon success by mere chance, that is what those who court luck for merit and angle for exploits desire; not only would the ministers of the altars of soil and grain of antiquity refuse to do such a thing, even the outlook of the six gentlemen did not stoop to this.

Moreover, on the basis of this, I would humbly offer an observation. Antiquity spoke of the divine dragon as something that no one can tame and rear, because it is without desire. What is called desire—does it refer merely to wealth and rank? Having an intention to establish a name for oneself, or harboring a mind to avoid harm, are both instances of it; pushed to the ultimate extreme, wherever the mind has a leaning or the thoughts have a dependency, all of these are desire. Where there is desire, there is no longer anything divine. Only the consummate men of antiquity formed one body with the myriad things, while remaining tranquil and unperturbed by any single thing impinging upon their minds. Their concern encompassed all under Heaven, yet in reality they regarded all under Heaven with detachment. Before affairs had taken shape, they cast aside restless covetousness and put away cleverness and acuity,…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
似若無所事事及其斷大事排大難不動
聲色而潜消默運於枝經肯綮之中蓋當
其時被其德者曾不知誰之爲功而萬世
之言元功者亦必首之何也無欲故也無
欲則神全神全則氣定氣定則慮審慮審
則注措精而天下之務成矣嗟乎是乾九
二之龍德而伊周之事乎愚生何足以知
之
第三問
===
張潘
同考試官教諭黃批鄉之先哲類能言之獨是
作低昂不爽權衡素定可覘造詣矣
同考試官教授顧批品藻中允有至論幾乎見
道之言也
考試官教授萬批義理精純
考試官教授吳批議論正大
君子之權衡人物也固當求一定之論而
後有以見先正之心尤當審不易之說而
punctuated:
似若無所事事；及其斷大事、排大難，不動聲色，而潜消默運於枝經肯綮之中。蓋當其時，被其德者曾不知誰之爲功，而萬世之言元功者亦必首之。何也？無欲故也。無欲則神全，神全則氣定，氣定則慮審，慮審則注措精，而天下之務成矣。嗟乎！是《乾》九二之龍德，而伊、周之事乎？愚生何足以知之！

第三問

張潘

同考試官教諭黃批：鄉之先哲，類能言之；獨是作低昂不爽，權衡素定，可覘造詣矣。
同考試官教授顧批：品藻中允，有至論，幾乎見道之言也。
考試官教授萬批：義理精純。
考試官教授吳批：議論正大。

君子之權衡人物也，固當求一定之論，而後有以見先正之心；尤當審不易之說，而
translation_en:
…appearing as though he had nothing to attend to. Yet when he decides great affairs and resolves great difficulties, he does not betray a sign on his face or in his voice, quietly dispelling and silently maneuvering them at the vital junctures and crucial points. Indeed, at the time, those who receive his beneficence do not even know whose achievement it is; yet for ten thousand generations, those who speak of supreme merit must place him first. Why is this? Because he is without desire. Being without desire, his spirit is whole; his spirit being whole, his vital energy is settled; his vital energy being settled, his deliberations are thorough; his deliberations being thorough, his measures are precise, and the affairs of the world are accomplished. Alas! Is this not the dragon virtue of the second-nine line of the Qian hexagram, and the undertaking of Yi Yin and the Duke of Zhou? How could this foolish student be worthy of knowing it!

Question Three

Zhang Pan 張潘

Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Huang 黃: Most candidates can speak of the former worthies of this province, but this essay alone weighs their merits without error, showing a long-established standard of judgment by which one may glimpse his scholarly attainment.
Comment by Associate Examiner and Instructor Gu 顧: His appraisals are fair and balanced, containing supreme arguments that nearly reach the words of one who perceives the Way.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wan 萬: The moral principles are refined and pure.
Comment by Examiner and Instructor Wu 吳: The discussion is upright and grand.

When the gentleman weighs and evaluates historical figures, he must certainly seek a settled conclusion before he has the means to perceive the minds of the former worthies; and he must especially examine an immutable doctrine before…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
後可以定後學之準何則人之有生凡其
身之發用孰非性之流行其得之雖有偏
全然亦各有一定之分焉故權衡者必有
一定之論而後方乎人者不爽其得之偏
全由於學之大小要其性之本眞則固自
有不易之體焉故權衡者亦必有不易之
說而後脩諸已者不謬知乎此則可以復
明問矣愚嘗觀
國家興道致治凡二百餘年豪傑挺生含淳
===
披燿彬彬乎盛哉見之四方雖更僕未易
數也而兩浙尤自古所稱文明之區光岳
之氣蜿嬗磅礴往往鍾瑰瑋之材發奇崛
之士今以道學言之章懋王守仁其著也
一則旣博復約而自成一家一則精詣超
悟而直契本體就而論之文成當俗學支
離之餘而功主於致知視文懿學專於脩
行大小誠爲不同然奮然以道自任其志
同也以節義言之方孝孺孫燧其烈也一
punctuated: 後可以定後學之準。何則？人之有生，凡其身之發用，孰非性之流行？其得之雖有偏全，然亦各有一定之分焉。故權衡者，必有一定之論，而後方乎人者不爽。其得之偏全，由於學之大小，要其性之本眞，則固自有不易之體焉。故權衡者，亦必有不易之說，而後脩諸已者不謬。知乎此，則可以復明問矣。愚嘗觀國家興道致治，凡二百餘年，豪傑挺生，含淳披燿，彬彬乎盛哉！見之四方，雖更僕未易數也。而兩浙尤自古所稱文明之區，光岳之氣，蜿嬗磅礴，往往鍾瑰瑋之材，發奇崛之士。今以道學言之，章懋、王守仁其著也。一則旣博復約而自成一家，一則精詣超悟而直契本體。就而論之，文成當俗學支離之餘，而功主於致知，視文懿學專於脩行，大小誠爲不同；然奮然以道自任，其志同也。以節義言之，方孝孺、孫燧其烈也。一
translation_en:
…before he can establish a standard for later scholars. Why is this? Once a person is born, among all the manifestations and functions of his person, which is not the flow of human nature? Although what each attains may be partial or complete, each nevertheless has a fixed allotment. Therefore, one who weighs and evaluates must possess a definitive discourse before his comparisons of others will be free of error. Whether what they attain is partial or complete stems from the greater or lesser scope of their learning; yet in essential terms, the original truth of their nature inherently possesses an unchanging substance. Therefore, one who weighs and evaluates must also possess an unchanging doctrine before his cultivation of himself will be free of fallacy. Understanding this, one can then reply to Your enlightened inquiry.

I have observed that since the Dynasty promoted the Way and brought about orderly rule over more than two hundred years, outstanding figures have stood forth, harbouring purity and displaying brilliance—how resplendent and flourishing! Seen across the four quarters of the realm, even if one changed attendants to keep count, they could not easily be numbered. And Western and Eastern Zhejiang have especially been acclaimed since antiquity as a region of cultural refinement, where the vital ether of celestial lights and sacred peaks winds and surges majestically, time and again concentrating in extraordinary talents and bringing forth remarkable scholars.

Now, to speak of the Learning of the Way (daoxue), Zhang Mao 章懋 and Wang Shouren 王守仁 are the prominent ones. The one proceeded from broad learning back to essential restraint, establishing a school of his own; the other achieved refined mastery and transcendent awakening, directly grasping the original substance. If we examine and discuss them closely: Wencheng 文成 [Wang Shouren], coming in the wake of the fragmented vulgar learning of his day, centered his effort on extending innate knowledge; compared to Wenyi 文懿 [Zhang Mao], whose learning focused on cultivating conduct, their greater and lesser scopes were truly different. Yet in rousing themselves to take the Way as their personal responsibility, their aspiration was the same.

To speak of moral integrity and righteousness, Fang Xiaoru 方孝孺 and Sun Sui 孫燧 are the heroic ones. The one…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
則誓死不移抗靖難之師一則挺身不屈
奪宸濠之魄就而論之寧海值大命改革
之後而徇主於旣衰視忠烈徇國於方盛
難易亦似有間然毅然以節自完其忠同
也語勳業則有劉基章溢其人焉學爲帝
師才稱王佐殱吳漢定中原占步如神謀
畫命中巍乎名世之英也青田之勳業其
尤偉乎而起身儒家父子宣力平寇之功
不減諸將則龍泉者亦青田之流亞哉語
===
詞章則有宋濂王禕其人焉口無毁言身
無飾行記
聖政纂
日曆禮樂
律令裁定居多燁乎經世之章也浦江之詞
翰其尤醇乎而史事擅長力任筆削才思
之雄克當
上心則義烏者亦浦江之儔匹哉之數公者其
品格雖殊而其有關於氣運有裨於民彝
punctuated: 則誓死不移，抗靖難之師；一則挺身不屈，奪宸濠之魄。就而論之，寧海值大命改革之後，而徇主於旣衰；視忠烈徇國於方盛，難易亦似有間，然毅然以節自完，其忠同也。語勳業，則有劉基、章溢其人焉。學爲帝師，才稱王佐，殱吳、漢，定中原，占步如神，謀畫命中，巍乎名世之英也，青田之勳業其尤偉乎！而起身儒家，父子宣力，平寇之功不減諸將，則龍泉者亦青田之流亞哉！語詞章，則有宋濂、王禕其人焉。口無毁言，身無飾行，記聖政，纂日曆，禮樂、律令，裁定居多，燁乎經世之章也，浦江之詞翰其尤醇乎！而史事擅長，力任筆削，才思之雄克當上心，則義烏者亦浦江之儔匹哉！之數公者，其品格雖殊，而其有關於氣運、有裨於民彝
translation_en:
… swore to the death not to waver, resisting the campaign to Clear Away Disorders; the other stood forth unyielding, striking terror into the soul of Chenhao 朱宸濠. If we examine and discuss them closely: Master Ninghai [Fang Xiaoru 方孝孺] encountered a time after the Great Mandate had shifted, and died for his ruler when the cause had already declined; compared with Master Zhonglie [Sun Sui 孫燧], who died for the dynasty when it was at its height, the difficulty of their circumstances may seem to differ, yet in resolutely preserving their integrity to the end, their loyalty was the same.

If we speak of meritorious achievements, there were men such as Liu Ji 劉基 and Zhang Yi 章溢. With learning worthy of an imperial preceptor and talent befitting a kingly counselor, he annihilated the rival states of Wu and Han, pacified the Central Plains, practiced divination and astrological calculation as if with divine prescience, and devised strategies that unerringly hit the mark—how lofty, a hero renowned in his generation! The meritorious achievements of Master Qingtian [Liu Ji] were especially magnificent! And rising from a Confucian family, with father and son exerting their strength to the utmost, his achievements in pacifying bandits were no less than those of the military commanders—thus Master Longquan [Zhang Yi] was indeed a worthy second to Qingtian!

If we speak of literary composition, there were men such as Song Lian 宋濂 and Wang Yi 王禕. With no slanderous words in his mouth and no affected conduct in his person, he recorded the Sacred Governance (Shengzheng記), compiled the Daily Records (Rili 日曆), and had a leading hand in determining rites, music, statutes, and ordinances—how resplendent, writings for ordering the world! The literary works of Master Pujiang [Song Lian] were especially pure! And excelling in historical scholarship, vigorously taking up the work of compilation and revision, with a boldness of talent and thought capable of satisfying the sovereign's mind—Master Yiwu [Wang Yi] was indeed the peer and equal of Pujiang!

As for these several gentlemen, although their personal qualities differed, in their bearing upon the destiny of the age and their benefit to the moral norms of the people …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
者則一其造就雖異而其發之於本心原
之於本性者則同譬之八音並奏於周廟
雖必有所重而缺一有所不可也譬之四
科並列於孔庭雖獨有所先而廢一亦有
所不可也斯固不特可稱浙產即往牒所
紀名卿材大夫何以加焉夫道德也節義
也勳業也詞章也四者得其一亦足以表
見而自立於天下迺昔人獨許文成能兼
之以爲除却講學便是完人而文成之自
===
許則又願盡捐三者而獨從事於講學以
毋愧完人此世之論者因有遺棄事物之
疑而從祀之議至今紛紛不决也愚竊以
爲不然道一而已學一而已離心性而求
事物則所爲措之事物者果何物耶離事
物而求心性則所爲具之心性者又何物
耶皐夔稷契師師相讓無節義可見而不
以其故貶聖孔子孟軻終身不一遇無勳
業可紀而不以其故讓德顏子終日默默
punctuated:
者則一；其造就雖異，而其發之於本心、原之於本性者則同。譬之八音並奏於周廟，雖必有所重，而缺一有所不可也；譬之四科並列於孔庭，雖獨有所先，而廢一亦有所不可也。斯固不特可稱浙產，即往牒所紀名卿材大夫，何以加焉！

夫道德也、節義也、勳業也、詞章也，四者得其一，亦足以表見而自立於天下。迺昔人獨許文成能兼之，以爲「除却講學，便是完人」；而文成之自許，則又願盡捐三者，而獨從事於講學，以毋愧完人。此世之論者因有遺棄事物之疑，而從祀之議至今紛紛不决也。愚竊以爲不然。道一而已，學一而已。離心性而求事物，則所爲措之事物者果何物耶？離事物而求心性，則所爲具之心性者又何物耶？皐、夔、稷、契師師相讓，無節義可見，而不以其故貶聖；孔子、孟軻終身不一遇，無勳業可紀，而不以其故讓德；顏子終日默默，
translation_en:
… are one and the same; although their attainments differed, that they sprang from the original mind and originated in the fundamental nature was identical. It is like the eight musical tones played together in the ancestral temple of Zhou: though some must take precedence, not one of them can be dispensed with; it is like the four fields of study ranked side by side in the courtyard of Confucius: though one alone comes first, not a single one can be discarded either. Truly, they may not only be praised as native sons of Zhejiang; even the renowned ministers and talented grandees recorded in past annals—how could they surpass them?

Now as for moral virtue (daode), integrity and righteousness (jieyi), meritorious achievement (xunye), and literary composition (cizhang): attaining even one of these four is sufficient for a man to distinguish himself and stand on his own in the world. Yet people of the past uniquely credited Wencheng [Wang Yangming 王陽明, posthumous title Wencheng 文成] with encompassing all of them, holding that "setting aside his philosophical lecturing (jiangxue), he was a complete man." What Wencheng aspired to for himself, however, was to cast aside the other three altogether and devote himself solely to philosophical learning, so as not to fall short of being a complete man. Because of this, critics in the world have harbored the suspicion that he abandoned practical affairs, and the debate over his enshrinement in the Confucian temple remains divided and unresolved to this day. I venture to disagree. The Way is one and only one; learning is one and only one. If one separates from mind and nature to seek practical affairs, then what is it that one applies to practical affairs? And if one separates from practical affairs to seek mind and nature, then what is it that is embodied within mind and nature? Gao Yao 皋陶, Kui 夔, Hou Ji 后稷, and Xie 契 deferentially yielded to one another in court, with no martyrdom of integrity and righteousness to be seen, yet they were not diminished in sageliness on that account; Confucius 孔子 and Mencius (Meng Ke 孟軻) never once met with an opportune ruler in their entire lives, with no meritorious achievements to be recorded, yet they did not yield in virtue on that account; Master Yan [Yan Hui 顏回] remained silent all day long …

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
如愚人無詞章可述而不以其故損賢是
非以三者爲不足務也三者皆道德之緒
餘而心性之流行也學而得其本心安常
履順可也成仁取義可也節義皆道德而
不以節義名也尸居淵默可也叅賛位育
可也勳業皆道德而不以勳業名也忘言
可也卽以其所自得者發揮纂述無不可
也詞章皆道德而不以詞章名也文成之
學始之詞章繼之仙釋終而志於孔孟之
===
傳凡三變矣自龍塲衡困之後超然有悟
於良知之旨不落言詮不涉玄解萬事萬
物之理莫非具足于本心而非有所待於
其外學問思辯之功莫非求全其本心而
非有所倚於其內知行合一動靜無間是
豈遺棄事物而爲一切空虛之談者以故
學日益茂造日益深四方之開發日益衆
今觀其平生忤權璫而不懾處危疑而不
亂節何堅也靖宸濠方張之難平思田累
punctuated: 如愚人，無詞章可述，而不以其故損賢。是非以三者爲不足務也，三者皆道德之緒餘而心性之流行也。學而得其本心，安常履順可也，成仁取義可也，節義皆道德而不以節義名也；尸居淵默可也，叅賛位育可也，勳業皆道德而不以勳業名也；忘言可也，卽以其所自得者發揮纂述無不可也，詞章皆道德而不以詞章名也。文成之學，始之詞章，繼之仙釋，終而志於孔孟之傳，凡三變矣。自龍塲衡困之後，超然有悟於良知之旨，不落言詮，不涉玄解。萬事萬物之理，莫非具足于本心，而非有所待於其外；學問思辯之功，莫非求全其本心，而非有所倚於其內。知行合一，動靜無間，是豈遺棄事物而爲一切空虛之談者？以故學日益茂，造日益深，四方之開發日益衆。今觀其平生，忤權璫而不懾，處危疑而不亂，節何堅也！靖宸濠方張之難，平思田累
translation_en:
… like a foolish person, with no literary compositions to recount, yet his worthiness is not diminished on that account. This is not because these three things [moral integrity, meritorious achievement, and literary composition] are deemed unworthy of pursuit; rather, all three are the surplus threads of the Way and its Virtue, and the natural outflow of the mind and human nature. When through learning one attains one's original mind, one may abide in normal and smooth circumstances, or one may die to achieve humanity and lay down one's life for righteousness—moral integrity is altogether the Way and its Virtue, without being famed merely as moral integrity; one may sit motionless like a ritual personator and remain silent as an abyss, or one may assist in the transforming and nourishing powers of Heaven and Earth so that all things attain their proper place and flourish—meritorious achievement is altogether the Way and its Virtue, without being famed merely as meritorious achievement; one may forget words, or one may expound and compile on the basis of what one has personally realized—literary composition is altogether the Way and its Virtue, without being famed merely as literary composition.

The learning of Wencheng [Wang Shouren 王守仁, posthumous title Wencheng 文成] began with literary composition, continued with Daoist immortality and Buddhism, and finally fixed its ambition upon the transmission of Confucius and Mencius, undergoing three transformations in all. After suffering adversity and distress at Longchang, he achieved a transcendent awakening to the essential meaning of innate knowledge (liangzhi 良知), neither falling into verbal explanations nor straying into abstruse interpretations. The principles of the myriad affairs and myriad things are without exception fully present in the original mind, without depending on anything external to it; the effort of studying, questioning, reflecting, and sifting is without exception a quest to keep one's original mind whole, without leaning upon anything internal to it. Knowledge and action are united as one, and activity and tranquillity are without gap—how could this be abandoning affairs and things to engage in utterly empty and hollow talk? For this reason, his learning grew ever more luxuriant, his attainment ever deeper, and those enlightened and inspired by him in all quarters grew ever more numerous. Now, if we examine his whole life: he defied a powerful eunuch [Liu Jin 劉瑾] without fear and stood amid peril and suspicion without confusion—how firm was his integrity! He quelled the newly surging rebellion of Chenhao [Zhu Chenhao 朱宸濠, Prince of Ning] and pacified thebandits of Sien and Tianzhou who had lasted for generations…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
世之寇勳何烈也談性命則發前人之所
未發闡時事則兼文士之所難兼詞章何
富也果何所本而得之者耶假令文成遺
棄事物則此三者果空虛無當者之所能
辦哉彼其願舍此而獨有所從良有見於
一貫之體也方今
聖天子在上
睿知夙成
遜志務學眞萬世治統道統之會賢公卿德
===
業日茂同心輔世方將啓學者以悟性脩
行之眞卽以文成而列之俎豆之末于以
示體用具備之學于以爲
聖世立敎之助不亦偉歟且
國朝治化隆熙道術齊一薛文清崛起於宋
儒之後以正學敎河汾而北方之學以盛
王文成又崛起於文清之後以正學敎江
浙而南方之學亦盛是二賢者心行一致
先後同功者也今以文成列於文清之次
punctuated: 世之寇，勳何烈也！談性命則發前人之所未發，闡時事則兼文士之所難兼，詞章何富也！果何所本而得之者耶？假令文成遺棄事物，則此三者，果空虛無當者之所能辦哉？彼其願舍此而獨有所從，良有見於一貫之體也。方今聖天子在上，睿知夙成，遜志務學，眞萬世治統、道統之會。賢公卿德業日茂，同心輔世，方將啓學者以悟性脩行之眞。卽以文成而列之俎豆之末，于以示體用具備之學，于以爲聖世立敎之助，不亦偉歟！且國朝治化隆熙，道術齊一，薛文清崛起於宋儒之後，以正學敎河、汾，而北方之學以盛；王文成又崛起於文清之後，以正學敎江、浙，而南方之學亦盛。是二賢者，心行一致，先後同功者也。今以文成列於文清之次，
translation_en:
… [pacifying the] bandits of successive generations [in Si'en and Tianzhou]—how illustrious were his meritorious achievements! When discussing human nature and destiny, he brought to light what predecessors had never expressed; when expounding on current affairs, he combined skills that literary men find difficult to unite—how rich were his writings! On what basis, indeed, did he attain all this? Supposing Wencheng [Wang Yangming 王陽明, canonized as Wencheng 文成] had abandoned affairs and things, could these three achievements truly have been managed by someone given to emptiness and impropriety? That he was willing to set those aside and follow a singular path was truly because he had insight into the substance of the single thread running through all things.

Right now, the Sacred Son of Heaven reigns above, his sagely wisdom early matured, humbling his will to devote himself to learning—truly the convergence of the succession of governance and the succession of the Way for ten thousand generations. Worthy dukes and ministers see their virtuous achievements flourish daily, assisting the world with one heart, and are just about to enlighten scholars in the truth of realizing human nature and cultivating conduct. If Wencheng is forthwith placed at the end of the sacrificial vessels [in the Confucian Temple], thereby demonstrating a learning complete in both substance and function, and thereby serving as an aid to establishing instruction in this sacred era, would it not be magnificent!

Moreover, our dynasty's governance and transformative influence are prosperous and bright, and its scholarly arts of the Way are unified. Xue Wenqing [Xue Xuan 薛瑄, canonized as Wenqing 文清] rose prominently after the Song Confucians, teaching orthodox learning in the Yellow River and Fen River region, whereby northern scholarship flourished. Wang Wencheng in turn rose prominently after Wenqing, teaching orthodox learning in the Jiangnan and Zhejiang regions, whereby southern scholarship also flourished. These two worthies were unified in mind and conduct, achieving the same merit one after the other. Now, to place Wencheng next to Wenqing…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
正有符於國故有合之義益可以彰
聖世作人之功不亦盛哉此公論之所共歸而
清朝之所當亟舉者也執事之問意者其亦
有見於此乎審於一定之論而諸賢之所
成者不泯其盛究其不易之說而後學之
所趣者得有所準執事之問意者其亦有
在於此乎愚生浙人也高山仰止景行行
止其於八君子者莫不懷願學之心然勳
業未可預期節義出於所遇文章則又發
===
於所性乃所願者從事道學而已乎道學
之士世所共訾皆贋者起之此贋者之過
非學之過也以文成之實心體文成之實
學愼之於無聲無臭之眞驗之於有體有
用之際此則效法先民以求自立於天地
者執事其許之乎
第四問
王士崧
同考試官敎諭秦批寬猛相濟自昔聞之乃用
punctuated:
正有符於國故有合之義，益可以彰聖世作人之功，不亦盛哉！此公論之所共歸，而清朝之所當亟舉者也。執事之問，意者其亦有見於此乎？審於一定之論，而諸賢之所成者不泯其盛；究其不易之說，而後學之所趣者得有所準。執事之問，意者其亦有在於此乎？愚生，浙人也。「高山仰止，景行行止」，其於八君子者，莫不懷願學之心。然勳業未可預期，節義出於所遇，文章則又發於所性，乃所願者，從事道學而已乎！道學之士，世所共訾，皆贋者起之，此贋者之過，非學之過也。以文成之實心，體文成之實學，愼之於無聲無臭之眞，驗之於有體有用之際，此則效法先民以求自立於天地者，執事其許之乎？

第四問
王士崧
同考試官敎諭秦批：寬猛相濟，自昔聞之，乃用
translation_en:
… precisely accords with the principle of combining pairs in our dynastic precedents, and can all the more manifest the achievement of our Sacred Age in cultivating men of talent—is it not magnificent! This is where public opinion universally converges, and what our Pure Court ought urgently to enact. In asking your question, sir, could it be that you also had this in mind? By examining the settled judgments, the flourishing achievements of the various worthies will not be obscured; by investigating the immutable doctrines, the direction toward which later scholars aspire will have a standard to follow. In asking your question, sir, could it be that your intention also lay here? I, a foolish student, am a native of Zhejiang. "The high mountain I look up to; the great road I travel along"—toward those eight noble men, there is none whom I do not cherish a wish to emulate. Yet meritorious deeds cannot be anticipated in advance, fidelity and righteousness arise from the circumstances one encounters, and literary composition issues from one's inborn nature; what I truly wish for, then, is simply to devote myself to the Learning of the Way! That scholars of the Learning of the Way are universally disparaged by the world is entirely provoked by counterfeit practitioners; this is the fault of the counterfeits, not the fault of the learning itself. With the sincere mind of Wencheng (Wang Shouren 王守仁), to embody the practical learning of Wencheng—being watchful over the truth that is without sound or odor, and verifying it in the realm where substance and function are both present—this is how I seek to model myself on the worthy predecessors so as to establish myself between Heaven and Earth. Will you, sir, grant your approval to this?

Fourth Policy Question
Wang Shisong 王士崧
