title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
之多有蹠盭是作得歸一之論可執此以從政矣
考試官敎授萬批深得吏治之宜
考試官敎授吳批用世之學
君子之論治也固必達於其用尤必明於
其本何謂本存之於心與物爲體克寬克
仁倂包而兼容者是也何謂用施之於政
與時咸宜可張可弛迭運而不窮者是也
然必有與物爲體之心然後有與時咸宜
之用故其闔闢操縱之權至於不可勝窮
===
而其本之寬者卒未之有易焉此論治之
準也執事以吏治寬猛策諸生豈以諸生
中有通於治理者乎愚非其人也雖然試
言之在昔唐虞三代莫不以寬仁治天下
不聞以猛也吾夫子論治載在論語中曰
寬曰不猛不聞以寬與猛對舉言之也自
寬猛之說記之左氏而後之儒者宗焉愚
則竊有疑之夫學者載籍雖博猶考信於
六藝云今天下所家傳而人誦者非魯論耶
punctuated:
之多有蹠盭。是作得歸一之論，可執此以從政矣。
考試官敎授萬批：深得吏治之宜。
考試官敎授吳批：用世之學。
君子之論治也，固必達於其用，尤必明於其本。何謂本？存之於心，與物爲體，克寬克仁，倂包而兼容者是也。何謂用？施之於政，與時咸宜，可張可弛，迭運而不窮者是也。然必有與物爲體之心，然後有與時咸宜之用。故其闔闢操縱之權，至於不可勝窮，而其本之寬者，卒未之有易焉。此論治之準也。
執事以吏治寬猛策諸生，豈以諸生中有通於治理者乎？愚非其人也。雖然，試言之。在昔唐、虞、三代，莫不以寬仁治天下，不聞以猛也。吾夫子論治，載在《論語》中，曰「寬」、曰「不猛」，不聞以寬與猛對舉言之也。自寬猛之說記之左氏，而後之儒者宗焉，愚則竊有疑之。夫學者載籍雖博，猶考信於六藝云。今天下所家傳而人誦者，非《魯論》耶？
translation_en:
… putting it into practice there are often perverse contradictions. This essay arrives at a unified argument; one may hold to this to engage in governance.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wan comments: Deeply grasps what is appropriate in administrative governance.
Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wu comments: Learning of practical use to the world.
When a gentleman discusses governance, while he must certainly comprehend its practical application, he must above all be clear about its fundamental root. What is meant by the root? Retaining it in the mind so as to form one body with all things, being capable of leniency and benevolence, embracing all and tolerating all—this is it. What is meant by practical application? Putting it into effect in administration so that it is always suited to the times, able to be either tightened or relaxed, alternating in operation without exhaustion—this is it. Yet only when one possesses a mind that forms one body with all things can one achieve a practical application that is suited to the times. Therefore, though the discretionary power of closing and opening, tightening and slackening, reaches inexhaustible variations, its root of leniency is ultimately never altered. This is the standard for discussing governance.
Your Excellency has presented the candidates with a policy question on leniency and severity in administrative governance; could it be that You believe there is someone among the candidates who thoroughly understands the principles of governance? Stupid as I am, I am not that person. Even so, let me venture to speak of it. In antiquity, during the Tang, Yu, and Three Dynasties, none failed to govern All-under-Heaven through leniency and benevolence; one does not hear of their doing so through severity. Our Master's discussions of governance, as recorded in the Analects (Lunyu), speak of "leniency" and of "not being severe"; one does not hear of his speaking of leniency and severity as paired counterparts. Ever since the doctrine of leniency and severity was recorded by Mr. Zuo [in the Zuo Tradition (Zuozhuan)], later Confucians have revered it as authoritative; yet I, in my humble opinion, harbour doubts about it. As it is said, although a scholar's reading of records be wide, he still verifies their credibility against the Six Classics. Now, is not that which every family transmits and every person recites throughout the realm today the Lu Analects (Lu Lun)?

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
假令寛不可無猛而聖人者獨以寛訓是
驅天下以慢也且以左語評之其言一寛
一猛似矣然其寛也勢且無猛而其猛也
勢且無寛寛也猛也如夏之葛冬之裘聖
人不覩其偏勝之勢而必立爲偏勝之法
何也執事所謂平中之治寧無出于寛猛
之外者是已其言寛猛相濟似矣然其濟
寛也而猛又將殘其濟猛也而寛又將慢
慢也殘也如水之必溺而火之必焚聖人
輒濟之而輒復病之何也執事所謂慢殘
之弊又有乘於寛猛之中者是已三代而
還漢吏治近古以漢事喻之黃霸之守潁
川也繼韓延壽也延壽尚禮教而霸承之
以寛和今考其政左刑罰右教化孝弟貞
義翕然成俗如璽書所云於王道近似焉
是以寛濟寛也而潁川治則安在乎寛之
後必猛也趙廣漢尹京兆以威嚴尹如霸
承之以平易夫京兆非他郡邑比也乃畿
punctuated: 假令寛不可無猛，而聖人者獨以寛訓，是驅天下以慢也。且以《左》語評之，其言「一寛一猛」，似矣；然其寛也，勢且無猛，而其猛也，勢且無寛。寛也、猛也，如夏之葛、冬之裘，聖人不覩其偏勝之勢，而必立爲偏勝之法，何也？執事所謂「平中之治，寧無出于寛猛之外」者，是已。其言「寛猛相濟」，似矣；然其濟寛也，而猛又將殘，其濟猛也，而寛又將慢。慢也、殘也，如水之必溺而火之必焚，聖人輒濟之而輒復病之，何也？執事所謂「慢殘之弊，又有乘於寛猛之中」者，是已。三代而還，漢吏治近古，以漢事喻之：黃霸之守潁川也，繼韓延壽也。延壽尚禮教，而霸承之以寛和。今考其政，左刑罰、右教化，孝弟貞義翕然成俗，如璽書所云，於王道近似焉。是以寛濟寛也，而潁川治，則安在乎寛之後必猛也？趙廣漢尹京兆以威嚴，尹如霸承之以平易。夫京兆非他郡邑比也，乃畿
translation_en: Suppose leniency cannot do without severity, yet the Sage taught only leniency—that would be driving the world into laxity! Moreover, if we evaluate the words of the Zuo Tradition (Zuo zhuan): its statement of "first leniency, then severity" seems plausible; yet when there is leniency, the tendency is that there will be no severity, and when there is severity, the tendency is that there will be no leniency. Leniency and severity are like kudzu cloth in summer and fur garments in winter: why would the Sage not foresee their tendency toward one-sided dominance, and yet insist on establishing a method of one-sided dominance? What Your Excellency referred to as "could there not be a balanced and moderate governance that transcends leniency and severity?" is precisely this. Its statement that "leniency and severity complement each other" seems plausible; yet when one complements leniency, severity will in turn lead to cruelty, and when one complements severity, leniency will in turn lead to laxity. Laxity and cruelty are like water inevitably drowning and fire inevitably burning: why would the Sage repeatedly complement them only to repeatedly suffer their ills again? What Your Excellency referred to as "the abuses of laxity and cruelty again take advantage from within leniency and severity" is precisely this. Since the Three Dynasties, the administration of officials in the Han dynasty was closest to antiquity. Let us illustrate this with Han affairs: When Huang Ba 黃霸 served as Grand Administrator of Yingchuan 潁川, he succeeded Han Yanshou 韓延壽. Yanshou esteemed ritual and moral instruction, and Ba followed him with leniency and harmony. Now, examining his governance, he relegated punishments and penalties to a secondary place and prioritized moral transformation; filial piety, fraternal duty, chastity, and righteousness harmoniously became the custom, and as the imperial letter with the grand seal stated, it closely approximated the Kingly Way. This was complementing leniency with leniency, and Yingchuan was well-governed—so where is the necessity that severity must follow leniency? Zhao Guanghan 趙廣漢 governed as Metropolitan Commandant of Jingzhao 京兆 with awe-inspiring strictness, and a Metropolitan Commandant like Ba [i.e., Huang Ba] succeeded him with plainness and ease. Now, Jingzhao is not comparable to other commanderies and districts; it is the metropolitan…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
輔之地而四方姦豪所輻輳而棼雜者也
螟賊不除禾將蠹焉棘刺不刈圃將蕪焉
而尹也一切姑息之是以寬濟猛也而京
兆不治則安在乎猛之後必寬也推之事
理則無當驗之往昔則罔效蓋左氏託孔
子以申其說而許魯齋氏又以爲孔子而
不易之也此愚之復明問所以斷其非確
論也然孔門論寬之旨執事所謂微而廣
者愚請旁引而極論之可乎天之於物也
===
即至纖至悉有一不在其兼覆之中者乎
滋之雨露震之雷霆凡以育物也而其兼
覆者未巳也父之於子也即至愚不肖有
一不在其兼愛之中者乎喜則撫摩之怒
則教笞之凡以育子也而其兼愛者未巳
也君子任民物之寄體天地之心廓父母
之愛欲惡以民休戚若巳匹夫匹婦咸欲
自盡是所謂寬也是治道之本原也而事
以時異政與勢遷則亦視其所宜而善其
punctuated: 輔之地，而四方姦豪所輻輳而棼雜者也。螟賊不除，禾將蠹焉；棘刺不刈，圃將蕪焉。而尹也一切姑息之，是以寬濟猛也，而京兆不治，則安在乎猛之後必寬也？推之事理則無當，驗之往昔則罔效，蓋左氏託孔子以申其說，而許魯齋氏又以爲孔子而不易之也。此愚之復明問，所以斷其非確論也。然孔門論寬之旨，執事所謂微而廣者，愚請旁引而極論之，可乎？天之於物也，即至纖至悉，有一不在其兼覆之中者乎？滋之雨露，震之雷霆，凡以育物也，而其兼覆者未巳也。父之於子也，即至愚不肖，有一不在其兼愛之中者乎？喜則撫摩之，怒則教笞之，凡以育子也，而其兼愛者未巳也。君子任民物之寄，體天地之心，廓父母之愛，欲惡以民，休戚若巳，匹夫匹婦咸欲自盡，是所謂寬也，是治道之本原也。而事以時異，政與勢遷，則亦視其所宜而善其
translation_en:
…the metropolitan region, where treacherous and overbearing elements from all quarters converged and mingled in confusion. If borers and pests are not eradicated, the grain will be ruined by them; if thorns and brambles are not cut down, the garden will become overgrown with weeds. Yet as Governor, he indulged them across the board. This was tempering severity with leniency, and yet the Capital Prefecture was not well governed—so where is the proof that severity must necessarily be followed by leniency? Examined in light of the principles of affairs, it is unfounded; tested against the past, it proves ineffective. In truth, Master Zuo (Zuo Qiuming 左丘明) attributed these words to Confucius (Kongzi 孔子) to advance his own theory, and Master Xu Luzhai (Xu Heng 許衡) in turn took them to be Confucius's own and therefore did not alter them. This is why, in replying to your enlightened question, I judge it not to be a definitive argument.

Nevertheless, regarding the purport of the Confucian school's discussions of leniency—which Your Excellency describes as subtle and broad—may I be permitted to draw upon wider analogies and discuss it to the fullest? In Heaven's relation to the myriad things, even down to the most minute and trivial, is there a single one not encompassed within its shelter? It nourishes them with rain and dew and shakes them with thunderbolts; all of this is in order to nurture things, and its all-encompassing shelter never ceases. In a father's relation to his sons, even down to the most foolish and unworthy, is there a single one not encompassed within his love? When pleased, he caresses them; when angry, he instructs and flogs them; all of this is in order to nurture his sons, and his all-encompassing love never ceases. The gentleman, entrusted with responsibility for the people and things, embodies the mind of Heaven and Earth and enlarges the love of parents. He shares the desires and aversions of the people and regards their joys and sorrows as his own, wishing that every common man and woman might fulfill their nature to the utmost. This is what is meant by leniency, and this is the fundamental source of the way of governance. Yet as affairs differ with the times and governance shifts with circumstances, one must also observe what is appropriate and skillfully adapt its…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
用於不窮宜于休養則休養施舍已責緩
刑恤獄衣食其饑寒而拊循其疾苦所以
雨露之撫摩之者也與天下休息也寬之
用也宜于振刷則振刷祛姦剔蠹詰暴緝
頑懲其不恪而兵其不恭所以雷霆之教
笞之者也與天下更始也亦寬之用也天
以兼覆爲心故滋者不得不滋震者不得
不震父以兼愛爲心故喜者不得不喜怒
者不得不怒君子以與物爲體爲心故休
===
養不得不休養振刷不得不振刷其休養
也非有心于惠其振刷也非有心于威率
吾與物爲體之心以流通之而其用自有
所不能已也自本原之義不明而一體之
意寖乖譚治者不寬則猛譚寬猛者不姑
息則操切姑息爲寬其究也網漏于吞舟
患成于舍豺治體日褻于上而民瘼日積
于下譬之人之患癰疽者袖手而待其潰
也此寬之害也非所謂寬者也以此言寬
punctuated: 用於不窮。宜于休養則休養，施舍已責，緩刑恤獄，衣食其饑寒，而拊循其疾苦，所以雨露之、撫摩之者也，與天下休息也，寬之用也；宜于振刷則振刷，祛姦剔蠹，詰暴緝頑，懲其不恪，而兵其不恭，所以雷霆之、教笞之者也，與天下更始也，亦寬之用也。天以兼覆爲心，故滋者不得不滋，震者不得不震；父以兼愛爲心，故喜者不得不喜，怒者不得不怒；君子以與物爲體爲心，故休養不得不休養，振刷不得不振刷。其休養也，非有心于惠；其振刷也，非有心于威。率吾與物爲體之心以流通之，而其用自有所不能已也。自本原之義不明，而一體之意寖乖，譚治者不寬則猛，譚寬猛者不姑息則操切。姑息爲寬，其究也網漏于吞舟，患成于舍豺，治體日褻于上，而民瘼日積于下，譬之人之患癰疽者，袖手而待其潰也。此寬之害也，非所謂寬者也。以此言寬，
translation_en: …application without exhaustion. When circumstances call for rest and nourishment, one rests and nourishes them: bestowing relief and remitting debts, relaxing punishments and showing compassion in criminal cases, clothing and feeding the hungry and cold, and comforting the sick and suffering. This is how one moistens them with rain and dew and strokes them with care, giving the realm rest—it is the functioning of leniency. When circumstances call for invigoration and reform, one invigorates and reforms them: expelling the wicked and rooting out parasites, prosecuting the violent and apprehending the recalcitrant, punishing the negligent, and taking up arms against the irreverent. This is how one shakes them with thunderbolts and disciplines them with the rod, making a fresh start with the realm—and it, too, is the functioning of leniency. Heaven takes universal shelter as its mind, and so where it must nourish, it cannot but nourish, and where it must shake, it cannot but shake. A father takes universal love as his mind, and so where he must be pleased, he cannot but be pleased, and where he must be angry, he cannot but be angry. The gentleman takes forming one body with all things as his mind, and so where he must rest and nourish, he cannot but rest and nourish, and where he must invigorate and reform, he cannot but invigorate and reform. In resting and nourishing, he has no deliberate intention of showing favor; in invigorating and reforming, he has no deliberate intention of displaying severity. He simply follows his mind that forms one body with all things and lets it flow forth, so that its functioning naturally cannot be stopped. Ever since the meaning of this fundamental source became obscured and the sense of forming a single body gradually went awry, those who discuss governance lean either toward leniency or toward severity, and those who discuss leniency and severity understand them either as lax indulgence or as harsh urgency. When lax indulgence is taken for leniency, in the end the net lets slip fishes large enough to swallow a boat, and disaster comes to pass from sparing ravenous wolves; the dignity of governance is daily profaned above, while the sufferings of the people daily accumulate below. It is like a person afflicted with a carbuncle or ulcer who folds his hands in his sleeves and waits for it to burst. This is the harm of leniency, not what is truly called leniency. To speak of leniency in this way…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
宜不免於左氏之慢也操切爲嚴其究也
鳥亂于畢弋魚亂于網罟萬民莫必其命
而四境不安其生譬之人無故而投之硝
黃以潰其腹心此寬之反也非所謂濟寬
者也以此濟寬宜不免於左氏之殘也遡
帝王致理之原察聖人論治之旨正左氏
傳經之訛考漢吏得失之跡寬也者果與
猛對舉之者耶抑寬其本耶嗟夫諸家之
論者何其紛紛也尚寬如理繩張絃之說
===
尚嚴如粱肉藥石之說彼此相勝迄無定
據其最調停參和者曰寬以待良民嚴以
馭姦民是吾以姦民之心逆吾民也曰撫
民當寬馭吏當嚴是吾以黠吏之心棄吾
吏也曰始嚴而終寬是又夏葛而冬裘不
相能者也是皆重於悖左氏而輕於信聖
言愚未敢以爲定据也蓋嘗論之吏治之
得失其大端不出於姑息操切之間而其
大本惟在於心術之微夫人誠有寬大之
punctuated: 宜不免於左氏之慢也。操切爲嚴，其究也，鳥亂于畢弋，魚亂于網罟，萬民莫必其命，而四境不安其生，譬之人無故而投之硝黃以潰其腹心，此寬之反也，非所謂濟寬者也。以此濟寬，宜不免於左氏之殘也。遡帝王致理之原，察聖人論治之旨，正左氏傳經之訛，考漢吏得失之跡，寬也者，果與猛對舉之者耶？抑寬其本耶？嗟夫！諸家之論者何其紛紛也！尚寬如理繩張絃之說，尚嚴如粱肉藥石之說，彼此相勝，迄無定據。其最調停參和者，曰：「寬以待良民，嚴以馭姦民。」是吾以姦民之心逆吾民也。曰：「撫民當寬，馭吏當嚴。」是吾以黠吏之心棄吾吏也。曰：「始嚴而終寬。」是又夏葛而冬裘，不相能者也。是皆重於悖左氏而輕於信聖言，愚未敢以爲定据也。蓋嘗論之，吏治之得失，其大端不出於姑息、操切之間，而其大本惟在於心術之微。夫人誠有寬大之
translation_en: …it fittingly cannot escape what Master Zuo (Zuo Qiuming 左丘明) called negligence. Taking harsh urgency as strictness, in the end, birds are thrown into chaos by hand-nets and corded arrows, fish are thrown into chaos by nets and traps, the myriad people cannot be sure of their lives, and the four borders cannot rest secure in their livelihoods. It is like a person who, for no reason, is dosed with saltpeter and rhubarb to ruin his belly and heart. This is the opposite of leniency, not what is meant by complementing leniency. Using this to complement leniency fittingly cannot escape what Master Zuo called cruelty. Tracing back to the origin of how emperors and kings achieved order, examining the purport of how the sages discussed governance, correcting the errors in Master Zuo's transmission of the Classics, and investigating the traces of the successes and failures of Han officials: is leniency truly something raised as an equal counterpart to severity? Or is leniency the foundation? Alas, how confused and numerous are the arguments of the various schools! Those who prize leniency offer analogies like untangling a cord or tuning a string; those who prize strictness offer analogies like fine grain and meat versus medicinal stones. Each tries to prevail over the other, arriving at no settled basis. Those who most seek to mediate and blend them say, "Use leniency to treat the good people, and strictness to control the wicked people"—this is for us to anticipate our people with a mind that presumes them wicked. They say, "Pacifying the people should be lenient, while controlling sub-officials should be strict"—this is for us to abandon our sub-officials with a mind that presumes them cunning. They say, "Begin with strictness and end with leniency"—this again is like kudzu cloth in summer and fur robes in winter, which cannot accommodate each other. All of these are reluctant to contradict Master Zuo while taking lightly the task of trusting the words of the sages; I, in my simplicity, dare not take them as a settled basis. I have ventured to discuss this: the successes and failures of official governance, in their broad outlines, do not go beyond the space between laxity and harsh urgency, while their great foundation lies solely in the subtleties of the disposition of the mind. If a person truly possesses a magnanimous and lenient…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
心則與物為體其政也時張而張不咈民
以從欲時弛而弛不違道以干譽所為不
同總之惟民是圖而已雖欲不善不可得
也何者有其心故有其事也夫人誠無寬
大之心則與物為二其政也欲張則張之
以博揮霍之名也欲弛則弛之以博安靜
之名也所為不同總之惟已是圖而已雖
欲善不可得也何者無其心故無其事也
夫君子之持權衡以覈吏治也執本原之
===
說以察之幾微之間而已矣雖然崇寬大
以臻化理有司之事也明道術以端趣舍
朝廷之權也蓋上之意嚮所在而天下不靡
然從者未之有也
第五問
邵夢弼
考試官教授萬批 浙中募兵利病千獨議論
剴切區畫精詳是抱先憂之志者
考試官教授吳批 通達時宜具見經濟
punctuated:
心，則與物為體。其政也，時張而張，不咈民以從欲；時弛而弛，不違道以干譽。所為不同，總之惟民是圖而已，雖欲不善，不可得也。何者？有其心，故有其事也。夫人誠無寬大之心，則與物為二。其政也，欲張則張之，以博揮霍之名也；欲弛則弛之，以博安靜之名也。所為不同，總之惟已是圖而已，雖欲善，不可得也。何者？無其心，故無其事也。夫君子之持權衡以覈吏治也，執本原之說以察之幾微之間而已矣。雖然，崇寬大以臻化理，有司之事也；明道術以端趣舍，朝廷之權也。蓋上之意嚮所在，而天下不靡然從者，未之有也。

第五問
邵夢弼
考試官教授萬批：浙中募兵利病，千獨議論剴切，區畫精詳，是抱先憂之志者。
考試官教授吳批：通達時宜，具見經濟。
translation_en:
…mind, then one forms a single body with all things. In one's governance, when it is time to tighten, one tightens without opposing the people to follow one's own desires; when it is time to relax, one relaxes without violating the Way to seek praise. Though the actions differ, in sum they are planned solely for the people; even if one wished for the governance not to be good, it would be impossible. Why is this? Because having the mind for it, one therefore has the corresponding deeds. If a person truly lacks a magnanimous mind, then one is separated into two from all things. In one's governance, when one wishes to tighten, one tightens in order to win a reputation for brisk decisiveness; when one wishes to relax, one relaxes in order to win a reputation for quietude. Though the actions differ, in sum they are planned solely for oneself [reading 已 as 己]; even if one wished for the governance to be good, it would be impossible. Why is this? Because lacking the mind for it, one therefore lacks the corresponding deeds. Thus, when a gentleman holds the scales to evaluate the governance of officials, he simply grasps the doctrine of fundamental origins to examine things in their subtle incipient moments. Even so, exalting magnanimity to achieve transformative order is the business of the authorities, whereas clarifying the Moral Way and its methods to rectify what is pursued and what is rejected is the prerogative of the Royal Court. Indeed, wherever the inclinations of the sovereign lie, it has never happened that the realm does not bend and follow accordingly.

Fifth Policy Question
Shao Mengbi 邵夢弼
Comment by Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wan 萬: On the advantages and disadvantages of recruiting soldiers in Zhejiang, you alone [?[千]] argue with incisive relevance and plan with precise detail; this is someone who cherishes the resolve to worry before the world worries.
Comment by Examiner and Confucian School Instructor Wu 吳: Thoroughly understanding what is appropriate to the times, fully demonstrating statecraft.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
嘗謂計安天下者莫病乎苟一時之便而
忽長遠之謀亦莫病乎飾虛具之文而忘
責成之實夫事有便於一時而將基乎不
測之憂者君子覩其始必慮其終曾不以
暫焉之可以舒患而行之不顧也何也患
之暫焉者小而終焉者大也事有切於要
務而尚蒙以虛具之文者君子循其名必
責其實曾不以文焉之可以逃責而置之
不問也何也事未有虛而能效實而不效
===
者也執事發策終篇而以調募浙兵為問
蓋地方大計也愚何足以答明問雖然桑
梓之患憂之久矣請以所聞熟數於前而
執事察焉在昔浙中倭夷初發難也當事
者以官兵為不足恃呼市人而集之軍已
又以東南之民柔脆而不可用乃調發狼
土青齊諸省兵數十千騷繹愈甚而效罔
奏卒其所以平難者竟浙兵也豈浙之兵
前後勇怯頓殊耶夫承平日久民方駭覩
punctuated: 嘗謂計安天下者，莫病乎苟一時之便，而忽長遠之謀；亦莫病乎飾虛具之文，而忘責成之實。夫事有便於一時，而將基乎不測之憂者，君子覩其始必慮其終，曾不以暫焉之可以舒患而行之不顧也。何也？患之暫焉者小，而終焉者大也。事有切於要務，而尚蒙以虛具之文者，君子循其名必責其實，曾不以文焉之可以逃責而置之不問也。何也？事未有虛而能效，實而不效者也。執事發策終篇，而以調募浙兵為問，蓋地方大計也，愚何足以答明問？雖然，桑梓之患，憂之久矣，請以所聞熟數於前，而執事察焉。在昔浙中倭夷初發難也，當事者以官兵為不足恃，呼市人而集之軍。已又以東南之民柔脆而不可用，乃調發狼土、青、齊諸省兵數十千，騷繹愈甚，而效罔奏。卒其所以平難者，竟浙兵也。豈浙之兵前後勇怯頓殊耶？夫承平日久，民方駭覩…
translation_en:
I have always maintained that in planning for the security of the realm, there is no greater flaw than settling for momentary convenience while neglecting long-term strategy; nor is there any greater flaw than dressing up empty formalities while forgetting the reality of holding people accountable for results. When a measure is convenient for the moment yet lays the groundwork for unpredictable anxieties in the future, a gentleman who sees its beginning must contemplate its end, never carrying it out recklessly merely because it temporarily relieves distress. Why is this? Because the immediate distress is small, whereas the ultimate calamity is great. When a matter is vital to pressing affairs yet is still cloaked in empty formalities, a gentleman who examines its name must demand its reality, never leaving it unscrutinized merely because the formality allows one to evade responsibility. Why is this? Because no undertaking has ever succeeded through emptiness or failed through substance.

At the close of your policy questions, Your Excellency asks about the transfer and recruitment of Zhejiang troops. This is indeed a matter of grand strategy for the region; how could someone as foolish as I suffice to answer your enlightened inquiry? Even so, I have long worried over the troubles of my native land; allow me to thoroughly recount what I have heard before you, that Your Excellency may examine it.

In the past, when the Japanese raiders first stirred up trouble in Zhejiang, those in charge deemed the regular government troops unreliable, so they called up townspeople and assembled them into an army. Soon after, considering the people of the southeast weak, fragile, and unusable, they transferred and deployed tens of thousands of native Wolf Troops (langbing) and aboriginal troops (tubing), as well as soldiers from the provinces of Shandong (Qing-Qi) and elsewhere. The disturbance along the post roads grew ever worse, yet no results were achieved. In the end, those who finally pacified the crisis were none other than the troops of Zhejiang! Could it be that the soldiers of Zhejiang suddenly changed from cowardly at first to brave later on? Rather, after a long period of peace, the people were at first terrified at the mere sight of…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
戈胄而將吏之駕馭未熟則始之不振非
怯也習見無恐人各利有上功而將吏之
指縱亦便則後之效捷非勇也夫浙不能
籍客兵以禦敵而浙兵又安能爲四方禦
敵哉兵法曰有必勝之將無必勝之兵夫
兵何常之有苟作其勇則淮陰驅市人而
與之戰亦可以成功苟無以作其勇則雖
秦之擊技魏之銳卒不免於敗北以是知
謂浙兵武勇四方皆莫及者非也而今南
===
北征備遂皆曰非浙兵不可其亦未察於
浙之往事矣乎夫南而征者事亟矣不募
恐無速效北而備者勢重矣不調恐有後
虞則其思及浙兵者是卽浙之往日思及
狼土青齊諸省兵之意也夫諸省之兵皆
嘗能爲諸省禦敵矣一不效於浙而置不
復問浙兵素不以武勇名也乃幾倖於禦
浙之敵而遂甲於四方曷故哉執事所謂
頑民狃兵之利而宿將狃浙兵之利者可
punctuated: 戈胄，而將吏之駕馭未熟，則始之不振，非怯也；習見無恐，人各利有上功，而將吏之指縱亦便，則後之效捷，非勇也。夫浙不能籍客兵以禦敵，而浙兵又安能爲四方禦敵哉？《兵法》曰：「有必勝之將，無必勝之兵。」夫兵何常之有？苟作其勇，則淮陰驅市人而與之戰，亦可以成功；苟無以作其勇，則雖秦之擊技、魏之銳卒，不免於敗北。以是知謂浙兵武勇四方皆莫及者，非也。而今南北征備，遂皆曰非浙兵不可，其亦未察於浙之往事矣乎？夫南而征者，事亟矣，不募恐無速效；北而備者，勢重矣，不調恐有後虞。則其思及浙兵者，是卽浙之往日思及狼、土、青、齊諸省兵之意也。夫諸省之兵，皆嘗能爲諸省禦敵矣，一不效於浙，而置不復問；浙兵素不以武勇名也，乃幾倖於禦浙之敵，而遂甲於四方，曷故哉？執事所謂「頑民狃兵之利，而宿將狃浙兵之利」者，可
translation_en: …weapons and armor, and the commanders and officers were not yet practiced in controlling them; thus their initial failure to rally was not out of cowardice. Once they grew accustomed to the sight and had no fear, each man saw advantage in winning top merit, and the commanders and officers also became adept at directing and unleashing them; thus their subsequent swift victories were not out of innate bravery. Now, if Zhejiang could not rely on guest troops from outside to ward off its enemies, how then can Zhejiang troops ward off enemies for all corners of the empire? The Art of War (Bingfa) says: "There are generals who are certain of victory; there are no soldiers who are certain of victory." What constancy is there in soldiers? If one rouses their courage, then even when the Marquis of Huaiyin [Han Xin] drove market-people into battle, he could achieve success; if one has no way to rouse their courage, then even the skilled strikers of Qin and the elite foot soldiers of Wei could not avoid defeat. From this we know that to claim Zhejiang soldiers are so martially brave that none in the four quarters can match them is false. And yet in present campaigns in the south and defense in the north, everyone consequently says that nothing will do except Zhejiang troops—have they not failed to examine Zhejiang's own past experience? Now, for those campaigning in the south, the affair is urgent, and they fear there will be no quick results if they do not recruit them; for those defending in the north, the situation is grave, and they fear future peril if they do not transfer them. Thus, their turning their thoughts to Zhejiang troops is the very same mentality as when Zhejiang in past days turned its thoughts to the wolf-troops [Lang] and native troops [Tu], and the soldiers of Qing, Qi, and other provinces. Those troops from the various provinces had all once been able to ward off enemies for their own provinces, yet once they proved ineffective in Zhejiang, they were cast aside and never asked after again. Zhejiang soldiers were never previously famed for martial bravery, yet having narrowly succeeded in warding off Zhejiang's enemies, they have suddenly been ranked first in all the four quarters—why is this? What Your Excellency refers to as "unruly commoners growing addicted to the profits of soldiering, and veteran generals growing addicted to the advantage of using Zhejiang troops" may…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
為灼見其原巳顧樂於從兵者誠頑民矣
而民不皆頑也愚民之常産無賴而誘惑
者恒多也亦不皆浙之民也四方之亡命
預集而待募者不少也是又不可不察也
樂用浙兵者在宿將矣而宿將非不察事
幾者也一困於土兵之不足而不得不藉
於調則調兵孰有若浙之服習者也再困
於度支之難請而惟調兵為可以破格則
欲厚廩以得士又孰有若調兵之為便者
===
===
也是又不可不原也嘗執是而較浙兵利
害之實亦有可言者矣夫將欲得兵之服
習者以効用而應之者非頑與愚則亡命
也愚者巳不服習而頑與亡命又烏有一
毫忠勇之念也其徼幸於厚利區區月廩
不足以繫其心而平日驕恣之氣將領者
寛之則無制而不可用急之則有怨言且
羣噪而呼矣主客之勢相持彼土之兵因
生嫌忌亦且為之解體而豈邊境之福哉
punctuated: 為灼見其原巳。顧樂於從兵者，誠頑民矣，而民不皆頑也，愚民之常産無賴而誘惑者恒多也；亦不皆浙之民也，四方之亡命預集而待募者不少也，是又不可不察也。樂用浙兵者，在宿將矣，而宿將非不察事幾者也。一困於土兵之不足，而不得不藉於調，則調兵孰有若浙之服習者也；再困於度支之難請，而惟調兵為可以破格，則欲厚廩以得士，又孰有若調兵之為便者也，是又不可不原也。嘗執是而較浙兵利害之實，亦有可言者矣。夫將欲得兵之服習者以効用，而應之者非頑與愚，則亡命也。愚者巳不服習，而頑與亡命，又烏有一毫忠勇之念也？其徼幸於厚利，區區月廩，不足以繫其心，而平日驕恣之氣，將領者寛之則無制而不可用，急之則有怨言，且羣噪而呼矣。主客之勢相持，彼土之兵因生嫌忌，亦且為之解體，而豈邊境之福哉？
translation_en:
…be considered a penetrating insight into its root cause. Yet while those who gladly join the military are indeed unruly commoners, not all of them are unruly—there are always many ignorant commoners without a steady livelihood who have been enticed and misled. Nor are they all commoners of Zhejiang—not a few are fugitives from all quarters who have gathered in advance to await recruitment. This, too, must not go unexamined. Those who gladly employ Zhejiang troops are the veteran commanders, yet these veteran commanders are not blind to the exigencies of affairs. First, they are hampered by the insufficiency of local troops and have no choice but to rely on transferred troops; and among transferred troops, who could be as accustomed to their command and well-trained as those of Zhejiang? Second, they are hampered by the difficulty of requesting funds from the revenue authorities, whereas only by transferring troops can regular limits be set aside; so if they wish to offer generous stipends to win men over, what could be more convenient than transferring troops? This, too, must be understood with sympathy.

If we hold to these points and weigh the actual advantages and disadvantages of Zhejiang troops, there is indeed something to be said. Now, commanders wish to obtain well-trained and accustomed troops for effective service, yet those who answer the call, if not the unruly and the ignorant, are fugitives. The ignorant are already untrained, and as for the unruly and the fugitives, how could they possess the slightest thought of loyalty or bravery? Since they seek windfall profits, a paltry monthly stipend is not enough to bind their hearts. Moreover, given their habitual arrogance and unruliness, if their commanders treat them leniently, they become undisciplined and unusable; if they press them strictly, there are resentful words, and they even raise an uproar and shout in packs. As host and guest troops stand in mutual opposition, the local soldiers there consequently develop resentment and jealousy, and their morale too breaks down—how could this be a blessing for the frontier?

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
且頑者之徼利無巳愚與亡命之從而集
者益衆焉今婺州之墟四方逋逃指爲淵
藪矣比屋皆束裝持挺以俟而農業就蕪
矣征輸多負矣官司亦莫之敢詰矣是使
民無定志而下易倍其上也綿綿不絕蔓
蔓若何萬一有斬干揭木之流出其間迺
駭而圖之豈將有及乎則豈非浙之隱憂
哉而長慮者不得不及之也迺議者有曰
用之可急四方之危不用將貽本土之患
===
此非以天下安危爲計而審於輕重緩急
之勢者亦惡能爲此言也就一時而論之
則危者恃以無恐而可患者亦緣以暫舒
焉將兩利而俱安之矣夫誰曰不便第四
方之所急者急在慣戰向義之士而如前
所謂應募者將焉用之夫浙之兵巳非昔
日禦敵之兵矣而猶望其爲四方禦敵毋
乃信之過與若本土之所爲患者患在民
之好兵不巳而募調不止則患將日深故
punctuated: 且頑者之徼利無巳，愚與亡命之從而集者益衆焉。今婺州之墟，四方逋逃指爲淵藪矣。比屋皆束裝持挺以俟，而農業就蕪矣，征輸多負矣，官司亦莫之敢詰矣。是使民無定志，而下易倍其上也。綿綿不絕，蔓蔓若何？萬一有斬干揭木之流出其間，迺駭而圖之，豈將有及乎？則豈非浙之隱憂哉！而長慮者不得不及之也。迺議者有曰：「用之可急四方之危，不用將貽本土之患。」此非以天下安危爲計，而審於輕重緩急之勢者，亦惡能爲此言也？就一時而論之，則危者恃以無恐，而可患者亦緣以暫舒焉，將兩利而俱安之矣，夫誰曰不便？第四方之所急者，急在慣戰向義之士，而如前所謂應募者，將焉用之？夫浙之兵巳非昔日禦敵之兵矣，而猶望其爲四方禦敵，毋乃信之過與？若本土之所爲患者，患在民之好兵不巳，而募調不止，則患將日深。故…
translation_en: Moreover, as the obstinate endlessly seek profit, the ignorant and the desperadoes who follow and gather grow ever more numerous. Today, the region of Wuzhou 婺州 (Jinhua) is pointed to by fugitives from all directions as a haven. Row upon row of households pack their gear and grasp staves, waiting to be called, while agriculture falls into neglect, tax and labor obligations go largely unpaid, and the authorities dare not even question them. This leaves the people without fixed purpose and makes inferiors easily turn against their superiors. "If when it is a slender thread it is not cut, what will you do when it spreads like creeping vines?" Should there by one chance in ten thousand arise among them men of the sort who cut down poles and raise wooden standards in rebellion, and only then do we take alarm and try to deal with it, will it not be too late? Is this not, then, a hidden danger for Zhejiang? Those who take the long view cannot fail to address it. Yet some who deliberate on the matter say: "Employing them can relieve the crises in the four quarters; not employing them will leave behind trouble in their native place." How could anyone make such a statement unless he were calculating for the security and danger of the whole realm and carefully weighing the relative importance and urgency of the situation? Considered in terms of the immediate moment, those in danger could rely on them to be free of fear, while the source of potential trouble at home would thereby be temporarily relieved; both sides would benefit and both would be kept safe—who would say this is not expedient? Yet what the four quarters urgently need are men seasoned in battle and devoted to righteousness; as for those who answer the recruitment calls as described above, of what use will they be? The soldiers of Zhejiang are already no longer the enemy-resisting soldiers of former days, and yet to still hope that they will resist enemies for the four quarters—is this not trusting them too much? As for what constitutes the trouble in their native place, the trouble lies in the people's unceasing fondness for soldiering; if recruitment and deployment do not stop, the trouble will deepen by the day. Therefore,…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
亟示之以不用正以定民之志而塞患之
源也又何患之能貽毋乃憂之過與得無
幾於利一時之便而忽長遠之謀者與愚
固曰患之暫焉者小而終焉者大君子必
慮之也夫調募之不可不止言官亦屢請
於
朝矣而議猶未决豈以南北之兵未練雖欲
止募而不可得耶夫兵之不可不練也廟
廊之臣非不責望於內封疆之臣非不竭
===
忠於外而竟未有成效者亡其所稱練者
皆虛文耶自非然者三年知方七年即戎
賢聖所作爲可想而胡今歷年之久而無
成也執事所謂各有其說者得非謂北塞
之民凋瘵於虜患即欲補練而苦於無人
南海之民攜貳於賊黨即使訓練而未得
其用與之二者亦當事者聊以應夫責望
者之言而非其實也夫北兵之所以未練
者其病正在於招補要之在營而縻食者
punctuated: 亟示之以不用，正以定民之志而塞患之源也，又何患之能貽？毋乃憂之過與？得無幾於利一時之便而忽長遠之謀者與？愚固曰：患之暫焉者小，而終焉者大，君子必慮之也。夫調募之不可不止，言官亦屢請於朝矣，而議猶未决，豈以南北之兵未練，雖欲止募而不可得耶？夫兵之不可不練也，廟廊之臣非不責望於內，封疆之臣非不竭忠於外，而竟未有成效者，亡其所稱練者皆虛文耶？自非然者，三年知方，七年即戎，賢聖所作爲可想，而胡今歷年之久而無成也？執事所謂各有其說者，得非謂北塞之民凋瘵於虜患，即欲補練而苦於無人；南海之民攜貳於賊黨，即使訓練而未得其用與？之二者，亦當事者聊以應夫責望者之言，而非其實也。夫北兵之所以未練者，其病正在於招補；要之在營而縻食者，
translation_en: …promptly showing them that they will not be employed is precisely how to settle the people's minds and block the source of trouble; what trouble could this possibly leave behind? Is that not worrying excessively? Does it not come close to favoring the convenience of the moment while neglecting long-term plans? I therefore maintain that the immediate trouble is small, whereas the ultimate trouble is great, and the gentleman must give thought to it. As for why the requisitioning and recruiting of troops must be halted, Censorate and Remonstrance Officials have repeatedly petitioned the Court about this, yet the deliberations remain undecided. Could it be because the troops of the North and South have not yet been trained, so that even though one wishes to stop recruiting, it is impossible to do so? That troops must be trained is something that ministers at court do not fail to demand from within, and frontier officials do not fail to devote their utmost loyalty to without; yet in the end there have been no tangible results—could it be that what they call "training" is all empty formality? Were it not so, we can well imagine what the worthies and sages accomplished when after three years the people knew their duty and after seven years they could go to war; why then have so many years now passed without success? When Your Excellency says that "each side has its own explanation," does this not mean that the people of the northern frontier are exhausted by the calamities of the northern raiders, so that even if one wished to replenish and train them, one suffers from a lack of men; and that the people of the southern coast are alienated and colluding with bandit gangs, so that even if they were trained, one could not make use of them? These two explanations are merely words used by those in charge to provisionally answer those who make demands of them, and are not the reality. The reason northern troops remain untrained is that the malady lies precisely in recruitment and replenishment; in short, those currently in the camps consuming rations…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
率皆未練之兵而又奚以補爲也使將領
各肯練其營兵使之一當十十當百卽不
補亦不害其爲練矣顧閱視者孰肯以不
補爲練也將領不得不以虛應之矣南兵
之所以未練者其病正在於懷疑要之左
右而前後者孰非反側之徒而又奚以疑
爲也使將領各肯推其誠心使之中無嫌
外無忌卽蔡人孰非吾人耶顧共事者孰
能諒其未信之跡也將領亦不得不以虛
===
應之矣夫不補而先練推誠而去疑似實
矣而猶有未盡者焉蓋所謂練兵者務在
得其死力得其誠心而一夫充兵卽一家
之心與力皆繫之兵矣練之者非舉其一
家之心與力而盡得之亦何有於兵也顧
今一兵之廩果能足其一身一家之欲否
乎而欲以之易其所謂死與誠也亦難矣
是故練兵難言也非以一兵兼二兵之廩
不能也誰爲繼之非減二兵而養一兵不
punctuated: 率皆未練之兵，而又奚以補爲也？使將領各肯練其營兵，使之一當十、十當百，卽不補，亦不害其爲練矣。顧閱視者孰肯以不補爲練也？將領不得不以虛應之矣。南兵之所以未練者，其病正在於懷疑。要之左右而前後者，孰非反側之徒？而又奚以疑爲也？使將領各肯推其誠心，使之中無嫌、外無忌，卽蔡人孰非吾人耶？顧共事者孰能諒其未信之跡也？將領亦不得不以虛應之矣。夫不補而先練，推誠而去疑，似實矣，而猶有未盡者焉。蓋所謂練兵者，務在得其死力，得其誠心。而一夫充兵，卽一家之心與力皆繫之兵矣。練之者，非舉其一家之心與力而盡得之，亦何有於兵也？顧今一兵之廩，果能足其一身一家之欲否乎？而欲以之易其所謂死與誠也，亦難矣。是故練兵難言也。非以一兵兼二兵之廩不能也，誰爲繼之？非減二兵而養一兵不
translation_en:
… are nearly all untrained soldiers, so what is the point of recruiting replacements? If the commanders were each willing to train the soldiers already in their camps so that one man could match ten and ten could match a hundred, then even without filling the ranks, it would not hinder them from being well-trained. Yet among those who conduct inspections, who is willing to regard not filling the ranks as proper training? Thus, the commanders have no choice but to respond with hollow formalities. As for why the southern troops remain untrained, the malady lies precisely in harboring suspicion. In truth, among those surrounding them on all sides, who is not of a vacillating and rebellious sort? What use is there in harboring suspicion? If the commanders were each willing to extend their sincere trust, so that there is no resentment within and no misgiving without, then even the people of Cai—who among them would not be our own people? Yet among their colleagues in office, who is able to excuse appearances before trust has been established? Thus, these commanders too have no choice but to respond with hollow formalities.

Now, training first without recruiting replacements, and extending sincerity while setting aside suspicion, would seem to be substantial measures; yet they still do not exhaust the matter. For what is called training troops consists above all in winning their willingness to fight to the death and winning their sincere loyalty. When one man serves as a soldier, the hearts and strength of his entire family are bound up with that soldier. If the one who trains them does not win over the hearts and strength of their entire families in full, what can he expect from the soldiers? Yet today, can the rations of a single soldier truly suffice to meet the needs of his own person and his whole family? To wish to exchange such rations for what we call their readiness to die and their sincere loyalty is hard indeed. Therefore, training troops is difficult to speak of. Unless one soldier is given the rations of two, it cannot be done—yet who will sustain the cost? Unless two soldiers are reduced in order to support one, it cannot…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
能也誰為任之但曰募曰調則廩倍於土
著不計也數浮於部牒不問也即寧家之
費道路之擾又幾倍於往昔而亦不較也
然則將領又何必以練兵而自苦哉使達
觀時務者肯以募兵之費充練兵之用而
又破格以閱視之推心以聽信之終之明
賞重罰以激勵而綜覈之如是而不效者
鮮也得無近於責成之實而非虛具之文
者乎愚固曰事未有虛而能效實而不效
===
者君子必責之也夫使練兵果效則募兵
可已而執事又謂兵之入薊入廣者且各
數千即罷將安歸尤至慮也夫蕭俛嘗建
銷兵之策於唐而軍士落籍者眾遂以基
朱克融王廷湊之亂陳升之嘗請減不中
程之兵於宋而羣情洶洶重以貽呂公弼
司馬光之憂則散兵豈非甚艱者哉夫浙
兵固皆農也而一任為兵則耳目心志已
失其故即使厚與行資以恤其歸會不足
punctuated:
能也，誰為任之？但曰募、曰調，則廩倍於土著不計也，數浮於部牒不問也，即寧家之費、道路之擾，又幾倍於往昔，而亦不較也。然則將領又何必以練兵而自苦哉？使達觀時務者肯以募兵之費充練兵之用，而又破格以閱視之，推心以聽信之，終之明賞重罰以激勵而綜覈之，如是而不效者，鮮也。得無近於責成之實，而非虛具之文者乎？愚固曰：事未有虛而能效、實而不效者，君子必責之也。
夫使練兵果效，則募兵可已。而執事又謂兵之入薊、入廣者且各數千，即罷，將安歸？尤至慮也。夫蕭俛嘗建銷兵之策於唐，而軍士落籍者眾，遂以基朱克融、王廷湊之亂；陳升之嘗請減不中程之兵於宋，而羣情洶洶，重以貽呂公弼、司馬光之憂。則散兵豈非甚艱者哉？夫浙兵固皆農也，而一任為兵，則耳目心志已失其故。即使厚與行資以恤其歸，會不足
translation_en:
…[unless one reduces two soldiers to support one, it is] impossible—and who would take responsibility for doing so? Yet as soon as people speak of recruiting (mu) or transferring (diao) troops, no one calculates that their rations are double those of local soldiers; no one questions that their numbers exceed the quotas in the Ministry's dispatches; and even when the expenses for settling their families and the disruptions along the roads are several times greater than in the past, no one bothers to compare them. This being so, why should commanders put themselves through hardship to train local troops? If those who take a farsighted view of current affairs were willing to apply the expenses of recruiting mercenaries toward the costs of training local troops—and furthermore, inspect them beyond conventional rules, place sincere trust in them, and finally rouse and thoroughly evaluate them with clear rewards and heavy punishments—then it would be rare for such efforts not to succeed. Would this not come close to the substance of demanding actual results, rather than the mere empty formality of paper provisions? Thus I say: there has never been an undertaking that achieved results through emptiness or failed to achieve results through substance, and the noble man must demand substance in it.

Now, if the training of local troops truly proves effective, the recruitment of mercenaries can cease. Yet Your Excellency further remarks that the Zhejiang soldiers who have entered Jizhou and Guangdong already number several thousand in each place, and asks where they will go once they are disbanded—a most profound concern indeed. In the Tang dynasty, Xiao Mian 蕭俛 once proposed a policy of reducing the army, and because so many soldiers were struck from the registers, it laid the foundation for the rebellions of Zhu Kerong 朱克融 and Wang Tingcou 王廷湊. In the Song dynasty, Chen Shengzhi 陳升之 once requested the reduction of soldiers who failed to meet standards, throwing public sentiment into an uproar and leaving grave anxieties for Lü Gongbi 呂公弼 and Sima Guang 司馬光. Is not the disbanding of troops, then, an exceedingly difficult matter? The soldiers of Zhejiang were originally all farmers, yet once they have served as soldiers, their eyes, ears, and minds have already lost their former ways. Even if they were given generous travel funds to compassionate them on their return home, it would not be enough…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
以當彼之一瞵而統押冗員實利之矣即
欲整其隊伍以防之逸曾何有于機會之
可制而奔竄流劫且任之矣至謂有司之
交割與夫里保之收籍則去歲薊鎮之更
番與夫閩中之罷遣者按牒亦不下數千
而交割收籍者能幾人也罷兵無歸資身
無策有不爲四方患者耶故愚以爲今且
未必議罷也而急在止募止募之令必明
必信使四方咸知浙兵之不復募而彼亦
===
無復再募之望是爲正其本也本之旣正
而又申告有司爲之寬其文法緩其逋負
清其田里量減其差徭使居者有爲農之
樂而出者有故土之思是爲招其來也由
是有謳吟而懷歸者聽之不必按籍而勾
也有缺伍而願補者從之不必連保而收
也有强横倍支月餼者徐察而遞減之無
取快於一時也有羸弱不任弓矢者日省
而漸汰之無取必於盡斥也以此而罷庶
punctuated: 以當彼之一瞵，而統押冗員實利之矣；即欲整其隊伍以防之逸，曾何有于機會之可制，而奔竄流劫且任之矣。至謂有司之交割，與夫里保之收籍，則去歲薊鎮之更番，與夫閩中之罷遣者，按牒亦不下數千，而交割收籍者能幾人也？罷兵無歸，資身無策，有不爲四方患者耶？故愚以爲今且未必議罷也，而急在止募。止募之令必明必信，使四方咸知浙兵之不復募，而彼亦無復再募之望，是爲正其本也。本之旣正，而又申告有司，爲之寬其文法，緩其逋負，清其田里，量減其差徭，使居者有爲農之樂，而出者有故土之思，是爲招其來也。由是有謳吟而懷歸者聽之，不必按籍而勾也；有缺伍而願補者從之，不必連保而收也；有强横倍支月餼者徐察而遞減之，無取快於一時也；有羸弱不任弓矢者日省而漸汰之，無取必於盡斥也。以此而罷，庶…
translation_en:
…to catch a single glance of theirs, while the superfluous officials escorting them are the ones who truly profit from it. Even if one wished to keep their ranks in order to prevent them from deserting, what opportunity is there really to keep them under control? Instead, they will simply be left to flee, scatter, and roam about plundering. As for talking of handing them over to the local authorities and having the village and baojia heads re-register them on the household rolls—last year, when troops were rotated out of Jizhen or dismissed from Fujian, according to the official registers they numbered no fewer than several thousand; yet how many of them were actually handed over and re-registered? When dismissed soldiers have nowhere to return to and no means to support themselves, how could they not become a scourge in every direction?

Therefore, in my humble opinion, for the present we need not even deliberate on dismissing them; the urgent priority lies in halting recruitment. The order to halt recruitment must be made clear and trustworthy, so that all quarters know that Zhejiang troops will no longer be recruited, and those men themselves have no further hope of being recruited again. This is what is meant by rectifying the root. Once the root is rectified, we should further instruct the local authorities to relax the strictness of the laws for them, defer their tax arrears, clear up their land and village claims, and proportionately reduce their corvée labor and service levies, so that those who remain at home take joy in farming and those who have gone away long for their native soil. This is what is meant by beckoning them to return.

Thereafter, if there are those who sing nostalgically and yearn to return home, let them do so, without insisting on checking the registers to conscript replacements; if there are vacancies in the ranks and men willing to fill them, allow them to do so, without requiring mutual-guarantor bonds to take them in; if there are overbearing soldiers drawing double monthly rations, investigate them unhurriedly and reduce their pay step by step, without seeking the satisfaction of doing it all at once; and if there are frail and weak men unequal to bow and arrow, inspect them daily and weed them out gradually, without insisting on expelling them all immediately. If they are demobilized in this way, perhaps…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
乎可散而亦可歸矣然天下之事言之於
無事之日常若迂緩不切而言之於患至
之日則事已無及募兵之爲漸患也似亦
不可謂之緩而不切矣則夫亟練兵而核
責成之實亟止募以圖長遠之謀者豈非
計安天下之大者歟抑愚又有言天下之
務莫大於紀綱而紀綱非上下以誠相應
莫與立也今
朝廷之上出一
===
令以示天下而百司庶政莫敢不懾服奔走不
可謂紀綱不立矣但恐以文墨相應而少
忠誠浹洽之實意則所謂紀綱悉虛也而
何有於練兵一事哉是又草茅之士私憂
過計之一念也不識執事以爲何如
punctuated: 乎可散而亦可歸矣。然天下之事，言之於無事之日，常若迂緩不切；而言之於患至之日，則事已無及。募兵之爲漸患也，似亦不可謂之緩而不切矣。則夫亟練兵而核責成之實，亟止募以圖長遠之謀者，豈非計安天下之大者歟？抑愚又有言：天下之務莫大於紀綱，而紀綱非上下以誠相應，莫與立也。今朝廷之上，出一令以示天下，而百司庶政莫敢不懾服奔走，不可謂紀綱不立矣。但恐以文墨相應，而少忠誠浹洽之實意，則所謂紀綱悉虛也，而何有於練兵一事哉？是又草茅之士，私憂過計之一念也。不識執事以爲何如？
translation_en:
… perhaps they can be dispersed and also returned to their homes. Yet in the affairs of the realm, when one speaks of them in days of peace, it always seems roundabout, unhurried, and lacking urgency; whereas when one speaks of them on the day disaster arrives, it is already too late to act. That recruited mercenaries are becoming a growing menace can hardly be called unhurried or lacking in urgency. Then surely, urgently training the regular troops and verifying the actual results of holding officials accountable, while urgently halting the recruitment of mercenaries in order to plan for the long term—is this not a paramount strategy for securing the peace of the realm?

Moreover, this humble candidate has a further word to offer: among the affairs of the realm, nothing is greater than discipline and order, and unless superiors and subordinates respond to one another with sincerity, there is no way for discipline and order to be established. Today, when the court above issues a single command to instruct the realm, across all the offices and myriad administrations none dare not submit in awe and hasten to obey; one cannot say that discipline and order have not been established. Yet I fear that if they respond merely with paperwork and lack the genuine intent of loyal sincerity and harmonious cooperation, then what is called discipline and order is entirely hollow—and what then will come of this single matter of training troops? This, again, is a thought born of the private worries and excessive calculations of a rustic scholar. I do not know what Your Excellency thinks of it.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
浙江鄕試錄後序
萬曆癸酉浙江鄕試錄成濟
川以職事序諸末簡庸申一
言以告多士曰記有之官先
事士先志夫士也何以志哉
玆歌鹿鳴而升也行且升之
天府服乃官政夫士也何以事
===
哉濟川聞之古之人以天地
萬物爲一體視宇宙內事莫
非分內故方其畎畝之中樂
堯舜之道而所志無非事者
比其出也則曰予弗克俾厥
后爲堯舜其心愧恥若撻於
市思天下之民匹夫匹婦有
punctuated:
浙江鄕試錄後序
萬曆癸酉《浙江鄕試錄》成，濟川以職事序諸末簡，庸申一言以告多士曰：《記》有之：「官先事，士先志。」夫士也，何以志哉？玆歌《鹿鳴》而升也，行且升之天府，服乃官政。夫士也，何以事哉？濟川聞之，古之人以天地萬物爲一體，視宇宙內事莫非分內。故方其畎畝之中，樂堯、舜之道，而所志無非事者；比其出也，則曰：「予弗克俾厥后爲堯、舜，其心愧恥，若撻於市。」思天下之民，匹夫匹婦有
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination

Now that the Record of the Zhejiang Provincial Examination of the guiyou year of the Wanli era (1573) has been completed, by virtue of my official duties I, Jichuan, write a postface for its final pages, and take this occasion to offer a word of advice to the many scholars, saying:

It is said in the Record of Rites (Liji): "Officials put service first; scholars put aspiration first." As for scholars, how should they set their aspirations? Now, having been advanced amid the singing of the "Lu ming" ("Cry of the Deer") ode, they are about to be presented to the celestial court and take up the duties of official governance. As for scholars, how then should they approach service?

I, Jichuan, have heard that the ancients regarded Heaven, Earth, and the myriad things as one body, and viewed nothing within the universe as falling outside their own responsibility. Therefore, while they were still amid the furrowed fields, they delighted in the Way of Yao and Shun, and what they aspired to was nothing other than public service. When the time came for them to go forth into office, they said: "If I cannot make my sovereign like Yao and Shun, my heart feels ashamed and disgraced, as though I had been beaten in the marketplace." If they thought that among the people of the realm there was a single common man or woman who…

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
不被堯舜之澤若已推而內
之溝中蓋其事也猶之乎其
志也用能成其保衡之業咨
爾諸士糊名而求之其素所
爲志我弗敢知然縱觀其言
類皆發其性靈澤之於道德
仁義語及委質則奮然欲以
身爲社稷水聲利之交而後
民情則毅然若將試□諸士
而藹藹乎民胞物與之□□
即以質之保衡又□□
其爲志也亦嘗有一
乎誠有其志也將有其事也
苟其無之則圖之始自今也
punctuated: 不被堯舜之澤，若已推而內之溝中。蓋其事也，猶之乎其志也，用能成其保衡之業。咨爾諸士，糊名而求之，其素所爲志，我弗敢知。然縱觀其言，類皆發其性靈，澤之於道德仁義；語及委質，則奮然欲以身爲社稷；水聲利之交，而後民情，則毅然若將試□諸士，而藹藹乎民胞物與之□□，即以質之保衡，又□□。其爲志也，亦嘗有一乎？誠有其志也，將有其事也；苟其無之，則圖之始自今也。
translation_en:
… did not receive the beneficence of Yao and Shun, it was as if he himself had pushed them into a ditch. Indeed, his deeds were just like his aspirations, and thereby he was able to accomplish his enterprise as Protector and Arbiter (Baoheng 保衡).

Ah, all you scholars! In seeking you out through sealed-name papers, I do not presume to know what your habitual aspirations have been. Yet looking broadly over your words, they generally express your innate spirit and are enriched by the Way, virtue, humaneness, and righteousness. When speaking of pledging allegiance to enter service, you are roused with the desire to devote yourselves to the altars of soil and grain; as for the confluence of reputation and profit [?], putting the people's conditions afterward [?], you are resolute as if about to test [?] you scholars, and harmonious with the [spirit of?] viewing the people as one's siblings and all things as one's companions, so that even if measured against the Protector and Arbiter, how could [?]!

As for such aspirations, have you indeed ever held them as one [with your deeds?]? If you truly possess the aspiration, you will have the deeds; if you do not possess it, then plan for it beginning from today.

title: 萬曆元年浙江鄉試錄
text:
蓋人有欲適千里者飾□
具齎斧戒僕御引其轅□□
鄉之曰吾將適□
走燕之道也□
首之無何
今者何以
周身自
===
之思澹
能成其美
念哉鹿鳴
示我周行我□
說勗焉
福建邵武府儒學教
川謹序
punctuated:

translation_en:
For when someone wishes to travel a thousand li, he outfits his [carriage?], prepares his travel funds and provisions, instructs his servants and driver, and turns his carriage shafts [to face?] toward it, saying, "I am going to travel to […]." [If it is] the road that runs to Yan, [and he turns the carriage's?] head toward it, before long [he will arrive; how does this differ from] today? How could one, with thoughts of self-protection and self-[interest?] grown faint [?], be able to bring his good qualities to completion? Be mindful of this! The ode "Deer Cry" (Luming) says, "Show me the grand highway"; I [therefore offer this?] explanation to encourage them.
Respectfullywritten as a postface by […]chuan, Instructor (jiaoshou) of the Confucian School of Shaowu Prefecture, Fujian.
